nodes.summary: Efron (1979) estimated the uncertainty of almost any statistic by resampling the data with replacement, replacing formulas with computation.

nodes.title: Lovász Theta Function
nodes.html: Lovász (1979) defined a number, computable by semidefinite programming, that bounds the Shannon capacity of a graph, and used it to prove that the capacity of the 5-cycle is √5. It was an early semidefinite relaxation and is central to combinatorial optimization.
nodes.summary: Lovász (1979) defined a number, computable by semidefinite programming, that bounds the Shannon capacity of a graph, and used it to prove that the capacity of the 5-cycle is √5.

nodes.title: Positive Mass Theorem
nodes.html: The total mass of an isolated gravitating system with non-negative local energy density is non-negative (Schoen and Yau, 1979; Witten gave a spinor proof in 1981). It is a cornerstone of mathematical general relativity and was used to resolve the Yamabe problem.
nodes.summary: The total mass of an isolated gravitating system with non-negative local energy density is non-negative (Schoen and Yau, 1979; Witten gave a spinor proof in 1981).

nodes.title: Amenability of Thompson’s Group F

progress.what: F contains no free subgroup of rank 2.
progress.html: F contains no free subgroup of rank 2.

progress.what: Published a claimed proof that F is amenable; an error was later found.
progress.html: Published a claimed proof that F is amenable; an error was later found.

progress.what: Claimed proof that F is nonamenable (family 248 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.
progress.html: Claimed proof that F is nonamenable (family 248 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.

nodes.html: Is Thompson’s group F, the group of piecewise-linear homeomorphisms of the unit interval with dyadic breakpoints and slopes that are powers of 2, amenable? Geoghegan popularized the question in 1979, and F has no free subgroups (Brin and Squier, 1985), the usual obstruction to amenability. Earlier claimed proofs have failed; OpenAI’s October 2026 claim of nonamenability, formalized in Lean, awaits review.
nodes.summary: Is Thompson’s group F, the group of piecewise-linear homeomorphisms of the unit interval with dyadic breakpoints and slopes that are powers of 2, amenable?

nodes.title: Union-Closed Sets Conjecture

progress.what: The first constant fraction (1%), using entropy. Within weeks others had pushed it to about 38%.
progress.html: The first constant fraction (1%), using entropy. Within weeks others had pushed it to about 38%.

nodes.html: In any finite family of sets closed under unions, other than the family containing only the empty set, some element belongs to at least half of the sets.
nodes.summary: In any finite family of sets closed under unions, other than the family containing only the empty set, some element belongs to at least half of the sets.

nodes.title: Mandelbrot Set
nodes.html: The set of complex numbers c for which iterating z → z² + c stays bounded. Mandelbrot’s computer pictures (1980) made it famous, and Douady and Hubbard (1982 to 1985) proved it is connected and studied its structure. Its boundary is a standard example of a fractal.
nodes.summary: The set of complex numbers c for which iterating z → z² + c stays bounded.

nodes.title: No Percolation at Criticality

progress.what: Proved that the critical point of bond percolation on the square lattice is 1/2, where Theodore Harris had shown in 1960 that there is no infinite cluster. This settled two dimensions.
progress.html: Proved that the critical point of bond percolation on the square lattice is 1/2, where Theodore Harris had shown in 1960 that there is no infinite cluster. This settled two dimensions.

progress.what: Proved it in high dimensions with the lace expansion (d ≥ 19, later d ≥ 11).
progress.html: Proved it in high dimensions with the lace expansion (d ≥ 19, later d ≥ 11).

progress.what: Claimed proof that critical bond and site percolation on ℤ³ have no infinite cluster, and that critical bond percolation has none on any quasi-transitive graph with p_c < 1, the Benjamini–Schramm conjecture (family 213 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.
progress.html: Claimed proof that critical bond and site percolation on ℤ³ have no infinite cluster, and that critical bond percolation has none on any quasi-transitive graph with p_c < 1, the Benjamini–Schramm conjecture (family 213 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.

nodes.html: Critical percolation should have no infinite cluster in any dimension d ≥ 2. Harry Kesten listed d ≥ 3 as open in 1982; it was known in the plane (Harris, 1960; Kesten, 1980) and in high dimensions (Hara and Slade, 1990), with three dimensions the key case. OpenAI’s October 2026 release claims ℤ³ and, for bond percolation, all quasi-transitive graphs, formalized in Lean but not yet independently reviewed.
nodes.summary: Critical percolation should have no infinite cluster in any dimension d ≥ 2.

nodes.title: Topological 4D Poincaré Conjecture
nodes.html: Freedman classified simply connected closed topological 4-manifolds and proved the Poincaré conjecture for them (1982). The smooth 4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture remains open.
nodes.summary: Freedman classified simply connected closed topological 4-manifolds and proved the Poincaré conjecture for them (1982).

nodes.title: Thurston’s Geometrization
nodes.html: Thurston proved that Haken 3-manifolds have geometric decompositions (1982) and conjectured that every closed 3-manifold can be cut into pieces with one of eight model geometries. Perelman proved the conjecture in 2003, which also settled the Poincaré conjecture.
nodes.summary: Thurston proved that Haken 3-manifolds have geometric decompositions (1982) and conjectured that every closed 3-manifold can be cut into pieces with one of eight model geometries.

nodes.title: Yau’s Nodal Set Conjecture

progress.what: Proved both bounds for real-analytic metrics.
progress.html: Proved both bounds for real-analytic metrics.

progress.what: Proved the lower bound for all smooth metrics and a polynomial upper bound.
progress.html: Proved the lower bound for all smooth metrics and a polynomial upper bound.

progress.what: Claimed proof of the sharp upper bound C√λ on every smooth closed surface, completing the conjecture there, and smooth counterexamples to the upper bound in dimensions 3, 4 and 5 (family 350 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.
progress.html: Claimed proof of the sharp upper bound C√λ on every smooth closed surface, completing the conjecture there, and smooth counterexamples to the upper bound in dimensions 3, 4 and 5 (family 350 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.

nodes.html: Shing-Tung Yau conjectured in 1982 that the zero set of a Laplace eigenfunction with eigenvalue λ has size between c√λ and C√λ. Donnelly and Fefferman proved it for real-analytic metrics in 1988 and Logunov proved the lower bound in 2018. OpenAI’s October 2026 release claims the upper bound on surfaces and counterexamples in dimensions 3 to 5, formalized in Lean but not yet independently reviewed.
nodes.summary: Shing-Tung Yau conjectured in 1982 that the zero set of a Laplace eigenfunction with eigenvalue λ has size between c√λ and C√λ.

nodes.title: Donaldson’s Theorem
nodes.html: Using moduli spaces of Yang–Mills instantons, Donaldson showed in 1983 that a closed smooth simply connected 4-manifold with definite intersection form must have the diagonal form, so many topological 4-manifolds admit no smooth structure. With Freedman’s work this gave exotic ℝ⁴.
nodes.summary: Using moduli spaces of Yang–Mills instantons, Donaldson showed in 1983 that a closed smooth simply connected 4-manifold with definite intersection form must have the diagonal form, so many topological 4-manifolds admit no smooth structure.

nodes.title: Faltings’s Theorem
nodes.html: A curve of genus at least 2 over a number field has only finitely many rational points (Faltings, 1983), proving Mordell’s conjecture of 1922. It implies, for example, that for each n ≥ 4 the Fermat equation has at most finitely many coprime integer solutions.
nodes.summary: A curve of genus at least 2 over a number field has only finitely many rational points (Faltings, 1983), proving Mordell’s conjecture of 1922.

nodes.title: Interior-Point Methods
nodes.html: Karmarkar (1984) gave a polynomial-time algorithm for linear programming that is also fast in practice, moving through the interior of the feasible region; Khachiyan’s ellipsoid method (1979) had first shown polynomial time. Nesterov and Nemirovski (1994) extended the approach to convex optimization.
nodes.summary: Karmarkar (1984) gave a polynomial-time algorithm for linear programming that is also fast in practice, moving through the interior of the feasible region; Khachiyan’s ellipsoid method (1979) had first shown polynomial time.

nodes.title: Jones Polynomial
nodes.html: A new knot invariant found in the theory of von Neumann algebras (Jones, 1984). Witten explained it through Chern–Simons quantum field theory (1989), and it opened the field of quantum topology. Jones received the Fields Medal in 1990.
nodes.summary: A new knot invariant found in the theory of von Neumann algebras (Jones, 1984).

nodes.title: abc Conjecture

progress.what: The best unconditional bound: c < exp(K r^(1/3) (log r)³), where r = rad(abc).
progress.html: The best unconditional bound: c < exp(K r^(1/3) (log r)³), where r = rad(abc).

progress.what: Announced a proof through inter-universal Teichmüller theory, published in 2021; most experts do not accept it.
progress.html: Announced a proof through inter-universal Teichmüller theory, published in 2021; most experts do not accept it.

progress.what: Reported a gap in the central argument of Mochizuki’s proof that they consider too severe to repair by small modifications.
progress.html: Reported a gap in the central argument of Mochizuki’s proof that they consider too severe to repair by small modifications.

progress.what: Proposed a different proof through arithmetic Teichmüller spaces; it has not gained acceptance either.
progress.html: Proposed a different proof through arithmetic Teichmüller spaces; it has not gained acceptance either.

nodes.html: For coprime positive integers with a + b = c, the conjecture (Oesterlé and Masser, 1985) says that for every ε > 0 only finitely many triples have c > rad(abc)^(1+ε), where rad(abc) is the product of the distinct primes dividing abc. It implies many other Diophantine results, such as Roth’s theorem and Faltings’s theorem. Mochizuki’s claimed proof (2012) is not accepted by most experts.
nodes.summary: For coprime positive integers with a + b = c, the conjecture (Oesterlé and Masser, 1985) says that for every ε > 0 only finitely many triples have c > rad(abc)^(1+ε), where rad(abc) is the product of the distinct primes dividing abc.

nodes.title: Bieberbach Conjecture
nodes.html: For a one-to-one analytic function f on the unit disk with f(0) = 0 and f′(0) = 1, the n-th Taylor coefficient satisfies |aₙ| ≤ n. Bieberbach conjectured it in 1916, and de Branges proved it in 1984 to 1985 (Acta Mathematica 1985) with inequalities for special functions.
nodes.summary: For a one-to-one analytic function f on the unit disk with f(0) = 0 and f′(0) = 1, the n-th Taylor coefficient satisfies |aₙ| ≤ n.

nodes.title: Falconer Distance Conjecture

progress.what: Sets of Hausdorff dimension above (d + 1)/2 have distance sets of positive measure.
progress.html: Sets of Hausdorff dimension above (d + 1)/2 have distance sets of positive measure.

progress.what: In the plane, lowered the dimension threshold to 5/4.
progress.html: In the plane, lowered the dimension threshold to 5/4.

progress.what: Claimed proof in every dimension d ≥ 2: compact sets of Hausdorff dimension above d/2 have distance sets of positive Lebesgue measure (family 073 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.
progress.html: Claimed proof in every dimension d ≥ 2: compact sets of Hausdorff dimension above d/2 have distance sets of positive Lebesgue measure (family 073 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.

nodes.html: Falconer’s conjecture says that a compact set in d-dimensional space with Hausdorff dimension above d/2 has a set of pairwise distances of positive length. It grew out of Kenneth Falconer’s 1985 work and is a continuous analogue of Erdős’s distinct distances problem. OpenAI’s October 2026 release claims a proof in every dimension, formalized in Lean but not yet independently reviewed.
nodes.summary: Falconer’s conjecture says that a compact set in d-dimensional space with Hausdorff dimension above d/2 has a set of pairwise distances of positive length.

nodes.title: MLC Conjecture

progress.what: Local connectivity at every parameter that is not infinitely renormalizable.
progress.html: Local connectivity at every parameter that is not infinitely renormalizable.

progress.what: Local connectivity at many infinitely renormalizable parameters, through a priori bounds and rigidity.
progress.html: Local connectivity at many infinitely renormalizable parameters, through a priori bounds and rigidity.

progress.what: The first infinitely renormalizable parameters of satellite type, using pacman renormalization.
progress.html: The first infinitely renormalizable parameters of satellite type, using pacman renormalization.

nodes.html: Is the Mandelbrot set locally connected? Douady and Hubbard showed in the 1980s that a yes would give a complete combinatorial model of the set and would imply that hyperbolic maps are dense in the quadratic family. Yoccoz proved local connectivity at every parameter that is not infinitely renormalizable; the infinitely renormalizable parameters are the remaining obstacle.
nodes.summary: Is the Mandelbrot set locally connected?

nodes.title: Sidorenko’s Conjecture

progress.what: Proved the conjecture for trees, even cycles and complete bipartite graphs.
progress.html: Proved the conjecture for trees, even cycles and complete bipartite graphs.

progress.what: Proved it for bipartite graphs with a vertex joined to every vertex on the other side.
progress.html: Proved it for bipartite graphs with a vertex joined to every vertex on the other side.

progress.what: Claimed counterexample: a connected bipartite graph with 35 vertices and 66 edges that occurs less often than in a random graph of the same edge density. The same graph would disprove the Skokan–Thoma forcing conjecture (family 161 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.
progress.html: Claimed counterexample: a connected bipartite graph with 35 vertices and 66 edges that occurs less often than in a random graph of the same edge density. The same graph would disprove the Skokan–Thoma forcing conjecture (family 161 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.

nodes.html: Alexander Sidorenko conjectured in 1986 that for every bipartite graph H, random graphs contain the fewest copies of H among all graphs of the same edge density. A major problem of extremal graph theory, it was proved for trees, even cycles, hypercubes and other families. OpenAI’s October 2026 release claims a counterexample with 35 vertices and 66 edges, formalized in Lean but not yet independently reviewed.
nodes.summary: Alexander Sidorenko conjectured in 1986 that for every bipartite graph H, random graphs contain the fewest copies of H among all graphs of the same edge density.

nodes.title: Residual Finiteness of Hyperbolic Groups

progress.what: Every hyperbolic group is residually finite if and only if every hyperbolic group has a proper finite-index subgroup.
progress.html: Every hyperbolic group is residually finite if and only if every hyperbolic group has a proper finite-index subgroup.

progress.what: Hyperbolic groups acting geometrically on CAT(0) cube complexes are virtually special, hence residually finite, completing Daniel Wise’s program.
progress.html: Hyperbolic groups acting geometrically on CAT(0) cube complexes are virtually special, hence residually finite, completing Daniel Wise’s program.

progress.what: Claimed construction of a torsion-free hyperbolic group that is not residually finite and not linear over any field (family 252 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.
progress.html: Claimed construction of a torsion-free hyperbolic group that is not residually finite and not linear over any field (family 252 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.

nodes.html: Hyperbolic groups, introduced by Mikhail Gromov in 1987, include the fundamental groups of negatively curved manifolds. Whether all are residually finite, so that elements can be told apart in finite quotients, was a central open question, answered yes for cubulated groups by Ian Agol (2013). OpenAI’s October 2026 release claims a torsion-free counterexample, formalized in Lean but not yet independently reviewed.
nodes.summary: Hyperbolic groups, introduced by Mikhail Gromov in 1987, include the fundamental groups of negatively curved manifolds.

nodes.title: Periodic Tiling Conjecture in 3D

progress.what: Proved the conjecture for the integer lattice ℤ².
progress.html: Proved the conjecture for the integer lattice ℤ².

progress.what: Disproved it in a sufficiently high dimension.
progress.html: Disproved it in a sufficiently high dimension.

progress.what: Claimed construction of a finite tile in ℤ³, and its unit-cube thickening in ℝ³, that tiles space by translations but admits no periodic tiling (family 155 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.
progress.html: Claimed construction of a finite tile in ℤ³, and its unit-cube thickening in ℝ³, that tiles space by translations but admits no periodic tiling (family 155 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.

nodes.html: The periodic tiling conjecture of Grünbaum and Shephard (1987) and Lagarias and Wang (1996) says a shape tiling space by translations can also tile it periodically. It holds for ℤ², and Greenfeld and Tao disproved it in 2022 in a high dimension, leaving three as the smallest open dimension. OpenAI’s October 2026 release claims a counterexample in ℤ³ and ℝ³, formalized in Lean but not yet independently reviewed.
nodes.summary: The periodic tiling conjecture of Grünbaum and Shephard (1987) and Lagarias and Wang (1996) says a shape tiling space by translations can also tile it periodically.

nodes.title: Calculus of Constructions
nodes.html: A dependent type theory strong enough to express most of mathematics (Coquand and Huet, 1988). Extended with inductive types it became the logic of the Coq proof assistant, and a close relative underlies Lean.
nodes.summary: A dependent type theory strong enough to express most of mathematics (Coquand and Huet, 1988).

nodes.title: Wavelets
nodes.html: Wavelets are localized oscillating functions that analyze signals at many scales. Morlet and Grossmann introduced them in the early 1980s, Meyer and Mallat (multiresolution analysis, 1989) built the theory, and Daubechies’s compactly supported wavelets (1988) made them practical. They power JPEG 2000 and many signal-processing methods.
nodes.summary: Wavelets are localized oscillating functions that analyze signals at many scales.

nodes.title: Mumford–Shah Conjecture

progress.what: Proved that minimizers exist.
progress.html: Proved that minimizers exist.

progress.what: Proved the conjecture for minimizers whose edge set has finitely many connected components.
progress.html: Proved the conjecture for minimizers whose edge set has finitely many connected components.

progress.what: Claimed proof of the interior regularity statement in the plane: near each point the edge set is a C^{1,α} arc, a crack tip or three arcs meeting at 120° (family 366 of OpenAI’s math release, not formalized). Not yet independently reviewed.
progress.html: Claimed proof of the interior regularity statement in the plane: near each point the edge set is a C^{1,α} arc, a crack tip or three arcs meeting at 120° (family 366 of OpenAI’s math release, not formalized). Not yet independently reviewed.

nodes.html: David Mumford and Jayant Shah conjectured in 1989 that for a minimizer of their image-segmentation functional in the plane, the edge set is a finite union of smooth arcs meeting only in 120° triple junctions or ending at crack tips. It is the model problem for free-discontinuity regularity. OpenAI’s October 2026 release claims the interior statement; it is not formalized and not yet independently reviewed.
nodes.summary: David Mumford and Jayant Shah conjectured in 1989 that for a minimizer of their image-segmentation functional in the plane, the edge set is a finite union of smooth arcs meeting only in 120° triple junctions or ending at crack tips.

nodes.title: No Projective Plane of Order 10
nodes.html: An enormous computer search showed that no finite projective plane of order 10 exists (Lam, Thiel and Swiercz, 1989). Order 10 was the smallest order that is not a prime power and is not excluded by the Bruck–Ryser theorem.
nodes.summary: An enormous computer search showed that no finite projective plane of order 10 exists (Lam, Thiel and Swiercz, 1989).

nodes.title: Seymour’s Second Neighbourhood Conjecture

progress.what: Proved the case of tournaments, conjectured by Nathaniel Dean.
progress.html: Proved the case of tournaments, conjectured by Nathaniel Dean.

progress.what: Every oriented graph has a vertex whose second neighbourhood is at least about 0.657 times as large as its first.
progress.html: Every oriented graph has a vertex whose second neighbourhood is at least about 0.657 times as large as its first.

progress.what: Claimed proof for every finite oriented graph (family 173 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.
progress.html: Claimed proof for every finite oriented graph (family 173 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.

nodes.html: Paul Seymour conjectured in 1990 that every finite oriented graph has a vertex with at least as many vertices at distance two as at distance one. In a social network, someone would have at least as many friends of friends as friends; tournaments were settled in 1996. OpenAI’s October 2026 release claims a full proof, formalized in Lean but not yet independently reviewed.
nodes.summary: Paul Seymour conjectured in 1990 that every finite oriented graph has a vertex with at least as many vertices at distance two as at distance one.

nodes.title: Cannon’s Conjecture

progress.what: Showed the conjecture follows if natural tilings of the sphere at infinity behave conformally.
progress.html: Showed the conjecture follows if natural tilings of the sphere at infinity behave conformally.

progress.what: Proved it when the Ahlfors-regular conformal dimension of the boundary is attained.
progress.html: Proved it when the Ahlfors-regular conformal dimension of the boundary is attained.

progress.what: Claimed proof that every hyperbolic group with 2-sphere boundary acts properly and cocompactly by isometries on hyperbolic 3-space (family 246 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.
progress.html: Claimed proof that every hyperbolic group with 2-sphere boundary acts properly and cocompactly by isometries on hyperbolic 3-space (family 246 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.

nodes.html: James Cannon conjectured in the early 1990s that every hyperbolic group whose boundary at infinity is a 2-sphere acts geometrically on hyperbolic 3-space. A proof would make each such torsion-free group the fundamental group of a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold, a central goal of geometric group theory. OpenAI’s October 2026 release claims a proof, formalized in Lean but not yet independently reviewed.
nodes.summary: James Cannon conjectured in the early 1990s that every hyperbolic group whose boundary at infinity is a 2-sphere acts geometrically on hyperbolic 3-space.

nodes.title: Monstrous Moonshine
nodes.html: McKay noticed in 1978 that 196884 = 196883 + 1, linking a coefficient of the j-function to the smallest representation of the Monster group. Conway and Norton (1979) conjectured a systematic connection, and Borcherds proved it in 1992 using vertex algebras, work for which he received the Fields Medal in 1998.
nodes.summary: McKay noticed in 1978 that 196884 = 196883 + 1, linking a coefficient of the j-function to the smallest representation of the Monster group.

nodes.title: Borsuk’s Conjecture Disproved
aliases: partition into pieces of smaller diameter
nodes.html: Borsuk conjectured in 1933 that every bounded set in n-dimensional space can be split into n + 1 pieces of smaller diameter. Kahn and Kalai (1993) showed that this fails in high dimensions, and Bondarenko (2013) showed that it fails for every n ≥ 65.
nodes.summary: Borsuk conjectured in 1933 that every bounded set in n-dimensional space can be split into n + 1 pieces of smaller diameter.

nodes.title: Semidefinite Programming
nodes.html: Optimization over positive semidefinite matrices, solvable efficiently by interior-point methods (Nesterov and Nemirovski, 1994; Alizadeh, 1995). Goemans and Williamson’s MAX-CUT algorithm (1995) made it central to approximation algorithms.
nodes.summary: Optimization over positive semidefinite matrices, solvable efficiently by interior-point methods (Nesterov and Nemirovski, 1994; Alizadeh, 1995).

nodes.title: Concentration of Measure
nodes.html: Functions of many independent variables are nearly constant. Milman used the phenomenon in 1971 to prove Dvoretzky’s theorem, and Talagrand’s isoperimetric inequalities in product spaces (1995) made it a general tool of high-dimensional probability.
nodes.summary: Functions of many independent variables are nearly constant.

nodes.title: False Discovery Rate
nodes.html: Controlling the expected share of false positives among all rejected hypotheses (Benjamini and Hochberg, 1995) allows thousands of hypotheses to be tested at once with reasonable power. It is the standard approach in genomics and neuroimaging.
nodes.summary: Controlling the expected share of false positives among all rejected hypotheses (Benjamini and Hochberg, 1995) allows thousands of hypotheses to be tested at once with reasonable power.

nodes.title: Fermat’s Last Theorem

quote.text: I have discovered a truly marvellous proof of this, which this margin is too narrow to contain.

nodes.html: No positive integers satisfy aⁿ + bⁿ = cⁿ for n > 2. Wiles proved it in 1995, with Taylor’s help on a gap, through the modularity of semistable elliptic curves, 358 years after Fermat’s note. A Lean formalization led by Kevin Buzzard is under way.
nodes.summary: No positive integers satisfy aⁿ + bⁿ = cⁿ for n > 2.

nodes.title: Lasso
aliases: least absolute shrinkage and selection operator
nodes.html: Least squares with an absolute-value penalty on the coefficients (Tibshirani, 1996) shrinks many of them to exactly zero and so selects a few relevant variables. It is a central method of sparse, high-dimensional statistics and machine learning.
nodes.summary: Least squares with an absolute-value penalty on the coefficients (Tibshirani, 1996) shrinks many of them to exactly zero and so selects a few relevant variables.

nodes.title: Robbins Conjecture
nodes.html: Robbins conjectured in the 1930s that a simple modification of Huntington’s axioms still characterizes Boolean algebra. The automated prover EQP, run by McCune, found the proof in 1996 after about eight days of search, an early theorem of real interest proved by computer.
nodes.summary: Robbins conjectured in the 1930s that a simple modification of Huntington’s axioms still characterizes Boolean algebra.

nodes.title: Kepler Conjecture
nodes.html: No packing of equal spheres is denser than the greengrocer’s stack, about 74%. Referees of Hales’s 1998 computer-assisted proof said they were 99% certain of it; the Flyspeck project completed a formal proof in 2014.
nodes.summary: No packing of equal spheres is denser than the greengrocer’s stack, about 74%.

nodes.title: Khovanov Homology
nodes.html: Khovanov (1999) categorified the Jones polynomial: his homology theory of links has the polynomial as its Euler characteristic. It detects the unknot (Kronheimer and Mrowka, 2011) and gave Rasmussen a combinatorial proof of the Milnor conjecture on slice genus (2004).
nodes.summary: Khovanov (1999) categorified the Jones polynomial: his homology theory of links has the polynomial as its Euler characteristic.

nodes.title: Non-Sofic Groups Exist

progress.what: Announced a construction of a non-sofic group, with a Lean formalization of each argument; independent review is pending.
progress.html: Announced a construction of a non-sofic group, with a Lean formalization of each argument; independent review is pending.

nodes.html: Sofic groups, introduced by Gromov in 1999, are groups approximable by finite permutation groups, and it was unknown whether every group is sofic. On 1 August 2026 OpenAI announced a construction of a non-sofic group, produced by an internal model with a Lean formalization. It has not yet been independently reviewed.
nodes.summary: Sofic groups, introduced by Gromov in 1999, are groups approximable by finite permutation groups, and it was unknown whether every group is sofic.

nodes.title: Schramm–Loewner Evolution
nodes.html: Schramm (2000) described the scaling limits of critical two-dimensional lattice models by random fractal curves driven by Brownian motion. Lawler, Schramm and Werner used them to compute Brownian exponents, and Smirnov proved conformal invariance of critical percolation (2001).
nodes.summary: Schramm (2000) described the scaling limits of critical two-dimensional lattice models by random fractal curves driven by Brownian motion.

nodes.title: Yang–Mills Mass Gap
nodes.html: Construct quantum Yang–Mills theory rigorously in four dimensions and prove that its lightest particle has positive mass. Physicists use the theory daily; mathematicians cannot yet define it. A Clay Millennium Prize problem.
nodes.summary: Construct quantum Yang–Mills theory rigorously in four dimensions and prove that its lightest particle has positive mass.

nodes.title: Catalan’s Conjecture
nodes.html: The only two consecutive perfect powers are 8 and 9, as Catalan conjectured in 1844. Mihăilescu proved it in 2002 using cyclotomic fields and Galois modules.
nodes.summary: The only two consecutive perfect powers are 8 and 9, as Catalan conjectured in 1844.

nodes.title: Lorenz Attractor Proof
nodes.html: Tucker proved in 2002, with rigorous computer arithmetic, that the Lorenz equations have a robust strange attractor, solving Smale’s 14th problem (posed in 1998). It showed that computer-assisted proofs can handle chaotic flows.
nodes.summary: Tucker proved in 2002, with rigorous computer arithmetic, that the Lorenz equations have a robust strange attractor, solving Smale’s 14th problem (posed in 1998).

nodes.title: Strong Perfect Graph Theorem
nodes.html: A graph is perfect, meaning that in every induced subgraph the chromatic number equals the clique number, exactly when it has no odd hole and no odd antihole. Berge conjectured this in 1961; Chudnovsky, Robertson, Seymour and Thomas announced a proof in 2002 (published 2006).
nodes.summary: A graph is perfect, meaning that in every induced subgraph the chromatic number equals the clique number, exactly when it has no odd hole and no odd antihole.

nodes.title: Persistent Homology
nodes.html: Record which holes in a shape persist as the scale of observation changes (Edelsbrunner, Letscher and Zomorodian, 2002; Carlsson and Zomorodian, 2005). It is the main tool of topological data analysis, which uses topology to study the shape of data.
nodes.summary: Record which holes in a shape persist as the scale of observation changes (Edelsbrunner, Letscher and Zomorodian, 2002; Carlsson and Zomorodian, 2005).

nodes.title: Poincaré Conjecture
nodes.html: Every simply connected, closed 3-manifold is a 3-sphere. Perelman completed Hamilton’s Ricci-flow programme in 2002–03 and declined both the Fields Medal and the Millennium Prize.
nodes.summary: Every simply connected, closed 3-manifold is a 3-sphere.

nodes.title: Classification of Finite Simple Groups
nodes.html: Every finite simple group is cyclic, alternating, of Lie type, or one of 26 sporadic groups. The proof, by hundreds of mathematicians, runs to tens of thousands of pages; it was declared complete in 1983, and a gap in the quasithin case was closed by Aschbacher and Smith in 2004.
nodes.summary: Every finite simple group is cyclic, alternating, of Lie type, or one of 26 sporadic groups.

nodes.title: Graph Minor Theorem
nodes.html: In any infinite list of finite graphs, one is a minor of a later one (Robertson and Seymour, about 20 papers, 1983 to 2004). It follows that every minor-closed family of graphs is defined by finitely many forbidden minors, as Wagner had conjectured.
nodes.summary: In any infinite list of finite graphs, one is a minor of a later one (Robertson and Seymour, about 20 papers, 1983 to 2004).

nodes.title: Compressed Sensing
nodes.html: Sparse signals can be recovered exactly from far fewer measurements than classical sampling requires, by solving a convex L1-minimization problem (Candès, Romberg and Tao; Donoho; 2006). It speeds up MRI scans and other imaging.
nodes.summary: Sparse signals can be recovered exactly from far fewer measurements than classical sampling requires, by solving a convex L1-minimization problem (Candès, Romberg and Tao; Donoho; 2006).

nodes.title: Finite Field Kakeya
nodes.html: Dvir (2008) proved in a short polynomial argument that a subset of a finite-field vector space containing a line in every direction has at least a constant times q^n points, as Wolff conjectured in 1999. The proof introduced the polynomial method to combinatorics.
nodes.summary: Dvir (2008) proved in a short polynomial argument that a subset of a finite-field vector space containing a line in every direction has at least a constant times q^n points, as Wolff conjectured in 1999.

nodes.title: Erdős Distinct Distances Problem
nodes.html: n points in the plane determine at least about n / log n distinct distances (Guth and Katz, preprint 2010), nearly matching the n / √(log n) bound that grid sets achieve and settling Erdős’s 1946 question up to a root of a logarithm. The proof combines the polynomial method with the geometry of lines in space.
nodes.summary: n points in the plane determine at least about n / log n distinct distances (Guth and Katz, preprint 2010), nearly matching the n / √(log n) bound that grid sets achieve and settling Erdős’s 1946 question up to a root of a logarithm.

nodes.title: Hirsch Conjecture Disproved
nodes.html: Hirsch conjectured in 1957 that a polytope with n facets in d dimensions has diameter at most n − d. Santos (2010) constructed a counterexample in dimension 43 with 86 facets. Whether the diameter is polynomial in n and d, the polynomial Hirsch conjecture, remains open.
nodes.summary: Hirsch conjectured in 1957 that a polytope with n facets in d dimensions has diameter at most n − d.

nodes.title: Homotopy Type Theory
nodes.html: Types are read as spaces and equalities as paths. Voevodsky’s univalence axiom (2009) and the collaborative HoTT book (2013) proposed a foundation for mathematics suited to computer proof assistants. The book came out of a special year at the Institute for Advanced Study (2012 to 2013).
nodes.summary: Types are read as spaces and equalities as paths.

nodes.title: Kadison–Singer Problem
nodes.html: Kadison and Singer asked in 1959 whether every pure state on the diagonal matrices extends uniquely to all bounded operators on ℓ². The question is equivalent to problems in signal processing and discrepancy theory. Marcus, Spielman and Srivastava solved it in 2013 using interlacing polynomials.
nodes.summary: Kadison and Singer asked in 1959 whether every pure state on the diagonal matrices extends uniquely to all bounded operators on ℓ².

nodes.title: Gaussian Correlation Inequality
nodes.html: Two symmetric convex sets are positively correlated under any centered Gaussian measure. Conjectured between the 1950s and the 1970s, it was proved in 2014 by the retired statistician Thomas Royen, in the Far East Journal of Theoretical Statistics; an exposition by Latała and Matlak (2017) brought it wide attention.
nodes.summary: Two symmetric convex sets are positively correlated under any centered Gaussian measure.

nodes.title: Regularity Structures
nodes.html: Hairer’s theory (2014) makes sense of singular stochastic PDEs, such as the KPZ equation and the dynamic Φ⁴₃ model, in which products of distributions occur. It earned him the 2014 Fields Medal.
nodes.summary: Hairer’s theory (2014) makes sense of singular stochastic PDEs, such as the KPZ equation and the dynamic Φ⁴₃ model, in which products of distributions occur.

nodes.title: Erdős Discrepancy Problem
nodes.html: Every infinite ±1 sequence has unbounded sums along some progression d, 2d, 3d, and so on. A SAT solver settled the bound-2 case (Konev and Lisitsa, 2014), and the Polymath5 project laid groundwork for Tao’s proof (2015).
nodes.summary: Every infinite ±1 sequence has unbounded sums along some progression d, 2d, 3d, and so on.

nodes.title: Boolean Pythagorean Triples
nodes.html: The integers 1 to 7824 can be coloured red and blue with no monochromatic Pythagorean triple a² + b² = c², but 1 to 7825 cannot (Heule, Kullmann and Marek, 2016). The SAT-solver proof is 200 terabytes long, the largest mathematical proof at the time.
nodes.summary: The integers 1 to 7824 can be coloured red and blue with no monochromatic Pythagorean triple a² + b² = c², but 1 to 7825 cannot (Heule, Kullmann and Marek, 2016).

nodes.title: Sphere Packing in 8 and 24 Dimensions
nodes.html: Viazovska proved that the E₈ lattice gives the densest packing of spheres in 8 dimensions (2016), and she and four coauthors proved the same for the Leech lattice in 24 dimensions. The proofs use modular forms; Viazovska received the Fields Medal in 2022.
nodes.summary: Viazovska proved that the E₈ lattice gives the densest packing of spheres in 8 dimensions (2016), and she and four coauthors proved the same for the Leech lattice in 24 dimensions.

nodes.title: Lean & Mathlib
nodes.html: The Lean prover (from 2013) and Mathlib (from 2017), a community-built library large enough to state and check research mathematics. It doubles as the training ground and the referee for AI provers.
nodes.summary: The Lean prover (from 2013) and Mathlib (from 2017), a community-built library large enough to state and check research mathematics.

nodes.title: Onsager’s Conjecture
nodes.html: Onsager predicted in 1949 that Euler flows with Hölder exponent above 1/3 conserve energy and that rougher ones can dissipate it. Isett (2018) constructed energy-dissipating solutions at every exponent below 1/3 by convex integration, and Buckmaster, De Lellis, Székelyhidi and Vicol (2019) refined the result.
nodes.summary: Onsager predicted in 1949 that Euler flows with Hölder exponent above 1/3 conserve energy and that rougher ones can dissipate it.

nodes.title: Sensitivity Conjecture
nodes.html: Huang (2019) proved in about two pages that the degree of a Boolean function is at most the square of its sensitivity, settling a conjecture of Nisan and Szegedy from 1992. The proof uses a signed adjacency matrix of the hypercube and eigenvalue interlacing.
nodes.summary: Huang (2019) proved in about two pages that the degree of a Boolean function is at most the square of its sensitivity, settling a conjecture of Nisan and Szegedy from 1992.

nodes.title: Connes Embedding Problem
nodes.html: MIP* = RE (Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright and Yuen, 2020) showed that interactive proofs with entangled provers can verify the halting problem. Together with earlier work it refutes Connes’s 1976 embedding conjecture on von Neumann algebras and Tsirelson’s problem in quantum information.
nodes.summary: MIP* = RE (Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright and Yuen, 2020) showed that interactive proofs with entangled provers can verify the halting problem.

nodes.title: Conway Knot Is Not Slice
nodes.html: Piccirillo (2020) proved that the Conway knot, an 11-crossing knot found by Conway around 1970, does not bound a smooth disk in the 4-ball. She did so by finding a second knot with the same 4-dimensional trace and applying Rasmussen’s s-invariant to it.
nodes.summary: Piccirillo (2020) proved that the Conway knot, an 11-crossing knot found by Conway around 1970, does not bound a smooth disk in the 4-ball.

nodes.title: AI-Guided Conjectures
nodes.html: A DeepMind team with the mathematicians Juhász and Lackenby (knot theory) and Williamson (representation theory) used neural networks to find patterns in data. They found a new relation between two families of knot invariants and a candidate approach to the combinatorial invariance conjecture for Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials (Nature, December 2021).
nodes.summary: A DeepMind team with the mathematicians Juhász and Lackenby (knot theory) and Williamson (representation theory) used neural networks to find patterns in data.

nodes.title: Unit Conjecture Disproved
nodes.html: The unit conjecture predicts that the group ring of a torsion-free group over a field has only trivial units. Gardam (2021) found a nontrivial unit in the group ring over the field with two elements of a crystallographic group, with the help of a SAT solver, refuting a conjecture attributed to Higman (1940) and Kaplansky.
nodes.summary: The unit conjecture predicts that the group ring of a torsion-free group over a field has only trivial units.

nodes.title: Euler Blow-Up
nodes.html: Elgindi (2019) proved that solutions of the 3D Euler equations with C^{1,α} velocity can blow up in finite time. Chen and Hou (2022 to 2023) proved finite-time blow-up from smooth data for the axisymmetric Euler equations in a cylinder, with a computer-assisted proof.
nodes.summary: Elgindi (2019) proved that solutions of the 3D Euler equations with C^{1,α} velocity can blow up in finite time.

nodes.title: Kahn–Kalai Conjecture
nodes.html: Kahn and Kalai conjectured in 2006 that the threshold at which a random structure acquires a monotone property lies within a logarithmic factor of its ‘expectation threshold’, a much simpler quantity. Park and Pham proved it in 2022 in a short paper.
nodes.summary: Kahn and Kalai conjectured in 2006 that the threshold at which a random structure acquires a monotone property lies within a logarithmic factor of its ‘expectation threshold’, a much simpler quantity.

nodes.title: Liquid Tensor Experiment
nodes.html: In December 2020 Peter Scholze challenged the Lean community to check a key theorem of the condensed mathematics he developed with Dustin Clausen. A team led by Johan Commelin completed the formalization in July 2022, confirming the theorem.
nodes.summary: In December 2020 Peter Scholze challenged the Lean community to check a key theorem of the condensed mathematics he developed with Dustin Clausen.

nodes.title: Aperiodic Monotile
nodes.html: In March 2023 the amateur David Smith, with Craig Kaplan, Joseph Samuel Myers and Chaim Goodman-Strauss, showed that a 13-sided tile called the hat tiles the plane only aperiodically (reflections allowed). Their ‘spectre’ tile (May 2023) does so without reflections, answering the einstein problem of a single aperiodic tile.
nodes.summary: In March 2023 the amateur David Smith, with Craig Kaplan, Joseph Samuel Myers and Chaim Goodman-Strauss, showed that a 13-sided tile called the hat tiles the plane only aperiodically (reflections allowed).

nodes.title: FunSearch
nodes.html: A language model writes programs, an evaluator scores them, and an evolutionary loop keeps the best. FunSearch found cap sets in dimension 8 larger than any previously known (Nature, December 2023), new mathematics from an LLM-driven search.
nodes.summary: A language model writes programs, an evaluator scores them, and an evolutionary loop keeps the best.

nodes.title: Polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa Conjecture
nodes.html: If a set A in F₂ⁿ has |A + A| ≤ K|A|, then A is covered by polynomially many (in K) cosets of a subgroup of size at most |A|. This polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture (Marton) was proved by Gowers, Green, Manners and Tao in November 2023 with entropy methods, and formalized in Lean within three weeks.
nodes.summary: If a set A in F₂ⁿ has |A + A| ≤ K|A|, then A is covered by polynomially many (in K) cosets of a subgroup of size at most |A|.

nodes.title: Exponential Improvement for Ramsey
nodes.html: The diagonal Ramsey number satisfies R(k, k) ≤ (4 − ε)^k for a fixed ε > 0 (Campos, Griffiths, Morris and Sahasrabudhe, 2023), the first exponential improvement on the 4^k bound of Erdős and Szekeres (1935). Gupta, Ndiaye, Norin and Wei lowered the base to 3.8.
nodes.summary: The diagonal Ramsey number satisfies R(k, k) ≤ (4 − ε)^k for a fixed ε > 0 (Campos, Griffiths, Morris and Sahasrabudhe, 2023), the first exponential improvement on the 4^k bound of Erdős and Szekeres (1935).

nodes.title: AI Olympiad Silver
nodes.html: AlphaProof and AlphaGeometry 2 solved four of the six problems at the 2024 International Mathematical Olympiad, a silver-medal score. AlphaProof’s solutions are machine-checked Lean proofs.
nodes.summary: AlphaProof and AlphaGeometry 2 solved four of the six problems at the 2024 International Mathematical Olympiad, a silver-medal score.

nodes.title: Bunkbed Conjecture Disproved
nodes.html: Stack two copies of a graph and join them by vertical edges. Kasteleyn’s 1985 bunkbed conjecture said that after random edge deletion a vertex is at least as likely to stay connected to another vertex on its level as to that vertex’s copy on the other level. Gladkov, Pak and Zimin disproved it in 2024 with a 7,222-vertex counterexample based on Hollom’s work.
nodes.summary: Stack two copies of a graph and join them by vertical edges.

nodes.title: Empty Hexagon Theorem
nodes.html: Among any 30 points in general position in the plane, six form an empty convex hexagon, and 29 points do not suffice (Heule and Scheucher, 2024). The proof is a SAT computation whose encoding was later verified in Lean. It settles the empty-hexagon case of the happy ending problem.
nodes.summary: Among any 30 points in general position in the plane, six form an empty convex hexagon, and 29 points do not suffice (Heule and Scheucher, 2024).

nodes.title: Equational Theories Project
nodes.html: A crowdsourced project launched by Terence Tao in September 2024 determined all 22,028,942 implications among 4,694 equational laws of magmas, using volunteers, automated provers and Lean. Every implication was formally verified by April 2025, and a paper by 34 authors followed in December 2025.
nodes.summary: A crowdsourced project launched by Terence Tao in September 2024 determined all 22,028,942 implications among 4,694 equational laws of magmas, using volunteers, automated provers and Lean.

nodes.title: Geometric Langlands Conjecture
nodes.html: In May 2024 Dennis Gaitsgory, Sam Raskin and seven coauthors announced a proof of the unramified categorical geometric Langlands conjecture over the complex numbers, in five papers of more than 1,000 pages. It is a geometric counterpart of the Langlands correspondence, for sheaves on curves.
nodes.summary: In May 2024 Dennis Gaitsgory, Sam Raskin and seven coauthors announced a proof of the unramified categorical geometric Langlands conjecture over the complex numbers, in five papers of more than 1,000 pages.

nodes.title: Kervaire Invariant Problem
nodes.html: Framed manifolds with Kervaire invariant one can exist only in dimensions 2^j − 2, and do exist in dimensions 2, 6, 14, 30 and 62. Hill, Hopkins and Ravenel (2009) ruled out all dimensions from 254 up, and Lin, Wang and Xu (preprint, 2024) constructed one in dimension 126, the last open case.
nodes.summary: Framed manifolds with Kervaire invariant one can exist only in dimensions 2^j − 2, and do exist in dimensions 2, 6, 14, 30 and 62.

nodes.title: Bourgain’s Slicing Problem
nodes.html: Bourgain asked in 1986 whether every convex body of volume 1 in n dimensions has a hyperplane section of (n − 1)-dimensional volume bounded below by a universal constant. Klartag and Lehec answered yes in December 2024, using a bound of Qingyang Guan and the method of stochastic localization.
nodes.summary: Bourgain asked in 1986 whether every convex body of volume 1 in n dimensions has a hyperplane section of (n − 1)-dimensional volume bounded below by a universal constant.

nodes.title: AlphaEvolve
nodes.html: Gemini-powered program evolution (May 2025) multiplied 4×4 complex matrices with 48 multiplications, beating the 49 that Strassen’s 1969 method gives, and raised the 11-dimensional kissing number bound to 593.
nodes.summary: Gemini-powered program evolution (May 2025) multiplied 4×4 complex matrices with 48 multiplications, beating the 49 that Strassen’s 1969 method gives, and raised the 11-dimensional kissing number bound to 593.

nodes.title: Autoformalization at Scale
aliases: strong prime number theorem in Lean
nodes.html: Math, Inc.’s Gauss agent completed a Lean formalization of the strong prime number theorem, a challenge set by Terence Tao and Alex Kontorovich in January 2024, in about three weeks (September 2025). In 2026 it helped complete Lean formalizations of Viazovska’s sphere-packing proofs in dimensions 8 and 24.
nodes.summary: Math, Inc.’s Gauss agent completed a Lean formalization of the strong prime number theorem, a challenge set by Terence Tao and Alex Kontorovich in January 2024, in about three weeks (September 2025).

nodes.title: AI Olympiad Gold
nodes.html: At the 2025 International Mathematical Olympiad, an advanced Gemini Deep Think model and an experimental OpenAI model each solved five of the six problems in natural language, scoring 35 of 42: gold-medal level.
nodes.summary: At the 2025 International Mathematical Olympiad, an advanced Gemini Deep Think model and an experimental OpenAI model each solved five of the six problems in natural language, scoring 35 of 42: gold-medal level.

nodes.title: Kakeya Conjecture in 3D
nodes.html: A set in three-dimensional space containing a unit line segment in every direction has Hausdorff and Minkowski dimension 3 (Hong Wang and Joshua Zahl, February 2025). It settles the Kakeya set conjecture in dimension 3; Wang received the 2026 Fields Medal, in large part for this work.
nodes.summary: A set in three-dimensional space containing a unit line segment in every direction has Hausdorff and Minkowski dimension 3 (Hong Wang and Joshua Zahl, February 2025).

nodes.title: Mizohata–Takeuchi Counterexample
nodes.html: The Mizohata–Takeuchi conjecture proposed a weighted L² inequality for Fourier extension from a hypersurface, with a constant depending only on the X-ray transform of the weight. Hannah Cairo, then 17, constructed a counterexample in February 2025.
nodes.summary: The Mizohata–Takeuchi conjecture proposed a weighted L² inequality for Fourier extension from a hypersurface, with a constant depending only on the X-ray transform of the weight.

nodes.title: Noperthedron
nodes.html: A convex body has Rupert’s property if a copy of it can pass through a straight hole cut in the body itself. Steininger and Yurkevich (2025) constructed the Noperthedron, a polyhedron with 90 vertices that lacks the property, disproving a conjecture from 2017. The proof is computer-assisted.
nodes.summary: A convex body has Rupert’s property if a copy of it can pass through a straight hole cut in the body itself.

nodes.title: Unknotting Number Is Not Additive
nodes.html: The unknotting number is the minimum number of crossing changes that turn a knot into the unknot. Brittenham and Hermiller (2025) found knots whose connected sum has a smaller unknotting number than the sum of the two, answering a question implicit since Wendt (1937). The knot 7₁ joined to its mirror image needs at most 5 changes, although each summand needs 3.
nodes.summary: The unknotting number is the minimum number of crossing changes that turn a knot into the unknot.

nodes.title: Crouzeix’s Conjecture
nodes.html: Crouzeix conjectured in 2004 that ‖p(A)‖ ≤ 2 max|p| over the numerical range of A, for every square matrix A and polynomial p; the best general constant had been 1 + √2. Shanmu Jin posted a proof, obtained with GPT-5.6 Sol, on 27 July 2026. Crouzeix, Greenbaum and Townsend reviewed it, and Lorist and Schwenninger gave a second proof on 4 August.
nodes.summary: Crouzeix conjectured in 2004 that ‖p(A)‖ ≤ 2 max|p| over the numerical range of A, for every square matrix A and polynomial p; the best general constant had been 1 + √2.

nodes.title: Cycle Double Cover Conjecture
nodes.html: Every bridgeless graph has a family of cycles that covers each edge exactly twice (Szekeres, 1973; Seymour, 1979). OpenAI announced a three-page proof by GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra on 10 July 2026 and released a Lean formalization a week later; Sang-il Oum wrote an exposition of the argument.
nodes.summary: Every bridgeless graph has a family of cycles that covers each edge exactly twice (Szekeres, 1973; Seymour, 1979).

nodes.title: Fermat’s Last Theorem in Lean
nodes.html: On 4 September 2026 Anthropic announced a complete Lean 4 proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem, written in about eleven days by Claude agents directed by Tianyi Peng and reviewed by Kevin Buzzard. At about 13 million lines, it follows Wiles’s proof as simplified by Darmon, Diamond and Taylor and adapts parts of Buzzard’s Imperial College FLT project.
nodes.summary: On 4 September 2026 Anthropic announced a complete Lean 4 proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem, written in about eleven days by Claude agents directed by Tianyi Peng and reviewed by Kevin Buzzard.

nodes.title: Hilbert’s Tenth Problem over ℚ
aliases: Hilbert's tenth problem over the rationals

progress.what: Defined ℤ inside ℚ by a first-order formula, so the full first-order theory of ℚ is undecidable.
progress.html: Defined ℤ inside ℚ by a first-order formula, so the full first-order theory of ℚ is undecidable.

progress.what: Defined ℤ in ℚ by a universal formula. An existential definition would settle the problem negatively.
progress.html: Defined ℤ in ℚ by a universal formula. An existential definition would settle the problem negatively.

progress.what: No algorithm exists for any infinite ring finitely generated over ℤ, including the ring of integers of every number field.
progress.html: No algorithm exists for any infinite ring finitely generated over ℤ, including the ring of integers of every number field.

progress.what: An independent proof for rings of integers of number fields, through rank stability of abelian varieties in quadratic extensions.
progress.html: An independent proof for rings of integers of number fields, through rank stability of abelian varieties in quadratic extensions.

progress.what: Claimed negative answer: no algorithm decides whether a polynomial equation with integer coefficients has a rational solution (family 004 of OpenAI’s math release, not formalized). Not yet independently reviewed.
progress.html: Claimed negative answer: no algorithm decides whether a polynomial equation with integer coefficients has a rational solution (family 004 of OpenAI’s math release, not formalized). Not yet independently reviewed.

nodes.html: Is there an algorithm that decides whether a polynomial equation with integer coefficients has a solution in rational numbers? Over the integers the answer is no (1970), and proofs posted in 2024 and 2025 give the same answer for the ring of integers of every number field, and OpenAI’s October 2026 release claims the same for ℚ. Mazur’s conjectures suggest that ℤ is not Diophantine over ℚ, so a negative answer would need a different approach.
nodes.summary: Is there an algorithm that decides whether a polynomial equation with integer coefficients has a solution in rational numbers?

nodes.title: Hopf Problem

progress.what: Among spheres, only S² and S⁶ admit almost complex structures.
progress.html: Among spheres, only S² and S⁶ admit almost complex structures.

progress.what: No complex structure on S⁶ is orthogonal for the round metric.
progress.html: No complex structure on S⁶ is orthogonal for the round metric.

progress.what: Posted a 108-page construction, generated with an internal Claude model, of a compact complex threefold claimed to be diffeomorphic to S⁶. Robert Bryant reported an emerging consensus that it is plausible, and Boris Alexeev posted a Lean formalization; scrutiny continues.
progress.html: Posted a 108-page construction, generated with an internal Claude model, of a compact complex threefold claimed to be diffeomorphic to S⁶. Robert Bryant reported an emerging consensus that it is plausible, and Boris Alexeev posted a Lean formalization; scrutiny continues.

nodes.html: Does the 6-sphere admit a complex structure? It carries an almost complex structure from the octonions, and among spheres only S² and S⁶ admit almost complex structures (Borel and Serre, 1953), but whether S⁶ has an integrable one, a question named after Heinz Hopf, has resisted attempts since the 1940s. An August 2026 construction by Levent Alpöge, made with an internal Claude model, is under review.
nodes.summary: Does the 6-sphere admit a complex structure?

nodes.title: Jacobian Conjecture Fails in 3D
nodes.html: Keller’s 1939 Jacobian conjecture says that a polynomial map from ℂⁿ to itself with constant nonzero Jacobian determinant is invertible. On 19 July 2026 Levent Alpöge posted a degree-7 counterexample in three variables, found with Claude Fable 5; its Jacobian is −2 and it maps three points to one. The case n = 2 remains open.
nodes.summary: Keller’s 1939 Jacobian conjecture says that a polynomial map from ℂⁿ to itself with constant nonzero Jacobian determinant is invertible.

nodes.title: Köthe Conjecture Disproved
nodes.html: Köthe asked in 1930 whether a ring with no nonzero nil ideal also has no nonzero nil one-sided ideal. In September 2026 a pre-release OpenAI model, GPT-6 Astra, run by Tom Adamczewski of Epoch AI, found a counterexample with a Lean 4 proof. Böhmler and Marczinzik wrote it up, and Greenfeld, King and Vendramin gave a second construction.
nodes.summary: Köthe asked in 1930 whether a ring with no nonzero nil ideal also has no nonzero nil one-sided ideal.

nodes.title: Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis

progress.what: A zero-free region σ > 1 − c/log t, which narrows toward Re s = 1 as t grows.
progress.html: A zero-free region σ > 1 − c/log t, which narrows toward Re s = 1 as t grows.

progress.what: The widest known region of this kind, σ > 1 − c/((log t)^(2/3) (log log t)^(1/3)), still narrowing toward Re s = 1.
progress.html: The widest known region of this kind, σ > 1 − c/((log t)^(2/3) (log log t)^(1/3)), still narrowing toward Re s = 1.

progress.what: Claimed proof that every Dirichlet L-function, including ζ(s), is zero-free in Re s > 7/8, with a companion proof of Re s > 11/12 (family 003 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.
progress.html: Claimed proof that every Dirichlet L-function, including ζ(s), is zero-free in Re s > 7/8, with a companion proof of Re s > 11/12 (family 003 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.

nodes.html: Is there some δ > 0 such that ζ(s) has no zeros with real part greater than 1 − δ? The Riemann hypothesis says δ = ½ works, yet every zero-free region proved from de la Vallée Poussin (1899) to Vinogradov and Korobov (1958) narrows toward the line Re s = 1 at large heights. A zero-free half-plane would give a power saving in the prime number theorem.
nodes.summary: Is there some δ > 0 such that ζ(s) has no zeros with real part greater than 1 − δ?

nodes.title: Sendov’s Conjecture
nodes.html: If all roots of a polynomial of degree n ≥ 2 lie in the closed unit disk, each root has a critical point within distance 1 (Sendov, 1959). Tao proved it for large degree in 2020. Lech Mazur posted a Lean-verified proof for all degrees, developed with GPT-5.6 Pro, on 5 August 2026, and Tao published a digest with a shorter Lean formalization on 12 August.
nodes.summary: If all roots of a polynomial of degree n ≥ 2 lie in the closed unit disk, each root has a critical point within distance 1 (Sendov, 1959).

nodes.title: Periodic Billiards in Triangles

progress.what: Every polygon whose angles are rational multiples of π has periodic billiard paths.
progress.html: Every polygon whose angles are rational multiples of π has periodic billiard paths.

progress.what: Every obtuse triangle with largest angle at most 100° has a periodic path.
progress.html: Every obtuse triangle with largest angle at most 100° has a periodic path.

progress.what: Extended computer searches to obtuse triangles with largest angle up to 112.4°.
progress.html: Extended computer searches to obtuse triangles with largest angle up to 112.4°.

progress.what: Claimed proof, in a June 2026 preprint, that the billiard flow in every polygon has a periodic orbit, by contradiction from a theorem of Galperin, Krüger and Troubetzkoy and the cut locus of rescaled metrics on the unit tangent bundle.
progress.html: Claimed proof, in a June 2026 preprint, that the billiard flow in every polygon has a periodic orbit, by contradiction from a theorem of Galperin, Krüger and Troubetzkoy and the cut locus of rescaled metrics on the unit tangent bundle.

nodes.html: Does every triangular billiard table have a periodic path? Acute triangles have one (Fagnano’s orbit), as do right triangles, triangles whose angles are rational multiples of π, and, by computer search, obtuse triangles with largest angle up to 112.4°. In June 2026 Giovanni Forni posted a claimed proof that every polygon has a periodic billiard orbit.
nodes.summary: Does every triangular billiard table have a periodic path?

nodes.title: Unit Distance Conjecture Disproved
nodes.html: Erdős conjectured in 1946 that n points in the plane determine at most n^{1+ε} unit distances for every ε > 0. In May 2026 an OpenAI model constructed point sets with n^{1+c} unit distances for an absolute constant c > 0, using class field towers; Will Sawin’s follow-up gave an explicit exponent above 1.014.
nodes.summary: Erdős conjectured in 1946 that n points in the plane determine at most n^{1+ε} unit distances for every ε > 0.

nodes.title: Irrationality of ζ(5)

progress.what: Infinitely many of the odd zeta values ζ(3), ζ(5), ζ(7), … are irrational.
progress.html: Infinitely many of the odd zeta values ζ(3), ζ(5), ζ(7), … are irrational.

progress.what: At least one of ζ(5), ζ(7), ζ(9), ζ(11) is irrational.
progress.html: At least one of ζ(5), ζ(7), ζ(9), ζ(11) is irrational.

progress.what: Posted a preprint proof that ζ(5) is irrational, using Hankel determinants with a positive moment representation. Moritz Firsching reports a complete Lean formalization, stated against the Formal Conjectures version of the problem.
progress.html: Posted a preprint proof that ζ(5) is irrational, using Hankel determinants with a positive moment representation. Moritz Firsching reports a complete Lean formalization, stated against the Formal Conjectures version of the problem.

nodes.html: Is ζ(5) = 1 + 1/2⁵ + 1/3⁵ + … irrational? Apéry proved ζ(3) irrational in 1978, and later work showed that infinitely many odd zeta values are irrational, including at least one of ζ(5), ζ(7), ζ(9), ζ(11) (Zudilin, 2001). A September 2026 preprint by Aabir Fauzan claims a proof for ζ(5), with a Lean formalization reported complete.
nodes.summary: Is ζ(5) = 1 + 1/2⁵ + 1/3⁵ + … irrational?

nodes.title: Autonomous AI Mathematician

quote.text: Wir müssen wissen. Wir werden wissen. (We must know. We will know.)

progress.what: Released 719 manuscripts in 372 result families, produced mostly by an unreleased internal model, with claimed proofs including the Unique Games Conjecture and the quasi-Riemann hypothesis; 300 top-line results are formalized in Lean. Three manuscripts were withdrawn the next day; independent review is under way.

Three manuscripts were withdrawn the next day; independent review is under way.

nodes.html: An AI that poses, proves and formally verifies a result mathematicians agree is major, with no human steering. Every vibemathed result is a step toward it.
nodes.summary: An AI that poses, proves and formally verifies a result mathematicians agree is major, with no human steering.

nodes.title: Erdős Problems

progress.what: Claimed proofs of several famous Erdős conjectures, including the reciprocal-sum conjecture on arithmetic progressions, superexponential van der Waerden numbers and the Erdős–Gallai cycle-decomposition conjecture (families 159, 160 and 181, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.
progress.html: Claimed proofs of several famous Erdős conjectures, including the reciprocal-sum conjecture on arithmetic progressions, superexponential van der Waerden numbers and the Erdős–Gallai cycle-decomposition conjecture (families 159, 160 and 181, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.

nodes.html: More than a thousand problems Erdős posed, many with cash prizes, catalogued by Thomas Bloom at erdosproblems.com. Since 2025 a growing number have been settled with AI in the loop; VibeMathed tracks them.

nodes.title: Invariant Subspace Problem

progress.what: Every compact operator has a nontrivial closed invariant subspace.
progress.html: Every compact operator has a nontrivial closed invariant subspace.

progress.what: So does every operator that commutes with a nonzero compact operator.
progress.html: So does every operator that commutes with a nonzero compact operator.

progress.what: An operator on a Banach space with no nontrivial closed invariant subspace (outlined 1976, published 1987); Charles Read found one on ℓ¹ in 1985.
progress.html: An operator on a Banach space with no nontrivial closed invariant subspace (outlined 1976, published 1987); Charles Read found one on ℓ¹ in 1985.

progress.what: Posted a preprint claiming that every operator on a Hilbert space has a nontrivial invariant subspace. Neither it nor a separate claim by Charles Neville has been accepted as a solution.
progress.html: Posted a preprint claiming that every operator on a Hilbert space has a nontrivial invariant subspace. Neither it nor a separate claim by Charles Neville has been accepted as a solution.

progress.what: Claimed a nonzero quasinilpotent operator on every separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space with no nontrivial hyperinvariant subspace, which answers the hyperinvariant subspace problem but not this one (family 293 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.
progress.html: Claimed a nonzero quasinilpotent operator on every separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space with no nontrivial hyperinvariant subspace, which answers the hyperinvariant subspace problem but not this one (family 293 of OpenAI’s math release, formalized in Lean). Not yet independently reviewed.

nodes.html: Does every bounded linear operator on a separable complex Hilbert space of dimension at least 2 have a closed invariant subspace other than {0} and the whole space? Yes for compact operators and many other classes, and no on some Banach spaces (Enflo, Read). The Hilbert space case is still open, despite claimed proofs posted in 2023.

nodes.title: Inverse Galois Problem

progress.what: His irreducibility theorem realizes the symmetric and alternating groups over ℚ.
progress.html: His irreducibility theorem realizes the symmetric and alternating groups over ℚ.

progress.what: Every finite solvable group occurs. Alexander Schmidt later found a gap, which Shafarevich closed in 1989.
progress.html: Every finite solvable group occurs. Alexander Schmidt later found a gap, which Shafarevich closed in 1989.

progress.what: Realized the Monster group with the rigidity method; by 1989 all sporadic groups but one had been realized.
progress.html: Realized the Monster group with the rigidity method; by 1989 all sporadic groups but one had been realized.

progress.what: Realized the Mathieu group M23, the last sporadic group, with an explicit polynomial of degree 23.
progress.html: Realized the Mathieu group M23, the last sporadic group, with an explicit polynomial of degree 23.

nodes.html: Is every finite group the Galois group of some finite extension of the rational numbers? Hilbert (1892) and Noether (1918) laid the groundwork, and all symmetric, alternating and solvable groups and, since 2026, all 26 sporadic simple groups are known to occur. The general problem is open, and explicit polynomials for particular groups are checkable targets.
nodes.summary: Is every finite group the Galois group of some finite extension of the rational numbers?

progress.what: Found nontrivial links whose Jones polynomial equals that of an unlink.
progress.html: Found nontrivial links whose Jones polynomial equals that of an unlink.

progress.what: Infinite families of such links.
progress.html: Infinite families of such links.

progress.what: Khovanov homology, which refines the Jones polynomial, detects the unknot.
progress.html: Khovanov homology, which refines the Jones polynomial, detects the unknot.

progress.what: Every prime knot with at most 24 crossings has a Jones polynomial different from the unknot’s.
progress.html: Every prime knot with at most 24 crossings has a Jones polynomial different from the unknot’s.

nodes.html: Does the Jones polynomial (1984) detect the unknot, that is, does every nontrivial knot have a Jones polynomial different from that of the unknot? Computer checks cover all prime knots with up to 24 crossings, nontrivial links with trivial Jones polynomial exist, and its refinement Khovanov homology does detect the unknot (Kronheimer and Mrowka, 2011).

nodes.title: Kakeya Conjecture

progress.what: Kakeya sets in ℝⁿ have Hausdorff dimension at least (n + 2)/2.
progress.html: Kakeya sets in ℝⁿ have Hausdorff dimension at least (n + 2)/2.

progress.what: A bound of (2 − √2)(n − 4) + 3, better than Wolff’s in high dimensions.
progress.html: A bound of (2 − √2)(n − 4) + 3, better than Wolff’s in high dimensions.

progress.what: Kakeya sets in ℝ⁴ have Hausdorff dimension at least 3.059.
progress.html: Kakeya sets in ℝ⁴ have Hausdorff dimension at least 3.059.

progress.what: Claimed proof of the conjecture in four dimensions, and of the stronger maximal-function version in three (family 074 of OpenAI’s math release, not formalized). Not yet independently reviewed.
progress.html: Claimed proof of the conjecture in four dimensions, and of the stronger maximal-function version in three (family 074 of OpenAI’s math release, not formalized). Not yet independently reviewed.

nodes.html: Must every set in ℝⁿ that contains a unit line segment in every direction have Hausdorff dimension n? It is true in the plane (Davies, 1971) and in three dimensions (Wang and Zahl, 2025), OpenAI’s October 2026 release claims four dimensions, and for n ≥ 5 only partial lower bounds are known. The restriction conjecture of Fourier analysis implies it, so it is a necessary step toward that problem.
nodes.summary: Must every set in ℝⁿ that contains a unit line segment in every direction have Hausdorff dimension n?

nodes.title: Polynomial Hirsch Conjecture

progress.what: The diameter is at most n·2^(d − 3), linear in the number of facets for fixed dimension.
progress.html: The diameter is at most n·2^(d − 3), linear in the number of facets for fixed dimension.

progress.what: A quasi-polynomial bound, n^(log₂ d + 2).
progress.html: A quasi-polynomial bound, n^(log₂ d + 2).

progress.what: Improved it to (n − d)^(log₂ d).
progress.html: Improved it to (n − d)^(log₂ d).

nodes.html: Is the diameter of the graph of every d-dimensional polytope with n facets bounded by a polynomial in n and d? A no would rule out any polynomial-time pivot rule for the simplex method. Santos’s 2010 counterexample to the exact Hirsch bound n − d does not settle it, and the best known upper bound is quasi-polynomial (Kalai and Kleitman, 1992).

nodes.title: Projective Plane of Order 12

progress.what: No plane of order n exists if n is 1 or 2 mod 4 and not a sum of two squares. This rules out 6, 14, 21, 22, … but not 10 or 12.
progress.html: No plane of order n exists if n is 1 or 2 mod 4 and not a sum of two squares. This rules out 6, 14, 21, 22, … but not 10 or 12.

progress.what: Re-derived the nonexistence of a plane of order 10 with SAT solvers that produce independently checkable certificates, and found consistency issues in the earlier searches.
progress.html: Re-derived the nonexistence of a plane of order 10 with SAT solvers that produce independently checkable certificates, and found consistency issues in the earlier searches.

nodes.html: A finite projective plane of order n has n² + n + 1 points and as many lines, with every two points on exactly one line. Planes exist for every prime power order, and every known plane has prime power order; the Bruck–Ryser theorem (1949) excludes orders such as 6 and 14, and a huge computer search excluded 10 (1989). Order 12 is the smallest case still open.
nodes.summary: A finite projective plane of order n has n² + n + 1 points and as many lines, with every two points on exactly one line.

nodes.title: Smooth 4D Poincaré Conjecture

progress.what: Proved the topological 4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture.
progress.html: Proved the topological 4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture.

progress.what: Showed that the Akbulut–Kirby homotopy 4-sphere, long a candidate counterexample, is standard.
progress.html: Showed that the Akbulut–Kirby homotopy 4-sphere, long a candidate counterexample, is standard.

progress.what: An infinite family of Cappell–Shaneson homotopy spheres are all standard.
progress.html: An infinite family of Cappell–Shaneson homotopy spheres are all standard.

progress.what: Proposed detecting an exotic 4-sphere with Khovanov homology’s Rasmussen invariant; computer calculations on candidate knots found none.
progress.html: Proposed detecting an exotic 4-sphere with Khovanov homology’s Rasmussen invariant; computer calculations on candidate knots found none.

nodes.html: Is every smooth 4-manifold homotopy equivalent to the 4-sphere diffeomorphic to it? Freedman (1982) proved the topological version, and in dimension 4 the smooth and piecewise-linear versions are equivalent. Candidate exotic 4-spheres, such as the Cappell–Shaneson spheres, have repeatedly turned out to be standard.
nodes.summary: Is every smooth 4-manifold homotopy equivalent to the 4-sphere diffeomorphic to it?

nodes.title: Mathematical Astronomy
nodes.html: Babylonian astronomers kept centuries of records and predicted lunar and planetary positions with arithmetic schemes. Greek astronomers inherited their data.
nodes.summary: Babylonian astronomers kept centuries of records and predicted lunar and planetary positions with arithmetic schemes.

nodes.title: Spherical Earth
nodes.html: Aristotle (about 350 BCE) argued that Earth is a sphere, because its shadow on the Moon in eclipses is always round and the stars visible from a place change as one travels north or south. The idea had been proposed by the Pythagoreans, and from Aristotle on it was the basis of Greek geography and astronomy.
nodes.summary: Aristotle (about 350 BCE) argued that Earth is a sphere, because its shadow on the Moon in eclipses is always round and the stars visible from a place change as one travels north or south.

nodes.title: Archimedes’ Principle
nodes.html: In On Floating Bodies (about 250 BCE) Archimedes showed that a body immersed in a fluid is pushed up by a force equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces. With his law of the lever it began the mathematical study of statics, and it underlies the design of ships, submarines and balloons.
nodes.summary: In On Floating Bodies (about 250 BCE) Archimedes showed that a body immersed in a fluid is pushed up by a force equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces.

nodes.title: Earth’s Circumference
nodes.html: Eratosthenes (about 240 BCE) found that the noon Sun was overhead at Syene but cast a shadow at Alexandria, about one fiftieth of a circle to the north. From the distance between the cities he put Earth’s circumference at about 250,000 stadia, which, depending on which stadion is meant, is close to the true 40,000 km. It began geodesy.
nodes.summary: Eratosthenes (about 240 BCE) found that the noon Sun was overhead at Syene but cast a shadow at Alexandria, about one fiftieth of a circle to the north.

nodes.title: Precession of the Equinoxes
nodes.html: Comparing his own measurements of star positions with older records, Hipparchus found about 129 BCE that the equinox points drift slowly westward along the ecliptic, by at least one degree per century. Newton explained the cause in 1687 as the pull of the Sun and Moon on Earth’s equatorial bulge, which turns the axis around a cone once every 26,000 years.
nodes.summary: Comparing his own measurements of star positions with older records, Hipparchus found about 129 BCE that the equinox points drift slowly westward along the ecliptic, by at least one degree per century.

nodes.title: Ptolemy’s Almagest
nodes.html: Claudius Ptolemy’s Almagest (about 150 CE) set out a complete geocentric model of the Sun, Moon and planets built from circles, epicycles and the equant, with tables for computing their positions. It remained the standard astronomical text of the Islamic world and Europe for about 1,400 years, until Copernicus and Kepler.
nodes.summary: Claudius Ptolemy’s Almagest (about 150 CE) set out a complete geocentric model of the Sun, Moon and planets built from circles, epicycles and the equant, with tables for computing their positions.

nodes.title: Optics
nodes.html: Ibn al-Haytham’s Book of Optics (c. 1021) explained vision as light entering the eye and tested claims by experiment. Snell’s law of refraction followed in 1621.
nodes.summary: Ibn al-Haytham’s Book of Optics (c.

nodes.title: Tusi Couple
nodes.html: In 1247 Nasir al-Din al-Tusi described a device in which a circle rolling inside a circle twice its size makes a point on its rim move back and forth along a straight line. He and other astronomers of the Maragha school used it to build planetary models without Ptolemy’s equant, and the same construction appears in Copernicus’s De revolutionibus.
nodes.summary: In 1247 Nasir al-Din al-Tusi described a device in which a circle rolling inside a circle twice its size makes a point on its rim move back and forth along a straight line.

nodes.title: Mean Speed Theorem
nodes.html: The Oxford Calculators of Merton College (about 1335) proved that a body accelerating uniformly covers the same distance as one moving at a constant speed equal to the average of its initial and final speeds. Nicole Oresme gave a graphical proof around 1350 by plotting speed against time, and Galileo used the result in his law of falling bodies.
