progress.html: The fraction of permutations of order n that are Costas arrays decays exponentially.

nodes.html: A Costas array is an n×n permutation pattern in which the vectors between all pairs of dots are distinct, giving sonar and radar frequency-hopping signals an ideal ambiguity function (Costas, 1965). Constructions and searches give arrays for every order up to 31, but none is known for orders 32 and 33. Solving it means finding one or proving none exists for those orders; whether arrays exist for every n is open.
nodes.summary: A Costas array is an n×n permutation pattern in which the vectors between all pairs of dots are distinct, giving sonar and radar frequency-hopping signals an ideal ambiguity function (Costas, 1965).

nodes.title: MEMS
nodes.html: Harvey Nathanson and Robert Wickstrom at Westinghouse built the resonant-gate transistor in 1965, a tiny vibrating metal beam on a silicon chip, one of the first MEMS devices made by semiconductor methods. Micromachining later produced the accelerometers that trigger airbags and orient phones, as well as gyroscopes, pressure sensors and microphones.
nodes.summary: Harvey Nathanson and Robert Wickstrom at Westinghouse built the resonant-gate transistor in 1965, a tiny vibrating metal beam on a silicon chip, one of the first MEMS devices made by semiconductor methods.

nodes.title: DRAM
nodes.html: Robert Dennard at IBM devised the one-transistor, one-capacitor memory cell in 1966 and patented it in 1968, storing each bit as charge on a tiny capacitor that must be refreshed. Intel’s 1103 chip of 1970 was the first widely sold DRAM and soon replaced magnetic-core memory, and DRAM remains the main working memory of computers.
nodes.summary: Robert Dennard at IBM devised the one-transistor, one-capacitor memory cell in 1966 and patented it in 1968, storing each bit as charge on a tiny capacitor that must be refreshed.

nodes.title: Optical Fibre Communication
nodes.html: Charles Kao and George Hockham argued in 1966 that glass fibre could carry light over long distances if its impurities were removed, and in 1970 Robert Maurer, Donald Keck and Peter Schultz at Corning made fibre with a loss below 20 decibels per kilometre. Fibre now carries nearly all long-distance data, including undersea cables, and Kao shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Physics.
nodes.summary: Charles Kao and George Hockham argued in 1966 that glass fibre could carry light over long distances if its impurities were removed, and in 1970 Robert Maurer, Donald Keck and Peter Schultz at Corning made fibre with a loss below 20 decibels per kilometre.

nodes.title: Grad’s Conjecture

progress.what: Smooth equilibria on solid tori with nested pressure surfaces whose only symmetry is a finite rotation group, posted 21 September 2026 with a Lean 4 certification of the results.
progress.html: Smooth equilibria on solid tori with nested pressure surfaces whose only symmetry is a finite rotation group, posted 21 September 2026 with a Lean 4 certification of the results.

progress.what: Explicit analytic families of non-axisymmetric equilibria with exact nested flux surfaces, posted 22 September 2026; the paper says the solutions were discovered with GPT-6 Astra Pro and every equation was checked by hand.
progress.html: Explicit analytic families of non-axisymmetric equilibria with exact nested flux surfaces, posted 22 September 2026; the paper says the solutions were discovered with GPT-6 Astra Pro and every equation was checked by hand.

nodes.html: Grad argued in 1967 that smooth plasma equilibria in a torus, with nested pressure surfaces and non-constant pressure, must have a symmetry such as axisymmetry; stellarators, whose fields have none, rely on such equilibria. In September 2026 two independent preprints posted counterexamples, one with a Lean 4 certification and one with explicit formulas found using an AI model. Neither is peer reviewed yet.
nodes.summary: Grad argued in 1967 that smooth plasma equilibria in a torus, with nested pressure surfaces and non-constant pressure, must have a symmetry such as axisymmetry; stellarators, whose fields have none, rely on such equilibria.

nodes.title: Programmable Logic Controller
nodes.html: General Motors asked in 1968 for a rugged, reprogrammable replacement for relay panels, and Dick Morley’s Bedford Associates answered with the Modicon 084 in 1969. A PLC runs control logic in software that technicians can change without rewiring, and PLCs still operate factory machinery, utilities and other automated systems.
nodes.summary: General Motors asked in 1968 for a rugged, reprogrammable replacement for relay panels, and Dick Morley’s Bedford Associates answered with the Modicon 084 in 1969.

nodes.title: Witsenhausen’s Counterexample

progress.what: The discrete version of the problem is NP-complete.
progress.html: The discrete version of the problem is NP-complete.

progress.what: Hierarchical search finds sloped step-function strategies with benchmark cost 0.1673, far below the best linear cost of about 0.96.
progress.html: Hierarchical search finds sloped step-function strategies with benchmark cost 0.1673, far below the best linear cost of about 0.96.

progress.what: Lattice quantization strategies come within a constant factor of the optimal cost for every choice of parameters.
progress.html: Lattice quantization strategies come within a constant factor of the optimal cost for every choice of parameters.

progress.what: A local search guided by variational optimality conditions gives the lowest known costs on the benchmark.
progress.html: A local search guided by variational optimality conditions gives the lowest known costs on the benchmark.

nodes.html: Two controllers act in turn on a Gaussian state: the first sees it exactly but pays k² per unit of control energy, the second sees it only through noise and must cancel it. Witsenhausen showed in 1968 that nonlinear signalling strategies beat every linear one, and the optimal pair is still unknown. Solving it means finding and proving the optimal laws; the standard benchmark is k = 0.2, σ = 5, best known cost about 0.1669.
nodes.summary: Two controllers act in turn on a Gaussian state: the first sees it exactly but pays k² per unit of control energy, the second sees it only through noise and must cancel it.

nodes.title: Charge-Coupled Device
nodes.html: Willard Boyle and George Smith sketched the charge-coupled device at Bell Labs in 1969, a chip that moves packets of electric charge along rows of tiny capacitors and so can read out an image. CCD sensors became the eyes of digital cameras, camcorders and space telescopes, and the pair shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Physics.
nodes.summary: Willard Boyle and George Smith sketched the charge-coupled device at Bell Labs in 1969, a chip that moves packets of electric charge along rows of tiny capacitors and so can read out an image.

nodes.title: Moon Landing

quote.text: That’s one small step for [a] man, one giant leap for mankind.

nodes.html: Apollo 11 landed on 20 July 1969. Its guidance computer was one of the first built from integrated circuits.
nodes.summary: Apollo 11 landed on 20 July 1969.

nodes.title: CT Scanner
nodes.html: Godfrey Hounsfield built the first computed tomography scanner at EMI, and on 1 October 1971 it imaged a patient’s brain at Atkinson Morley’s Hospital in London, with a computer combining X-ray measurements taken from many angles. Allan Cormack had worked out the mathematics, and the two shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. CT is now routine in diagnosis.
nodes.summary: Godfrey Hounsfield built the first computed tomography scanner at EMI, and on 1 October 1971 it imaged a patient’s brain at Atkinson Morley’s Hospital in London, with a computer combining X-ray measurements taken from many angles.

nodes.title: Space Station
nodes.html: The Soviet Union launched Salyut 1, the first space station, on 19 April 1971, and later stations such as Skylab, Mir and Tiangong followed. The International Space Station has been continuously crewed since November 2000, and its laboratories have given long-term data on human health in weightlessness, on materials and on the Earth.
nodes.summary: The Soviet Union launched Salyut 1, the first space station, on 19 April 1971, and later stations such as Skylab, Mir and Tiangong followed.

nodes.title: Digital Fly-by-Wire
nodes.html: NASA’s modified F-8 Crusader made the first flight of an aircraft with a fully digital fly-by-wire system on 25 May 1972, using an Apollo guidance computer and no mechanical backup. The Airbus A320 of 1987 brought digital fly-by-wire to airliners, where computers now stabilize the aircraft and keep it within safe limits.
nodes.summary: NASA’s modified F-8 Crusader made the first flight of an aircraft with a fully digital fly-by-wire system on 25 May 1972, using an Apollo guidance computer and no mechanical backup.

nodes.title: Humanoid Robot
nodes.html: Ichiro Kato’s group at Waseda University completed WABOT-1 around 1972, the first full-scale humanoid robot, which walked on two legs, gripped objects with its hands and spoke Japanese. Honda’s ASIMO (2000) and later machines such as Boston Dynamics’ Atlas walk, run and carry loads, and humanoid robots are now being developed as general-purpose workers.
nodes.summary: Ichiro Kato’s group at Waseda University completed WABOT-1 around 1972, the first full-scale humanoid robot, which walked on two legs, gripped objects with its hands and spoke Japanese.

nodes.title: Low-Autocorrelation Binary Sequences

progress.what: Skew-symmetric families with asymptotic merit factor above 6.34, matching the best known for any binary sequences.
progress.html: Skew-symmetric families with asymptotic merit factor above 6.34, matching the best known for any binary sequences.

progress.what: A branch-and-bound algorithm running in time Θ(N·1.73^N) finds all optimal sequences up to N = 66, and skew-symmetric optima up to 119.
progress.html: A branch-and-bound algorithm running in time Θ(N·1.73^N) finds all optimal sequences up to N = 66, and skew-symmetric optima up to 119.

progress.what: With colleagues, used LABS as a quantum benchmark: QAOA’s simulated time-to-solution scales better than branch-and-bound, with runs on Quantinuum trapped-ion processors.
progress.html: With colleagues, used LABS as a quantum benchmark: QAOA’s simulated time-to-solution scales better than branch-and-bound, with runs on Quantinuum trapped-ion processors.

nodes.html: Find ±1 sequences of length N whose aperiodic autocorrelations have the least total energy, that is the highest Golay merit factor, as wanted for radar pulse compression (Golay, 1972). Exact optima are known only for N ≤ 66 (2016), and the best proven asymptotic merit factor is about 6.34, against Golay’s heuristic ceiling of about 12.32. Progress means certified optima beyond 66 or better asymptotic constructions.
nodes.summary: Find ±1 sequences of length N whose aperiodic autocorrelations have the least total energy, that is the highest Golay merit factor, as wanted for radar pulse compression (Golay, 1972).

nodes.title: Interstellar Probe

progress.what: Project Daedalus (1973–78) designed an uncrewed fusion-rocket probe to reach Barnard’s Star in about 50 years.
progress.html: Project Daedalus (1973–78) designed an uncrewed fusion-rocket probe to reach Barnard’s Star in about 50 years.

progress.what: Voyager 1 entered interstellar space; launched in 1977, it is the farthest human-made object.
progress.html: Voyager 1 entered interstellar space; launched in 1977, it is the farthest human-made object.

progress.what: Breakthrough Starshot proposed a fleet of gram-scale probes on metre-scale sails pushed by a ground laser array of up to 100 GW.
progress.html: Breakthrough Starshot proposed a fleet of gram-scale probes on metre-scale sails pushed by a ground laser array of up to 100 GW.

nodes.html: Send a working probe to another star and receive its data within a human lifetime; at today’s probe speeds, reaching Alpha Centauri (4.4 light years) would take tens of thousands of years. Voyager 1 (launched 1977) reached interstellar space in 2012, and Breakthrough Starshot (2016) proposed laser-driven gram-scale sails at 15–20% of light speed before pausing in 2025. Solving it means a probe that reaches another star system and reports back.
nodes.summary: Send a working probe to another star and receive its data within a human lifetime; at today’s probe speeds, reaching Alpha Centauri (4.4 light years) would take tens of thousands of years.

nodes.title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging
nodes.html: Paul Lauterbur showed in 1973 that magnetic field gradients could encode the position of nuclear spin signals and so form images, and Peter Mansfield developed fast imaging methods. Raymond Damadian’s team scanned the first human body in 1977. MRI shows soft tissue in fine detail without ionizing radiation, and Lauterbur and Mansfield shared the 2003 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
nodes.summary: Paul Lauterbur showed in 1973 that magnetic field gradients could encode the position of nuclear spin signals and so form images, and Peter Mansfield developed fast imaging methods.

nodes.title: Pulse Oximeter
nodes.html: Takuo Aoyagi and Michio Kishi at Nihon Kohden developed pulse oximetry in 1972, finding that the pulsing of arterial blood changes how red and infrared light pass through the skin, and the company filed a patent in 1974. Pulse oximeters read blood oxygen without drawing blood and became standard in anaesthesia, intensive care and home monitoring.
nodes.summary: Takuo Aoyagi and Michio Kishi at Nihon Kohden developed pulse oximetry in 1972, finding that the pulsing of arterial blood changes how red and infrared light pass through the skin, and the company filed a patent in 1974.

nodes.title: Rendezvous Search Problem

progress.what: Proposed the stay-or-search strategy for n locations, conjectured optimal.
progress.html: Proposed the stay-or-search strategy for n locations, conjectured optimal.

progress.what: Formalized rendezvous search as a mathematical problem, including the continuous version.
progress.html: Formalized rendezvous search as a mathematical problem, including the continuous version.

progress.what: Proved the Anderson–Weber strategy optimal for three locations, the first non-trivial symmetric case solved.
progress.html: Proved the Anderson–Weber strategy optimal for three locations, the first non-trivial symmetric case solved.

nodes.html: Two players placed among n identical locations move each period and want to meet as soon as possible, but cannot agree on roles beforehand (Alpern, 1976); search-and-rescue teams and robots face versions of it. For the symmetric discrete game, Anderson and Weber’s 1990 randomized strategy is conjectured optimal, and Weber proved it for n = 3 in 2012. Solving it means proving or refuting optimality for n ≥ 4.
nodes.summary: Two players placed among n identical locations move each period and want to meet as soon as possible, but cannot agree on roles beforehand (Alpern, 1976); search-and-rescue teams and robots face versions of it.

nodes.title: Human-Powered Aircraft
nodes.html: Paul MacCready’s Gossamer Condor, pedalled by Bryan Allen, flew a figure-eight course on 23 August 1977 to win the first Kremer prize, and the Gossamer Albatross crossed the English Channel on 12 June 1979. Their ultralight structures led to solar-powered and high-altitude aircraft, and AeroVelo’s Atlas won the Sikorsky human-powered helicopter prize in 2013.
nodes.summary: Paul MacCready’s Gossamer Condor, pedalled by Bryan Allen, flew a figure-eight course on 23 August 1977 to win the first Kremer prize, and the Gossamer Albatross crossed the English Channel on 12 June 1979.

nodes.title: Cochlear Implant
nodes.html: André Djourno and Charles Eyriès in Paris stimulated a deaf patient’s auditory nerve with an implanted coil in 1957. Graeme Clark’s multichannel implant, first used in Melbourne in 1978, and a parallel design by Ingeborg Hochmair in Austria let patients understand speech, and implants have since restored hearing to hundreds of thousands of people.
nodes.summary: André Djourno and Charles Eyriès in Paris stimulated a deaf patient’s auditory nerve with an implanted coil in 1957.

nodes.title: Model Predictive Control
nodes.html: Jacques Richalet’s group in France in 1978 and Charles Cutler at Shell in 1979 developed controllers that predict a process’s future behaviour with a model and repeatedly solve an optimization over a moving time horizon, applying only the first step. Model predictive control became standard in refineries and chemical plants and is now used in rockets, cars and power systems.
nodes.summary: Jacques Richalet’s group in France in 1978 and Charles Cutler at Shell in 1979 developed controllers that predict a process’s future behaviour with a model and repeatedly solve an optimization over a moving time horizon, applying only the first step.

nodes.title: Cellular Network
nodes.html: Bell Labs engineers, notably Douglas Ring in 1947, proposed cellular networks, in which a region is divided into cells that reuse frequencies. Martin Cooper of Motorola made the first handheld mobile phone call in 1973, and NTT opened the first commercial cellular network in Tokyo in 1979. There are now more mobile subscriptions than people.
nodes.summary: Bell Labs engineers, notably Douglas Ring in 1947, proposed cellular networks, in which a region is divided into cells that reuse frequencies.

nodes.title: Robust Control
nodes.html: George Zames posed the problem of designing feedback that performs well for a whole family of plant models in 1981, using the H-infinity norm to measure sensitivity. John Doyle, Keith Glover and colleagues gave an efficient state-space solution in 1988 and 1989. Robust control gives guarantees against model error and is used in aircraft, spacecraft and industrial systems.
nodes.summary: George Zames posed the problem of designing feedback that performs well for a whole family of plant models in 1981, using the H-infinity norm to measure sensitivity.

nodes.title: Scanning Tunneling Microscope
nodes.html: Image individual atoms, and move them, using a quantum tunnelling current (1981). In 1989 IBM researchers spelled the company’s logo with 35 xenon atoms.
nodes.summary: Image individual atoms, and move them, using a quantum tunnelling current (1981).

nodes.title: Space Shuttle
nodes.html: Columbia made the first flight of NASA’s Space Shuttle, the first reusable crewed orbiter, on 12 April 1981. The shuttles flew 135 missions until 2011, launched the Hubble Space Telescope and helped build the International Space Station, but the Challenger accident of 1986 and the Columbia accident of 2003 killed fourteen astronauts.
nodes.summary: Columbia made the first flight of NASA’s Space Shuttle, the first reusable crewed orbiter, on 12 April 1981.

nodes.title: Artificial Heart
nodes.html: Robert Jarvik’s Jarvik-7, implanted in the dentist Barney Clark by William DeVries in Utah in December 1982, was meant as a permanent artificial heart, and Clark lived 112 days. Continuous-flow pumps now support thousands of patients with heart failure, and a magnetically levitated total artificial heart, BiVACOR, was first implanted in 2024.
nodes.summary: Robert Jarvik’s Jarvik-7, implanted in the dentist Barney Clark by William DeVries in Utah in December 1982, was meant as a permanent artificial heart, and Clark lived 112 days.

nodes.title: IGBT
nodes.html: Jayant Baliga at General Electric demonstrated the insulated-gate bipolar transistor in 1982, a switch that combines the easy voltage control of a MOSFET with the high current capacity of a bipolar transistor. IGBTs switch the power in electric cars, trains, wind turbines, solar inverters and air conditioners.
nodes.summary: Jayant Baliga at General Electric demonstrated the insulated-gate bipolar transistor in 1982, a switch that combines the easy voltage control of a MOSFET with the high current capacity of a bipolar transistor.

nodes.title: Dynamic Legged Robot
nodes.html: Marc Raibert’s Leg Laboratory at Carnegie Mellon University built one-legged hopping machines in the early 1980s that balanced by bouncing, showing that dynamic balance can come from simple control rules. His company Boston Dynamics later built the quadruped BigDog (2005) and the humanoid Atlas, and legged robots now walk, run and flip outside the laboratory.
nodes.summary: Marc Raibert’s Leg Laboratory at Carnegie Mellon University built one-legged hopping machines in the early 1980s that balanced by bouncing, showing that dynamic balance can come from simple control rules.

nodes.title: Small-Time Local Controllability

progress.what: A general sufficient condition: every bad Lie bracket must be neutralized by good brackets of higher order.
progress.html: A general sufficient condition: every bad Lie bracket must be neutralized by good brackets of higher order.

progress.what: Quadratic obstructions for scalar-input systems: at quadratic order every bracket is bad, with drifts measured by negative Sobolev norms of the control.
progress.html: Quadratic obstructions for scalar-input systems: at quadratic order every bracket is bad, with drifts measured by negative Sobolev norms of the control.

progress.what: New quartic sufficient conditions and quartic obstructions, answering Kawski’s 1987 question about Hall bases that separate good and bad quartic brackets.
progress.html: New quartic sufficient conditions and quartic obstructions, answering Kawski’s 1987 question about Hall bases that separate good and bad quartic brackets.

progress.what: Factor-parity Hall sets: their good brackets can all be steered in small time, and each bad bracket yields an obstruction.
progress.html: Factor-parity Hall sets: their good brackets can all be steered in small time, and each bad bracket yields an obstruction.

nodes.html: Find a test, in terms of the Lie brackets of its vector fields at an equilibrium, for when a nonlinear control system can reach every nearby state in arbitrarily short time. Exact criteria exist for linear and driftless systems, but with drift Sussmann’s conditions (1983, 1987) are only sufficient and the full list of good and bad brackets is unknown. Solving it means a necessary and sufficient criterion, even just for scalar-input systems.
nodes.summary: Find a test, in terms of the Lie brackets of its vector fields at an equilibrium, for when a nonlinear control system can reach every nearby state in arbitrarily short time.

nodes.title: 3D Printing
nodes.html: Chuck Hull filed the patent for stereolithography in 1984, building solid objects layer by layer from liquid resin hardened by ultraviolet light, after Hideo Kodama’s 1981 paper on the same idea. Carl Deckard’s selective laser sintering (1986) and Scott Crump’s fused deposition modelling (1989) followed. Additive manufacturing is now used for prototypes, tools, implants and aerospace parts.
nodes.summary: Chuck Hull filed the patent for stereolithography in 1984, building solid objects layer by layer from liquid resin hardened by ultraviolet light, after Hideo Kodama’s 1981 paper on the same idea.

nodes.title: Flash Memory
nodes.html: Fujio Masuoka at Toshiba invented flash memory, presented in 1984, a non-volatile memory that can be erased in blocks and keeps its data without power. NAND flash followed in 1987, and flash memory now stores data in phones, cameras, USB sticks and solid-state drives, and has largely replaced the hard disk in laptops.
nodes.summary: Fujio Masuoka at Toshiba invented flash memory, presented in 1984, a non-volatile memory that can be erased in blocks and keeps its data without power.

nodes.title: SLAM
nodes.html: Randall Smith and Peter Cheeseman showed in 1986 how a robot could estimate the positions of map features and its own position together, treating their errors as correlated, and Hugh Durrant-Whyte and colleagues made the idea into practical algorithms. SLAM lets robots, drones and phones build a map while moving through unknown places.
nodes.summary: Randall Smith and Peter Cheeseman showed in 1986 how a robot could estimate the positions of map features and its own position together, treating their errors as correlated, and Hugh Durrant-Whyte and colleagues made the idea into practical algorithms.

nodes.title: Deep Brain Stimulation
nodes.html: Alim-Louis Benabid and Pierre Pollak in Grenoble reported in 1987 that stimulating the thalamus with high-frequency pulses from an implanted electrode stopped tremor, and the method spread to Parkinson’s disease and dystonia. In 2025 the US approved a version that senses the patient’s brain signals and adapts its stimulation.
nodes.summary: Alim-Louis Benabid and Pierre Pollak in Grenoble reported in 1987 that stimulating the thalamus with high-frequency pulses from an implanted electrode stopped tremor, and the method spread to Parkinson’s disease and dystonia.

nodes.title: Erbium-Doped Fibre Amplifier
nodes.html: David Payne’s group at the University of Southampton and Emmanuel Desurvire at Bell Labs showed in 1987 that fibre doped with erbium ions can amplify light directly when pumped by a laser, with no conversion to electricity. Erbium amplifiers replaced electronic repeaters on long fibre links, made wavelength-division multiplexing practical and let undersea cables carry far more data.
nodes.summary: David Payne’s group at the University of Southampton and Emmanuel Desurvire at Bell Labs showed in 1987 that fibre doped with erbium ions can amplify light directly when pumped by a laser, with no conversion to electricity.

nodes.title: Adaptive Optics
nodes.html: Horace Babcock proposed in 1953 correcting atmospheric blur by measuring the distorted wavefront and reshaping a mirror in real time. The first astronomical system, COME-ON, was tested in France in 1989 and moved to ESO’s 3.6 metre telescope in Chile. Adaptive optics now lets large ground telescopes rival space telescopes in sharpness at some wavelengths.
nodes.summary: Horace Babcock proposed in 1953 correcting atmospheric blur by measuring the distorted wavefront and reshaping a mirror in real time.

nodes.title: Hubble Space Telescope
nodes.html: Lyman Spitzer argued in 1946 for a telescope in space, and NASA and ESA launched the Hubble Space Telescope on 24 April 1990. Astronauts corrected a flaw in its mirror in 1993, and it went on to make deep images and measure the age and expansion of the universe. The James Webb Space Telescope, with a folding 6.5 metre mirror, followed in 2021.
nodes.summary: Lyman Spitzer argued in 1946 for a telescope in space, and NASA and ESA launched the Hubble Space Telescope on 24 April 1990.

nodes.title: Exact Quasisymmetric Stellarator

progress.what: A near-axis expansion indicates that quasisymmetry can generally be imposed only to second order in the distance from the magnetic axis.
progress.html: A near-axis expansion indicates that quasisymmetry can generally be imposed only to second order in the distance from the magnetic axis.

progress.what: Optimized fields that are quasisymmetric to much higher precision than thought possible over a large volume, with symmetry-breaking fields about as weak as Earth’s for a 1 T device.
progress.html: Optimized fields that are quasisymmetric to much higher precision than thought possible over a large volume, with symmetry-breaking fields about as weak as Earth’s for a 1 T device.

nodes.html: Do smooth magnetic equilibria exist that are exactly quasisymmetric throughout a volume, confining particles as well as a tokamak without being axisymmetric? Garren and Boozer’s 1991 near-axis expansion suggests the equations are overdetermined away from the magnetic axis, yet optimized fields reach quasisymmetry to remarkable precision (Landreman and Paul, 2022). Solving it means an exact construction or a proof of impossibility.
nodes.summary: Do smooth magnetic equilibria exist that are exactly quasisymmetric throughout a volume, confining particles as well as a tokamak without being axisymmetric?

nodes.title: Digital Mobile Phone (GSM)
nodes.html: The Groupe Spécial Mobile, formed by European telecom administrations in 1982 and later part of ETSI, specified a digital mobile standard, and the first GSM call was made in Helsinki in July 1991. SIM cards, text messages, encryption and roaming between countries made it the world’s dominant mobile system, used by billions.
nodes.summary: The Groupe Spécial Mobile, formed by European telecom administrations in 1982 and later part of ETSI, specified a digital mobile standard, and the first GSM call was made in Helsinki in July 1991.

nodes.title: Offshore Wind Farm
nodes.html: Denmark built the first offshore wind farm at Vindeby in 1991, eleven 450 kilowatt turbines in shallow water off Lolland. Offshore turbines can be larger and meet steadier wind than onshore ones, and floating designs such as Hywind Scotland (2017) opened deep water to wind power.
nodes.summary: Denmark built the first offshore wind farm at Vindeby in 1991, eleven 450 kilowatt turbines in shallow water off Lolland.

nodes.title: Blue LED
nodes.html: Isamu Akasaki and Hiroshi Amano made the first gallium nitride blue LEDs in Nagoya in 1989, and Shuji Nakamura at Nichia made bright, efficient ones in 1993. Blue light completed the red and green LEDs, and with a phosphor it gave white light at a fraction of the energy of incandescent bulbs. The three shared the 2014 Nobel Prize in Physics.
nodes.summary: Isamu Akasaki and Hiroshi Amano made the first gallium nitride blue LEDs in Nagoya in 1989, and Shuji Nakamura at Nichia made bright, efficient ones in 1993.

nodes.title: CMOS Image Sensor
nodes.html: Eric Fossum and his team at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory developed the CMOS active-pixel sensor in 1993, a camera on a chip in which each pixel has its own amplifier and the circuits are made with standard CMOS processes. It cost less and used less power than CCDs, put a camera in every phone, and now dominates digital imaging.
nodes.summary: Eric Fossum and his team at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory developed the CMOS active-pixel sensor in 1993, a camera on a chip in which each pixel has its own amplifier and the circuits are made with standard CMOS processes.

nodes.title: Taillard Job-Shop Benchmarks

progress.what: Reinforcement learning that shrinks constraint-programming search trees raised the lower bounds of many open instances.
progress.html: Reinforcement learning that shrinks constraint-programming search trees raised the lower bounds of many open instances.

progress.what: New constraint-programming lower bounds for ta18 and the open 20×20 instances.
progress.html: New constraint-programming lower bounds for ta18 and the open 20×20 instances.

progress.what: A schedule of makespan 1997 for ta45, matching its lower bound and closing the instance, found by memetic tabu search with path relinking and CP-SAT (manuscript in preparation).
progress.html: A schedule of makespan 1997 for ta45, matching its lower bound and closing the instance, found by memetic tabu search with path relinking and CP-SAT (manuscript in preparation).

progress.what: New best schedules for ta26, ta32, ta44 and ta46.
progress.html: New best schedules for ta26, ta32, ta44 and ta46.

nodes.html: Find the shortest schedules (makespans) for Taillard’s 80 job-shop instances (1993), from 15 jobs on 15 machines to 100 jobs on 20 machines, and prove them optimal; they are the standard test of factory scheduling methods. As of the 28 September 2026 update, 20 instances with 20 or 30 jobs still have a gap between the best schedule and the best lower bound. Each instance closed counts.
nodes.summary: Find the shortest schedules (makespans) for Taillard’s 80 job-shop instances (1993), from 15 jobs on 15 machines to 100 jobs on 20 machines, and prove them optimal; they are the standard test of factory scheduling methods.

nodes.title: Differential Flatness Test

progress.what: For single-input systems, linearization by dynamic feedback reduces to static feedback, so flatness is checkable there.
progress.html: For single-input systems, linearization by dynamic feedback reduces to static feedback, so flatness is checkable there.

progress.what: A necessary and sufficient condition stated with polynomial matrices of differential operators; turning it into a finite test remains open.
progress.html: A necessary and sufficient condition stated with polynomial matrices of differential operators; turning it into a finite test remains open.

progress.what: A complete, finite test for two-input systems that can be linearized by a two-dimensional endogenous dynamic feedback.
progress.html: A complete, finite test for two-input systems that can be linearized by a two-dimensional endogenous dynamic feedback.

nodes.html: A nonlinear control system is differentially flat when a few output functions determine all its states and inputs without integration, which turns trajectory planning into algebra (Fliess, Lévine, Martin and Rouchon, 1995). No general, checkable necessary and sufficient test for flatness is known; tests exist only for special classes such as single-input systems. Solving it means a finite, verifiable criterion for multi-input systems.
nodes.summary: A nonlinear control system is differentially flat when a few output functions determine all its states and inputs without integration, which turns trajectory planning into algebra (Fliess, Lévine, Martin and Rouchon, 1995).

nodes.title: GPS
nodes.html: Satellite navigation using atomic clocks in orbit, fully operational in 1995. Without relativistic corrections its positions would drift by roughly 10 km a day.
nodes.summary: Satellite navigation using atomic clocks in orbit, fully operational in 1995.

nodes.title: MIRUP Cutting-Stock Conjecture

progress.what: Instances with integrality gap 6/5, the largest known.
progress.html: Instances with integrality gap 6/5, the largest known.

progress.what: For bin packing, the configuration LP has an additive integrality gap of O(log OPT), the best bound known.
progress.html: For bin packing, the configuration LP has an additive integrality gap of O(log OPT), the best bound known.

progress.what: All instances with up to 9 item lengths have the round-up property; the smallest counterexample has 10, and the worst known proper gap rose from 1.003 to 1.0625.
progress.html: All instances with up to 9 item lengths have the round-up property; the smallest counterexample has 10, and the worst known proper gap rose from 1.003 to 1.0625.

nodes.html: In one-dimensional cutting stock, rolls or bars are cut into ordered lengths using as few stock pieces as possible. Scheithauer and Terno conjectured in 1995 that the optimum never exceeds the Gilmore–Gomory linear-programming bound rounded up, plus one; the largest gap found is 6/5, and the best general bound grows logarithmically. Solving it means a proof that the gap is always below 2, or an instance with gap at least 2.
nodes.summary: In one-dimensional cutting stock, rolls or bars are cut into ordered lengths using as few stock pieces as possible.

nodes.title: MIMO Wireless
nodes.html: Arogyaswami Paulraj and Thomas Kailath at Stanford filed the foundational patent on spatial multiplexing with multiple antennas in 1992, and Gerard Foschini at Bell Labs proposed the layered space-time architecture BLAST in 1996. Using several antennas at both ends lets a radio link carry several data streams on one frequency, and MIMO is now at the core of Wi-Fi, 4G and 5G.
nodes.summary: Arogyaswami Paulraj and Thomas Kailath at Stanford filed the foundational patent on spatial multiplexing with multiple antennas in 1992, and Gerard Foschini at Bell Labs proposed the layered space-time architecture BLAST in 1996.

nodes.title: Mars Rover
nodes.html: NASA’s Sojourner, a small six-wheeled rover carried by the Mars Pathfinder lander, drove on Mars in July 1997. The larger rovers Spirit and Opportunity (2004) and Curiosity (2012) followed, and Opportunity covered 45 kilometres over fourteen years. Perseverance (2021) has been collecting rock samples for return to Earth.
nodes.summary: NASA’s Sojourner, a small six-wheeled rover carried by the Mars Pathfinder lander, drove on Mars in July 1997.

nodes.title: Static Output Feedback Stabilization

progress.what: Claimed NP-hardness of unrestricted static output feedback stabilization, even with a single input, by reduction from the Betweenness problem. ChatGPT 5.6 and Claude Opus 5 helped with ideation, verification code, writing and adversarial review.
progress.html: Claimed NP-hardness of unrestricted static output feedback stabilization, even with a single input, by reduction from the Betweenness problem. ChatGPT 5.6 and Claude Opus 5 helped with ideation, verification code, writing and adversarial review.

progress.what: Claimed strong NP-hardness in continuous and discrete time by reduction from 3SAT. The authors report that ChatGPT 5.6 produced a first one-shot proof on 2 August 2026, which they then simplified with it.
progress.html: Claimed strong NP-hardness in continuous and discrete time by reduction from 3SAT. The authors report that ChatGPT 5.6 produced a first one-shot proof on 2 August 2026, which they then simplified with it.

progress.what: An independent claim of NP-hardness by reduction from Subset Sum.
progress.html: An independent claim of NP-hardness by reduction from Subset Sum.

progress.what: Claimed the problem is complete for the existential theory of the reals for two-input integer plants, strongly NP-hard for a family of single-input plants, and polynomial-time when an effective gain dimension is fixed.
progress.html: Claimed the problem is complete for the existential theory of the reals for two-input integer plants, strongly NP-hard for a family of single-input plants, and polynomial-time when an effective gain dimension is fixed.

nodes.html: Given a linear plant, decide whether some constant gain from its measured outputs to its inputs makes it stable. Blondel and Tsitsiklis proved this NP-hard in 1997 only for gains confined to intervals, leaving the unrestricted case, a long-standing open question of control theory. In September 2026 four independent preprints claimed it is NP-hard, so no efficient exact test exists unless P = NP; none is peer reviewed yet.
nodes.summary: Given a linear plant, decide whether some constant gain from its measured outputs to its inputs makes it stable.

nodes.title: Wi-Fi
nodes.html: The IEEE approved the 802.11 wireless local network standard in 1997 under the chairmanship of Vic Hayes. The faster 802.11a and 802.11b versions followed in 1999, and OFDM radio, covered by patents from CSIRO’s John O’Sullivan and colleagues, later made Wi-Fi fast. It is now the usual way to connect devices to the Internet indoors.
nodes.summary: The IEEE approved the 802.11 wireless local network standard in 1997 under the chairmanship of Vic Hayes.

nodes.title: Continuous Glucose Monitor
nodes.html: MiniMed’s Continuous Glucose Monitoring System gained US FDA approval in 1999, using a small sensor under the skin to record glucose every few minutes for later review. Real-time monitors followed in the 2000s, replacing finger-prick tests for many people with diabetes and supplying the readings that automated insulin delivery systems use.
nodes.summary: MiniMed’s Continuous Glucose Monitoring System gained US FDA approval in 1999, using a small sensor under the skin to record glucose every few minutes for later review.

nodes.title: CubeSat
nodes.html: Jordi Puig-Suari of Cal Poly and Bob Twiggs of Stanford proposed the CubeSat standard in 1999, a 10 centimetre cube that fits a standard launch dispenser, and the first were launched in 2003. Standard parts and shared rides made satellites cheap enough for universities, companies and developing countries, and well over a thousand CubeSats have flown.
nodes.summary: Jordi Puig-Suari of Cal Poly and Bob Twiggs of Stanford proposed the CubeSat standard in 1999, a 10 centimetre cube that fits a standard launch dispenser, and the first were launched in 2003.

nodes.title: FinFET
nodes.html: Chenming Hu’s group at Berkeley, including Tsu-Jae King Liu and Jeffrey Bokor, and Hitachi’s Digh Hisamoto developed the FinFET by 1999, a transistor whose channel is a thin vertical fin wrapped by the gate on several sides. The gate controls leakage better as transistors shrink; Intel began production in 2011, and gate-all-around transistors, which succeed FinFETs, entered production in 2022.
nodes.summary: Chenming Hu’s group at Berkeley, including Tsu-Jae King Liu and Jeffrey Bokor, and Hitachi’s Digh Hisamoto developed the FinFET by 1999, a transistor whose channel is a thin vertical fin wrapped by the gate on several sides.

nodes.title: Surgical Robot
nodes.html: Intuitive Surgical’s da Vinci system, which lets a surgeon operate small instruments through tiny cuts while seated at a console, received US FDA clearance for general laparoscopic surgery in 2000. Robot-assisted operations in urology, gynaecology and general surgery now number millions a year.
nodes.summary: Intuitive Surgical’s da Vinci system, which lets a surgeon operate small instruments through tiny cuts while seated at a console, received US FDA clearance for general laparoscopic surgery in 2000.

nodes.title: Stability of Switched Linear Systems

progress.what: Deciding whether the joint spectral radius is at most 1, or whether all products stay bounded, is undecidable, even for a pair of matrices.
progress.html: Deciding whether the joint spectral radius is at most 1, or whether all products stay bounded, is undecidable, even for a pair of matrices.

progress.what: The finiteness conjecture, which would have made the strict question decidable, is false: the joint spectral radius need not be attained by any finite product.
progress.html: The finiteness conjecture, which would have made the strict question decidable, is false: the joint spectral radius need not be attained by any finite product.

progress.what: An explicit counterexample to the finiteness conjecture.
progress.html: An explicit counterexample to the finiteness conjecture.

progress.what: An invariant-polytope algorithm computes the exact joint spectral radius, with a certificate, for many families of matrices.
progress.html: An invariant-polytope algorithm computes the exact joint spectral radius, with a certificate, for many families of matrices.

nodes.html: Given a finite set of matrices, decide whether every long product of them shrinks to zero, that is whether their joint spectral radius ρ is below 1; this is the stability of a linear system that switches arbitrarily among them. Blondel and Tsitsiklis proved in 2000 that deciding ρ ≤ 1 is undecidable, but whether ρ < 1 is decidable is unknown. Solving it means an algorithm or an undecidability proof.
nodes.summary: Given a finite set of matrices, decide whether every long product of them shrinks to zero, that is whether their joint spectral radius ρ is below 1; this is the stability of a linear system that switches arbitrarily among them.

nodes.title: Capacity of Optical Fibre

progress.what: Capacity estimates for nonlinear fibre peak and then fall as signal power rises, suggesting a nonlinear limit.
progress.html: Capacity estimates for nonlinear fibre peak and then fall as signal power rises, suggesting a nonlinear limit.

progress.what: A closed-form lower bound on capacity, at any signal-to-noise ratio, for links with zero average dispersion.
progress.html: A closed-form lower bound on capacity, at any signal-to-noise ratio, for links with zero average dispersion.

progress.what: Systematic capacity-limit estimates for optically routed networks, the reference curves of the nonlinear limit.
progress.html: Systematic capacity-limit estimates for optically routed networks, the reference curves of the nonlinear limit.

progress.what: Spectral efficiency is at most log(1 + SNR) for a cascade model of the nonlinear Schrödinger channel, an upper bound that grows without limit.
progress.html: Spectral efficiency is at most log(1 + SNR) for a cascade model of the nonlinear Schrödinger channel, an upper bound that grows without limit.

nodes.html: What is the Shannon capacity of a long amplified optical fibre, where the Kerr effect makes the signal interfere with itself and with amplifier noise? Achievable-rate estimates (Mitra and Stark 2001; Essiambre et al. 2010) peak and then fall as launch power grows, while the best upper bound, log(1 + SNR), keeps rising (2015). Solving it means closing that gap, or at least deciding whether capacity stays bounded as power grows.
nodes.summary: What is the Shannon capacity of a long amplified optical fibre, where the Kerr effect makes the signal interfere with itself and with amplifier noise?

nodes.title: Home Robot
nodes.html: iRobot, founded by Rodney Brooks, Colin Angle and Helen Greiner, launched the Roomba robot vacuum cleaner in September 2002. It was the first home robot to sell in large numbers, and iRobot has sold tens of millions of them, which brought autonomous navigation into ordinary homes.
nodes.summary: iRobot, founded by Rodney Brooks, Colin Angle and Helen Greiner, launched the Roomba robot vacuum cleaner in September 2002.

nodes.title: Warehouse Robots
nodes.html: Kiva Systems, founded in 2003 by Mick Mountz with Raffaello D’Andrea and Peter Wurman, built mobile robots that slide under shelves and carry them to human pickers, so that pickers stay at a station. Amazon bought Kiva in 2012 and had more than 200,000 such robots by 2020, and warehouse automation is now standard in large e-commerce.
nodes.summary: Kiva Systems, founded in 2003 by Mick Mountz with Raffaello D’Andrea and Peter Wurman, built mobile robots that slide under shelves and carry them to human pickers, so that pickers stay at a station.

nodes.title: Private Crewed Spaceflight
nodes.html: Burt Rutan’s Scaled Composites, funded by Paul Allen, flew SpaceShipOne above 100 kilometres in June 2004, the first crewed spaceflight by a privately funded vehicle, and won the 10 million dollar Ansari X Prize, announced in 1996, with two flights in five days ending on 4 October 2004. It started the commercial suborbital flight industry.
nodes.summary: Burt Rutan’s Scaled Composites, funded by Paul Allen, flew SpaceShipOne above 100 kilometres in June 2004, the first crewed spaceflight by a privately funded vehicle, and won the 10 million dollar Ansari X Prize, announced in 1996, with two flights in five days ending on 4 October 2004.

nodes.title: Scramjet
nodes.html: NASA’s unpiloted X-43A reached Mach 9.6 on 16 November 2004 under scramjet power, a speed record for an air-breathing aircraft, after the HyShot flights of 2002 had shown supersonic combustion in flight. A scramjet burns fuel in a supersonic airflow and so needs no turbine, and the concept is studied for hypersonic missiles and reusable launch vehicles.
nodes.summary: NASA’s unpiloted X-43A reached Mach 9.6 on 16 November 2004 under scramjet power, a speed record for an air-breathing aircraft, after the HyShot flights of 2002 had shown supersonic combustion in flight.

nodes.title: Arduino
nodes.html: Massimo Banzi, David Cuartielles, Tom Igoe, Gianluca Martino and David Mellis made the first Arduino board at the Interaction Design Institute Ivrea in 2005 as a cheap, open-source microcontroller for design students. Its simple programming environment and open hardware let artists, students and hobbyists build working electronics, and it became a standard tool of the maker movement.
nodes.summary: Massimo Banzi, David Cuartielles, Tom Igoe, Gianluca Martino and David Mellis made the first Arduino board at the Interaction Design Institute Ivrea in 2005 as a cheap, open-source microcontroller for design students.

nodes.title: Autonomous Desert Driving
nodes.html: Stanford’s Stanley, led by Sebastian Thrun, drove 212 kilometres of desert track without a driver to win the DARPA Grand Challenge and its 2 million dollar prize on 8 October 2005; in the 2004 race no vehicle got past 12 kilometres. The contest brought researchers together, and many team members went on to lead self-driving car projects.
nodes.summary: Stanford’s Stanley, led by Sebastian Thrun, drove 212 kilometres of desert track without a driver to win the DARPA Grand Challenge and its 2 million dollar prize on 8 October 2005; in the 2004 race no vehicle got past 12 kilometres.

nodes.title: Optical Lattice Clock
nodes.html: Hidetoshi Katori proposed in 2001 trapping atoms in an optical lattice at a magic wavelength, where the trapping light does not shift the clock transition, and strontium lattice clocks from his group followed in 2003 and 2005. Optical clocks now keep time far better than the caesium clocks that define the second, and are expected to lead to a new definition of it.
nodes.summary: Hidetoshi Katori proposed in 2001 trapping atoms in an optical lattice at a magic wavelength, where the trapping light does not shift the clock transition, and strontium lattice clocks from his group followed in 2003 and 2005.

nodes.title: Brain–Computer Interface
nodes.html: In 2006 Matthew Nagle, paralysed by a spinal injury, used a 96-electrode array implanted in his motor cortex by the BrainGate team led by John Donoghue and Leigh Hochberg to move a computer cursor and operate a robotic hand with his thoughts. Later participants controlled robot arms and typed, and brain implants are now being tested to restore movement and speech.
nodes.summary: In 2006 Matthew Nagle, paralysed by a spinal injury, used a 96-electrode array implanted in his motor cortex by the BrainGate team led by John Donoghue and Leigh Hochberg to move a computer cursor and operate a robotic hand with his thoughts.

nodes.title: Evolved Antenna
nodes.html: Jason Lohn, Gregory Hornby and Derek Linden at NASA Ames used a genetic algorithm to design antennas for the three Space Technology 5 satellites, launched in March 2006. Each satellite carried an evolved antenna of unusual bent-wire shape beside a conventional helix antenna, and it was reported as the first computer-evolved hardware to fly in space.
nodes.summary: Jason Lohn, Gregory Hornby and Derek Linden at NASA Ames used a genetic algorithm to design antennas for the three Space Technology 5 satellites, launched in March 2006.

nodes.title: Super-Resolution Microscopy
nodes.html: Light microscopes were long thought limited by diffraction to about 200 nanometres, until Stefan Hell’s STED microscopy (2000) and the single-molecule methods PALM, from Eric Betzig’s group, and STORM, from Xiaowei Zhuang’s (both 2006), produced sharper images. Hell, Betzig and William Moerner won the 2014 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
nodes.summary: Light microscopes were long thought limited by diffraction to about 200 nanometres, until Stefan Hell’s STED microscopy (2000) and the single-molecule methods PALM, from Eric Betzig’s group, and STORM, from Xiaowei Zhuang’s (both 2006), produced sharper images.

nodes.title: Convex Landing Guidance
nodes.html: Behçet Açıkmeşe and Scott Ploen showed in 2007 that the fuel-optimal powered-descent problem for a lander can be turned into a convex optimization problem without loss of optimality, which flight computers can solve quickly. JPL flew the method on Masten Space Systems’ Xombie rocket in 2012 and 2013, and similar guidance is used to land reusable rocket boosters.
nodes.summary: Behçet Açıkmeşe and Scott Ploen showed in 2007 that the fuel-optimal powered-descent problem for a lander can be turned into a convex optimization problem without loss of optimality, which flight computers can solve quickly.

nodes.title: General-Purpose Household Robot

progress.what: Figure 01 learned to operate a Keurig coffee machine from video demonstrations with end-to-end neural networks.
progress.html: Figure 01 learned to operate a Keurig coffee machine from video demonstrations with end-to-end neural networks.

progress.what: π0, a vision-language-action flow model for general robot control across many robots and tasks.
progress.html: π0, a vision-language-action flow model for general robot control across many robots and tasks.

progress.what: π0.5 performed long, dexterous tasks such as cleaning a kitchen or bedroom in entirely new homes.
progress.html: π0.5 performed long, dexterous tasks such as cleaning a kitchen or bedroom in entirely new homes.

nodes.html: A robot that can enter an unfamiliar home and do the chores, from laundry to cooking, safely and without supervision; Steve Wozniak’s coffee test asks it to find the machine, the coffee and a mug and brew a cup. Robots now make coffee in demonstrations and clean kitchens in homes they have never seen (π0.5, 2025), but none does general household work reliably. Solving it means robust unsupervised performance across ordinary homes.
nodes.summary: A robot that can enter an unfamiliar home and do the chores, from laundry to cooking, safely and without supervision; Steve Wozniak’s coffee test asks it to find the machine, the coffee and a mug and brew a cup.

nodes.title: Smartphone
nodes.html: IBM’s Simon of 1994 combined a phone with a touchscreen, e-mail and apps, and Apple’s iPhone, announced in January 2007, joined a multi-touch screen, a camera, a web browser and mobile data in one device. Smartphones now put a networked computer, camera and GPS receiver in billions of pockets and changed how people communicate, shop, navigate and work.
nodes.summary: IBM’s Simon of 1994 combined a phone with a touchscreen, e-mail and apps, and Apple’s iPhone, announced in January 2007, joined a multi-touch screen, a camera, a web browser and mobile data in one device.

nodes.title: Lithium-Ion Electric Car
nodes.html: The Tesla Roadster, developed by a team that included Martin Eberhard, Marc Tarpenning and JB Straubel, began deliveries in 2008 as the first production car to use lithium-ion cells and to travel more than 300 kilometres on a charge, and the mass-market Nissan Leaf followed in 2010. Electric cars passed a fifth of new car sales worldwide in 2024.
nodes.summary: The Tesla Roadster, developed by a team that included Martin Eberhard, Marc Tarpenning and JB Straubel, began deliveries in 2008 as the first production car to use lithium-ion cells and to travel more than 300 kilometres on a charge, and the mass-market Nissan Leaf followed in 2010.

nodes.title: RepRap
nodes.html: Adrian Bowyer started the RepRap project at the University of Bath in 2005 to build an open-source 3D printer that could print most of its own parts. Its first design, Darwin, made copies of its own plastic parts in 2008, and the freely shared designs seeded the desktop 3D printer industry.
nodes.summary: Adrian Bowyer started the RepRap project at the University of Bath in 2005 to build an open-source 3D printer that could print most of its own parts.

nodes.title: Solar Sail
nodes.html: JAXA’s IKAROS, launched in May 2010, was the first spacecraft to demonstrate solar sailing in interplanetary space, using a 14 metre square membrane pushed by sunlight on its way past Venus. The Planetary Society’s LightSail 2 raised its orbit around Earth by light pressure alone in 2019.
nodes.summary: JAXA’s IKAROS, launched in May 2010, was the first spacecraft to demonstrate solar sailing in interplanetary space, using a 14 metre square membrane pushed by sunlight on its way past Venus.

nodes.title: Global Village Construction Set

progress.what: 12 of the 50 machines designed, blueprinted and prototyped, 4 of them fully documented.
progress.html: 12 of the 50 machines designed, blueprinted and prototyped, 4 of them fully documented.

progress.what: Reported about 33% completion of the set.
progress.html: Reported about 33% completion of the set.

nodes.html: Publish open-source designs for the 50 industrial machines a small community needs to sustain modern life, from a tractor and a brick press to a 3D printer, so that anyone can build them from the documentation, as Marcin Jakubowski of Open Source Ecology set out in a 2011 TED talk. By 2014 12 machines had been prototyped, and OSE reported a third of the set done in 2018. Solving it means all 50 built and replicated by others.
nodes.summary: Publish open-source designs for the 50 industrial machines a small community needs to sustain modern life, from a tractor and a brick press to a 3D printer, so that anyone can build them from the documentation, as Marcin Jakubowski of Open Source Ecology set out in a 2011 TED talk.

nodes.title: Quadruple Pendulum Swing-Up

progress.what: Swing-up of a triple pendulum on a cart, validated on hardware, with nonlinear feedforward and optimal feedback control.
progress.html: Swing-up of a triple pendulum on a cart, validated on hardware, with nonlinear feedforward and optimal feedback control.

progress.what: Model-free reinforcement learning swings up and balances a real triple inverted pendulum.
progress.html: Model-free reinforcement learning swings up and balances a real triple inverted pendulum.

progress.what: A model-free reinforcement-learning policy (truncated quantile critics) that swings up and balances a quadruple inverted pendulum in real time from measured data, described as a first for model-free control.
progress.html: A model-free reinforcement-learning policy (truncated quantile critics) that swings up and balances a quadruple inverted pendulum in real time from measured data, described as a first for model-free control.

nodes.html: Swing a four-link pendulum on a cart from hanging straight down to balanced upright, and hold it there, on real hardware. The triple pendulum was first swung up on a cart in 2013, and a 2025 paper reports a model-free reinforcement-learning swing-up of a quadruple pendulum in real time, but its abstract and video do not show a physical rig. A documented, reproducible hardware demonstration would settle it.
nodes.summary: Swing a four-link pendulum on a cart from hanging straight down to balanced upright, and hold it there, on real hardware.

nodes.title: Calibration-Free Cuffless Blood Pressure

progress.what: IEEE 1708, the first standard for wearable cuffless blood pressure devices.
progress.html: IEEE 1708, the first standard for wearable cuffless blood pressure devices.

progress.what: PulseDB, a large cleaned dataset from MIMIC-III and VitalDB for benchmarking cuffless methods.
progress.html: PulseDB, a large cleaned dataset from MIMIC-III and VitalDB for benchmarking cuffless methods.

progress.what: A benchmark of 11 machine-learning methods on four open datasets, with validation that avoids subject leakage.
progress.html: A benchmark of 11 machine-learning methods on four open datasets, with validation that avoids subject leakage.

progress.what: On the NBPDB benchmark no evaluated model met the standard; adding age, sex and BMI brought one model to mean absolute errors of 4.75 mmHg systolic and 2.90 mmHg diastolic.
progress.html: On the NBPDB benchmark no evaluated model met the standard; adding age, sex and BMI brought one model to mean absolute errors of 4.75 mmHg systolic and 2.90 mmHg diastolic.

nodes.html: Estimate blood pressure from an optical pulse signal (PPG) at the finger or wrist, without calibrating against a cuff, as accurately as AAMI/ISO 81060-2 demands of any monitor: mean error within ±5 mmHg and standard deviation at most 8 mmHg. On the 2026 NBPDB benchmark (101,453 PPG segments from MIMIC-III and VitalDB) none of the published models tested met it; solving it means a model that does on held-out public data.
nodes.summary: Estimate blood pressure from an optical pulse signal (PPG) at the finger or wrist, without calibrating against a cuff, as accurately as AAMI/ISO 81060-2 demands of any monitor: mean error within ±5 mmHg and standard deviation at most 8 mmHg.

nodes.title: Full Self-Driving (Level 5)

progress.what: Carnegie Mellon and General Motors’ Boss won the DARPA Urban Challenge, driving a 96 km urban course while obeying traffic rules.
progress.html: Carnegie Mellon and General Motors’ Boss won the DARPA Urban Challenge, driving a 96 km urban course while obeying traffic rules.

progress.what: The first public robotaxi service without safety drivers, in Phoenix.
progress.html: The first public robotaxi service without safety drivers, in Phoenix.

progress.what: 500,000 paid driverless rides a week in 10 US metro areas and 200 million fully autonomous miles by June 2026, still within mapped service areas.
progress.html: 500,000 paid driverless rides a week in 10 US metro areas and 200 million fully autonomous miles by June 2026, still within mapped service areas.

nodes.html: A car that drives itself anywhere and in any conditions a competent human driver could, with no human fallback: Level 5 in SAE’s J3016 taxonomy (2014). As of 2026 no such system exists; Waymo’s driverless Level 4 robotaxis, limited to mapped areas of 10 US metros, gave 500,000 paid rides a week in June 2026. Solving it means unrestricted driverless operation with safety at least matching human drivers.
nodes.summary: A car that drives itself anywhere and in any conditions a competent human driver could, with no human fallback: Level 5 in SAE’s J3016 taxonomy (2014).

nodes.title: DIY Artificial Pancreas
nodes.html: Dana Lewis and Scott Leibrand built a closed-loop insulin delivery system from an insulin pump, a glucose monitor and open software in 2014 and 2015, and shared it online as OpenAPS under the slogan ‘we are not waiting’. The first commercial hybrid closed-loop system, Medtronic’s MiniMed 670G, was approved in 2016, and many people with diabetes still build their own.
nodes.summary: Dana Lewis and Scott Leibrand built a closed-loop insulin delivery system from an insulin pump, a glucose monitor and open software in 2014 and 2015, and shared it online as OpenAPS under the slogan ‘we are not waiting’.

nodes.title: Reusable Orbital Rockets
nodes.html: A Falcon 9 first stage landed upright after an orbital launch on 21 December 2015. Individual boosters now fly dozens of times.
nodes.summary: A Falcon 9 first stage landed upright after an orbital launch on 21 December 2015.

nodes.title: Starshot Lightsail Design

progress.what: Set out the materials requirements: very high reflectivity at the laser wavelength, strong thermal emission and low mass.
progress.html: Set out the materials requirements: very high reflectivity at the laser wavelength, strong thermal emission and low mass.

progress.what: Nanostructured sails that ride a laser beam stably, pushed back toward its centre when they drift or tilt.
progress.html: Nanostructured sails that ride a laser beam stably, pushed back toward its centre when they drift or tilt.

progress.what: First direct measurement of laser radiation pressure on a tethered 50 nm silicon nitride lightsail membrane.
progress.html: First direct measurement of laser radiation pressure on a tethered 50 nm silicon nitride lightsail membrane.

nodes.html: Design a sail of about a gram and a few metres across that a ground laser array of up to 100 GW can push to 15–20% of light speed without melting, tearing or sliding off the beam, as Breakthrough Starshot proposed in 2016. It is a materials, photonics and stability problem that can be posed and checked in simulation; solving it means a buildable design that meets the mass, reflectivity, cooling and beam-riding targets together.
nodes.summary: Design a sail of about a gram and a few metres across that a ground laser array of up to 100 GW can push to 15–20% of light speed without melting, tearing or sliding off the beam, as Breakthrough Starshot proposed in 2016.

nodes.title: Tensor Processing Unit
nodes.html: Google deployed its first Tensor Processing Unit in 2015 and described it publicly in 2016, an application-specific chip built around a large matrix-multiply unit for neural network inference, designed by a team led by Norman Jouppi. It ran those workloads many times more efficiently than contemporary CPUs and GPUs, and it started a wave of custom AI accelerator chips.
nodes.summary: Google deployed its first Tensor Processing Unit in 2015 and described it publicly in 2016, an application-specific chip built around a large matrix-multiply unit for neural network inference, designed by a team led by Norman Jouppi.

nodes.title: Grid-Scale Battery
nodes.html: Tesla and Neoen’s Hornsdale Power Reserve in South Australia, a 100 megawatt lithium-ion battery completed in late 2017, showed that batteries can steady a grid by responding to faults in fractions of a second. Grid-scale batteries have since multiplied around the world and help solar and wind supply evening demand.
nodes.summary: Tesla and Neoen’s Hornsdale Power Reserve in South Australia, a 100 megawatt lithium-ion battery completed in late 2017, showed that batteries can steady a grid by responding to faults in fractions of a second.

nodes.title: Wind Farm Layout Benchmark

progress.what: The first wind farm layout optimization, using a genetic algorithm.
progress.html: The first wind farm layout optimization, using a genetic algorithm.

progress.what: Results of the first Task 37 case studies: gradient-based optimization with wake expansion continuation (SNOPT+WEC) found the highest energy production.
progress.html: Results of the first Task 37 case studies: gradient-based optimization with wake expansion continuation (SNOPT+WEC) found the highest energy production.

progress.what: Eight methods on the 81-turbine Borssele case reached wake losses of 15.48 to 15.70%, against 17.28% for the starting layout; the best layout came from a new sequential allocation method.
progress.html: Eight methods on the 81-turbine Borssele case reached wake losses of 15.48 to 15.70%, against 17.28% for the starting layout; the best layout came from a new sequential allocation method.

nodes.html: Place wind turbines inside a site to maximize annual energy production when each turbine’s wake slows those downwind. IEA Wind Task 37 fixed the turbine, wake model, wind rose and boundaries in public case studies (2018): 16, 36 and 64 turbines in circular sites, and 81 turbines in the Borssele III and IV zones. Published layouts are heuristic local optima; solving a case means a layout proven optimal or a certified bound that closes the gap.
nodes.summary: Place wind turbines inside a site to maximize annual energy production when each turbine’s wake slows those downwind.

nodes.title: EUV Lithography
nodes.html: Hiroo Kinoshita proposed extreme ultraviolet projection lithography in 1986, and after three decades of work by ASML and its partners, EUV scanners that use 13.5 nanometre light from a tin plasma entered volume chip production in 2019. The machines, which cost more than 150 million dollars each, print the finest features on the most advanced processors.
nodes.summary: Hiroo Kinoshita proposed extreme ultraviolet projection lithography in 1986, and after three decades of work by ASML and its partners, EUV scanners that use 13.5 nanometre light from a tin plasma entered volume chip production in 2019.

nodes.title: Satellite Megaconstellation
nodes.html: SpaceX launched the first 60 Starlink satellites in May 2019, the start of a broadband constellation that now has thousands of low-orbit satellites, many linked by lasers. Starlink serves millions of customers, including places with no cable or fibre, and it has prompted rival constellations and concern among astronomers about satellite trails.
nodes.summary: SpaceX launched the first 60 Starlink satellites in May 2019, the start of a broadband constellation that now has thousands of low-orbit satellites, many linked by lasers.

nodes.title: Sim-to-Real Robot Learning
nodes.html: In 2019 OpenAI trained a neural network entirely in simulation, with randomized physics that grew harder as the policy improved, and it solved a Rubik’s Cube with a real robot hand. Jemin Hwangbo, Marco Hutter and colleagues had trained the ANYmal quadruped in simulation to walk and recover from falls, and sim-to-real transfer is now a standard way to train robot controllers.
nodes.summary: In 2019 OpenAI trained a neural network entirely in simulation, with randomized physics that grew harder as the policy improved, and it solved a Rubik’s Cube with a real robot hand.

nodes.title: Driverless Robotaxi
nodes.html: Waymo opened fully driverless rides to the public in the Phoenix area in October 2020, after years of testing with safety drivers. The service has since grown to many US cities and by mid-2026 was giving about 500,000 paid rides a week, the first driverless taxi service at commercial scale.
nodes.summary: Waymo opened fully driverless rides to the public in the Phoenix area in October 2020, after years of testing with safety drivers.

nodes.title: 20-Tesla HTS Fusion Magnet
by: MIT Plasma Science and Fusion Center
nodes.html: In September 2021 Commonwealth Fusion Systems and the MIT Plasma Science and Fusion Center tested a large toroidal-field model coil wound from high-temperature superconducting tape that reached 20 tesla. Stronger magnets allow a tokamak of a given power to be much smaller, which is the basis of the compact SPARC design.
nodes.summary: In September 2021 Commonwealth Fusion Systems and the MIT Plasma Science and Fusion Center tested a large toroidal-field model coil wound from high-temperature superconducting tape that reached 20 tesla.

nodes.title: Mars Helicopter
nodes.html: NASA’s Ingenuity, a 1.8 kilogram helicopter carried to Mars by the Perseverance rover and led at JPL by MiMi Aung, made the first powered, controlled flight on another planet on 19 April 2021, in air about one percent as dense as Earth’s. It flew 72 times before it was damaged in January 2024, and showed that aircraft can scout Mars.
nodes.summary: NASA’s Ingenuity, a 1.8 kilogram helicopter carried to Mars by the Perseverance rover and led at JPL by MiMi Aung, made the first powered, controlled flight on another planet on 19 April 2021, in air about one percent as dense as Earth’s.

nodes.title: Asteroid Deflection
nodes.html: NASA’s DART spacecraft struck the asteroid Dimorphos at about 6 kilometres a second on 26 September 2022 and shortened its orbit around Didymos by more than half an hour, the first measured change to the motion of a celestial body by a human-made object. The test showed that a kinetic impactor can deflect an asteroid, a method of planetary defence.
nodes.summary: NASA’s DART spacecraft struck the asteroid Dimorphos at about 6 kilometres a second on 26 September 2022 and shortened its orbit around Didymos by more than half an hour, the first measured change to the motion of a celestial body by a human-made object.

nodes.title: Autonomous Robotic Surgery
nodes.html: Axel Krieger’s group at Johns Hopkins reported in 2022 that its Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot sewed together two ends of pig intestine inside live animals with no human guiding the needle, using 3D imaging and planning software. In 2025 its SRT-H system, trained on surgeons’ demonstrations, autonomously performed key steps of gallbladder removal on pig tissue outside the body.
nodes.summary: Axel Krieger’s group at Johns Hopkins reported in 2022 that its Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot sewed together two ends of pig intestine inside live animals with no human guiding the needle, using 3D imaging and planning software.

nodes.title: BEHAVIOR Household Benchmark

progress.what: With colleagues, released BEHAVIOR: 100 household activities specified in a predicate logic, with human VR demonstrations as a baseline.
progress.html: With colleagues, released BEHAVIOR: 100 household activities specified in a predicate logic, with human VR demonstrations as a baseline.

progress.what: With colleagues, released BEHAVIOR-1K: 1,000 activities in 50 scenes, simulated in OmniGibson.
progress.html: With colleagues, released BEHAVIOR-1K: 1,000 activities in 50 scenes, simulated in OmniGibson.

progress.what: Won the first BEHAVIOR Challenge: 12.4% full-task success and a partial-credit score of 0.26 on the held-out test set.
progress.html: Won the first BEHAVIOR Challenge: 12.4% full-task success and a partial-credit score of 0.26 on the held-out test set.

nodes.html: Make a robot policy complete long everyday household activities, from cooking to cleaning, in the BEHAVIOR-1K simulator (Stanford, 2022). The 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge at CoRL scores 100 full-length tasks in 7 scenes by average success with partial credit; in the first round (NeurIPS 2025, 50 tasks) the winning team fully completed 12.4% of held-out test episodes. Solving it means near-complete success on the full benchmark.
nodes.summary: Make a robot policy complete long everyday household activities, from cooking to cleaning, in the BEHAVIOR-1K simulator (Stanford, 2022).

nodes.title: Fusion Ignition
nodes.html: On 5 December 2022 the National Ignition Facility released 3.15 MJ of fusion energy from 2.05 MJ of laser light: scientific breakeven, though far from wall-plug breakeven.
nodes.summary: On 5 December 2022 the National Ignition Facility released 3.15 MJ of fusion energy from 2.05 MJ of laser light: scientific breakeven, though far from wall-plug breakeven.

nodes.title: AI Plasma Control
nodes.html: Jonas Degrave, Federico Felici and colleagues at Google DeepMind and EPFL’s Swiss Plasma Center trained a deep reinforcement learning controller in simulation that shaped the plasma in the TCV tokamak, reported in Nature in February 2022. In 2024 a reinforcement learning controller predicted and avoided tearing instabilities in plasmas at the DIII-D tokamak.
nodes.summary: Jonas Degrave, Federico Felici and colleagues at Google DeepMind and EPFL’s Swiss Plasma Center trained a deep reinforcement learning controller in simulation that shaped the plasma in the TCV tokamak, reported in Nature in February 2022.

nodes.title: CARLA Leaderboard 2.0

progress.what: CARLA, an open-source urban driving simulator.
progress.html: CARLA, an open-source urban driving simulator.

progress.what: CarLLaVA, a camera-only vision-language driving model, won the sensor track of the 2024 CARLA challenge.
progress.html: CarLLaVA, a camera-only vision-language driving model, won the sensor track of the 2024 CARLA challenge.

progress.what: Leaderboard 2.1 made the infraction penalty linear, ending an exploit in which agents scored higher by stopping partway along a route.
progress.html: Leaderboard 2.1 made the infraction penalty linear, ending an exploit in which agents scored higher by stopping partway along a route.

nodes.html: Drive long routes through dense simulated traffic and dozens of pre-crash scenarios in the CARLA simulator, scored by driving score = route completion × infraction penalty (Leaderboard 2.0, 2023). When the 2.0 results were frozen, the best scores were 6.9 out of 100 with sensors only (CarLLaVA, 2024) and 12.5 with an HD map. Solving it means driving scores near 100 on the official routes, now under the Leaderboard 2.1 rules (2025).
nodes.summary: Drive long routes through dense simulated traffic and dozens of pre-crash scenarios in the CARLA simulator, scored by driving score = route completion × infraction penalty (Leaderboard 2.0, 2023).

nodes.title: Champion-Level Drone Racing
nodes.html: Swift, an autonomous racing drone built by Elia Kaufmann, Davide Scaramuzza and colleagues at the University of Zurich, won races against three world-champion human pilots and recorded the fastest lap, as reported in Nature in August 2023. It flew from its own onboard camera images with a control policy trained by reinforcement learning in simulation.
nodes.summary: Swift, an autonomous racing drone built by Elia Kaufmann, Davide Scaramuzza and colleagues at the University of Zurich, won races against three world-champion human pilots and recorded the fastest lap, as reported in Nature in August 2023.

nodes.title: Enhanced Geothermal
nodes.html: Fervo Energy’s Project Red in Nevada, tested in 2023, generated 3.5 megawatts from hot rock with no natural flow, using horizontal wells drilled with oil-field techniques and fractures created between them. Enhanced geothermal systems could extend geothermal power beyond volcanic regions.
nodes.summary: Fervo Energy’s Project Red in Nevada, tested in 2023, generated 3.5 megawatts from hot rock with no natural flow, using horizontal wells drilled with oil-field techniques and fractures created between them.

nodes.title: Lifelong Path Planning for 10,000 Robots

progress.what: Rolling-horizon collision resolution scales lifelong planning to 1,000 robots on simulated warehouse maps.
progress.html: Rolling-horizon collision resolution scales lifelong planning to 1,000 robots on simulated warehouse maps.

progress.what: The winners of the 2023 League of Robot Runners set out the open challenges: 10,000 agents at about one second per step, congestion, and realistic robot models.
progress.html: The winners of the 2023 League of Robot Runners set out the open challenges: 10,000 agents at about one second per step, congestion, and realistic robot models.

nodes.html: Keep up to 10,000 warehouse robots moving to a stream of new goals without collisions or gridlock, planning each step within about a second. The League of Robot Runners competition (since 2023) publishes maps, instances and best-known throughputs, and its 2023 champions list scale and congestion as unsolved. Solving it means planners that beat the archived best throughputs at 10,000 robots within the time limit.
nodes.summary: Keep up to 10,000 warehouse robots moving to a stream of new goals without collisions or gridlock, planning each step within about a second.

nodes.title: Pebble-Bed Reactor
nodes.html: China’s HTR-PM at Shidaowan in Shandong, built by Tsinghua University, China Huaneng and others, began commercial operation in December 2023 and is described as the first Generation IV reactor in commercial service. Its fuel is tennis-ball-sized graphite pebbles holding thousands of ceramic-coated uranium particles, and its design lets decay heat leave passively after a loss of cooling.
nodes.summary: China’s HTR-PM at Shidaowan in Shandong, built by Tsinghua University, China Huaneng and others, began commercial operation in December 2023 and is described as the first Generation IV reactor in commercial service.

nodes.title: Speech Neuroprosthesis
nodes.html: Two papers in Nature in August 2023 showed implants decoding attempted speech from paralysed people at 62 words a minute, by Francis Willett, Jaimie Henderson and colleagues at Stanford, and 78 words a minute with a digital avatar, by Edward Chang’s team at UCSF. In 2024 a UC Davis team including Sergey Stavisky and David Brandman reached 97.5 percent accuracy with a man with ALS.
nodes.summary: Two papers in Nature in August 2023 showed implants decoding attempted speech from paralysed people at 62 words a minute, by Francis Willett, Jaimie Henderson and colleagues at Stanford, and 78 words a minute with a digital avatar, by Edward Chang’s team at UCSF.

nodes.title: Vision-Language-Action Models
nodes.html: Google DeepMind’s RT-2, announced in July 2023, fine-tuned a vision-language model to output robot actions as text tokens, so a robot could follow instructions involving objects and concepts from web data. Physical Intelligence’s π0 (2024) and Google DeepMind’s Gemini Robotics (2025) extended the approach to policies that work across many tasks and robot bodies.
