Metallic glasses are strong and elastic and make good transformer cores; bulk metallic glasses from slower-cooling alloys appeared in the 1990s.
nodes.summary: Pol Duwez’s group at Caltech cooled a gold-silicon melt at about a million degrees per second in 1960 and froze it into a disordered, glass-like metal.

nodes.title: Structure of the Hydrated Electron

progress.what: Simulations with a new electron–water pseudopotential gave an electron that encompasses water molecules without a cavity, challenging the consensus picture.
progress.html: Simulations with a new electron–water pseudopotential gave an electron that encompasses water molecules without a cavity, challenging the consensus picture.

progress.what: A machine-learned potential reproduced a stable cavity structure and the electron’s localization dynamics without treating the electron explicitly.
progress.html: A machine-learned potential reproduced a stable cavity structure and the electron’s localization dynamics without treating the electron explicitly.

progress.what: Fast, DFT-accurate Deep Potential molecular dynamics of the hydrated electron again supported the cavity model.
progress.html: Fast, DFT-accurate Deep Potential molecular dynamics of the hydrated electron again supported the cavity model.

nodes.html: Does an extra electron in liquid water sit in a cavity it carves out, or spread over the surrounding water molecules? The hydrated electron, identified by its absorption spectrum by Hart and Boag in 1962, drives radiation chemistry, and simulations have supported both pictures. A solution is one first-principles model that reproduces its measured optical, vibrational and thermodynamic properties together and rules out the alternative.
nodes.summary: Does an extra electron in liquid water sit in a cavity it carves out, or spread over the surrounding water molecules?

nodes.title: Noble Gas Compounds
nodes.html: Neil Bartlett found in 1962 that platinum hexafluoride oxidises xenon to an orange-yellow solid that he formulated as xenon hexafluoroplatinate, overturning the belief that the noble gases are chemically inert. Xenon fluorides were made within months, and the discovery reshaped textbooks and ideas about bonding.
nodes.summary: Neil Bartlett found in 1962 that platinum hexafluoride oxidises xenon to an orange-yellow solid that he formulated as xenon hexafluoroplatinate, overturning the belief that the noble gases are chemically inert.

nodes.title: Shape-Memory Alloys
nodes.html: William Buehler and colleagues at the US Naval Ordnance Laboratory found between 1959 and 1962 that an alloy of nickel and titanium, named Nitinol, returns to a remembered shape when warmed, through a reversible martensitic transformation. Nitinol is used in vascular stents, orthodontic wires and actuators.
nodes.summary: William Buehler and colleagues at the US Naval Ordnance Laboratory found between 1959 and 1962 that an alloy of nickel and titanium, named Nitinol, returns to a remembered shape when warmed, through a reversible martensitic transformation.

nodes.title: Stable Helium Compound at 1 atm

progress.what: Compressed arsenolite took up helium to form the clathrate As4O6·2He, which exists above about 3 GPa.
progress.html: Compressed arsenolite took up helium to form the clathrate As4O6·2He, which exists above about 3 GPa.

progress.what: Predicted by evolutionary structure search and then made in a diamond anvil cell: Na2He, an electride stable above 113 GPa.
progress.html: Predicted by evolutionary structure search and then made in a diamond anvil cell: Na2He, an electride stable above 113 GPa.

progress.what: Detected the helium hydride ion HeH+ in the planetary nebula NGC 7027; as a charged species it does not settle the question.
progress.html: Detected the helium hydride ion HeH+ in the planetary nebula NGC 7027; as a charged species it does not settle the question.

progress.what: Static DFT structure searches placed a weakly bound van der Waals compound, HeN4, on the convex hull from 0 to 68 GPa; it has not been made.
progress.html: Static DFT structure searches placed a weakly bound van der Waals compound, HeN4, on the convex hull from 0 to 68 GPa; it has not been made.

nodes.html: Find a neutral compound of helium that is thermodynamically stable at ordinary pressure, a goal since the first noble-gas compound was made in 1962. Na2He, made in a diamond anvil cell in 2017, is stable only above 113 GPa, and a 2021 calculation put a van der Waals solid, HeN4, on the convex hull at 0 GPa, though it has not been made. A solution is a compound predicted to be stable at 1 atm and room temperature and then synthesized.
nodes.summary: Find a neutral compound of helium that is thermodynamically stable at ordinary pressure, a goal since the first noble-gas compound was made in 1962.

nodes.title: Carbon Fibre
nodes.html: Akio Shindo in Japan (1961) and William Watt, Leslie Phillips and William Johnson at the Royal Aircraft Establishment (1963) made strong, stiff carbon fibres by heating polyacrylonitrile fibres under tension. Carbon-fibre composites are light and strong enough for airliners, racing cars, wind turbine blades and sports equipment.
nodes.summary: Akio Shindo in Japan (1961) and William Watt, Leslie Phillips and William Johnson at the Royal Aircraft Establishment (1963) made strong, stiff carbon fibres by heating polyacrylonitrile fibres under tension.

nodes.title: Solid-Phase Synthesis
nodes.html: Bruce Merrifield attached the first amino acid of a peptide to insoluble polymer beads in 1963 and added further residues one at a time, washing away excess reagents after each step. Solid-phase synthesis made peptides, and later DNA and RNA, quick to make and automatable, and won him the 1984 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
nodes.summary: Bruce Merrifield attached the first amino acid of a peptide to insoluble polymer beads in 1963 and added further residues one at a time, washing away excess reagents after each step.

nodes.title: Density Functional Theory
nodes.html: Pierre Hohenberg and Walter Kohn proved in 1964 that the ground-state energy of a many-electron system is determined by its electron density, and Kohn and Lu Jeu Sham made this practical in 1965. Density functional theory is now the most widely used method for calculating the properties of molecules and materials, and brought Kohn the 1998 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
nodes.summary: Pierre Hohenberg and Walter Kohn proved in 1964 that the ground-state energy of a many-electron system is determined by its electron density, and Kohn and Lu Jeu Sham made this practical in 1965.

nodes.title: QSAR
nodes.html: Corwin Hansch and Toshio Fujita showed in 1964 that the biological activity of related compounds can be fitted to their lipophilicity and to electronic substituent constants. This founded quantitative structure-activity relationships (QSAR), which predict the properties of untested molecules and are forerunners of today’s machine-learning property models.
nodes.summary: Corwin Hansch and Toshio Fujita showed in 1964 that the biological activity of related compounds can be fitted to their lipophilicity and to electronic substituent constants.

nodes.title: Crystal Structure Databases
nodes.html: Olga Kennard founded the Cambridge Structural Database in 1965 to collect all published crystal structures of organic and metal-organic compounds; it now holds more than a million. With the Inorganic Crystal Structure Database and the Protein Data Bank, such archives became the data on which modern computational chemistry and materials machine learning rely.
nodes.summary: Olga Kennard founded the Cambridge Structural Database in 1965 to collect all published crystal structures of organic and metal-organic compounds; it now holds more than a million.

nodes.title: Aramid Fibre (Kevlar)
nodes.html: Stephanie Kwolek at DuPont noticed in 1965 that a cloudy, thin solution of an aromatic polyamide was liquid-crystalline, and spun it into fibres about five times stronger than steel by weight. Sold as Kevlar from 1971, the fibre is used in body armour, tyres, ropes and aircraft parts.
nodes.summary: Stephanie Kwolek at DuPont noticed in 1965 that a cloudy, thin solution of an aromatic polyamide was liquid-crystalline, and spun it into fibres about five times stronger than steel by weight.

nodes.title: Woodward–Hoffmann Rules
nodes.html: Robert Woodward and Roald Hoffmann showed in 1965 that the symmetry of molecular orbitals decides whether concerted reactions such as electrocyclic ring closures and cycloadditions occur, and with what stereochemistry. With Kenichi Fukui’s frontier orbital theory (1952), the rules won Hoffmann and Fukui the 1981 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
nodes.summary: Robert Woodward and Roald Hoffmann showed in 1965 that the symmetry of molecular orbitals decides whether concerted reactions such as electrocyclic ring closures and cycloadditions occur, and with what stereochemistry.

nodes.title: Coupled-Cluster Theory
nodes.html: Jiří Čížek adapted the exponential cluster expansion from nuclear physics to molecular electrons in 1966. After Rodney Bartlett and others made it practical in the 1970s and 1980s, coupled cluster with single, double and perturbative triple excitations, CCSD(T) (1989), became the gold standard for accurate small-molecule energies.
nodes.summary: Jiří Čížek adapted the exponential cluster expansion from nuclear physics to molecular electrons in 1966.

nodes.title: Retrosynthetic Analysis
nodes.html: E. J. Corey formalised in 1967 the planning of an organic synthesis by working backwards from the target molecule, cutting it at strategic bonds into simpler pieces. His LHASA program (1969) was an early computer synthesis planner, and retrosynthetic analysis is how chemists teach and design syntheses; Corey won the 1990 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
nodes.summary: E.

nodes.title: Supramolecular Chemistry
nodes.html: Charles Pedersen’s accidental synthesis of crown ethers in 1967, which wrap around metal ions, was followed by Jean-Marie Lehn’s cryptands and Donald Cram’s host-guest molecules. The three shared the 1987 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for founding what Lehn called chemistry beyond the molecule, the study of molecular recognition and self-assembly.
nodes.summary: Charles Pedersen’s accidental synthesis of crown ethers in 1967, which wrap around metal ions, was followed by Jean-Marie Lehn’s cryptands and Donald Cram’s host-guest molecules.

nodes.title: Asymmetric Catalysis
nodes.html: William Knowles used a chiral rhodium phosphine catalyst in 1968 to hydrogenate an alkene so that one mirror-image form was favoured, and Monsanto made L-DOPA for Parkinson’s disease this way in 1974. Noyori’s BINAP catalysts and Sharpless’s asymmetric epoxidation (both 1980) followed, and the three shared the 2001 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
nodes.summary: William Knowles used a chiral rhodium phosphine catalyst in 1968 to hydrogenate an alkene so that one mirror-image form was favoured, and Monsanto made L-DOPA for Parkinson’s disease this way in 1974.

nodes.title: Molecular Mechanics Force Fields
nodes.html: Shneior Lifson and Arieh Warshel treated molecules as balls and springs with fitted parameters in their consistent force field (1968), and Norman Allinger’s MM2 (1977) refined it for organic chemistry. Force fields make it cheap enough to simulate proteins, polymers and drug binding with molecular dynamics.
nodes.summary: Shneior Lifson and Arieh Warshel treated molecules as balls and springs with fitted parameters in their consistent force field (1968), and Norman Allinger’s MM2 (1977) refined it for organic chemistry.

nodes.title: Deriving the Madelung Rule

progress.what: Reviewed Allen and Knight’s 2002 response to Löwdin’s challenge and judged that it does not explain the rule.
progress.html: Reviewed Allen and Knight’s 2002 response to Löwdin’s challenge and judged that it does not explain the rule.

progress.what: Argued that a neutral atom in the mean-field approximation has an O(4) symmetry that explains the n + ℓ, n rule.
progress.html: Argued that a neutral atom in the mean-field approximation has an O(4) symmetry that explains the n + ℓ, n rule.

progress.what: Claimed an analytical solution of Löwdin’s challenge from Tietz-type equations in Bertrand spacetimes, while conceding that it does not yet describe the exceptions among transition metals, lanthanides and actinides.
progress.html: Claimed an analytical solution of Löwdin’s challenge from Tietz-type equations in Bertrand spacetimes, while conceding that it does not yet describe the exceptions among transition metals, lanthanides and actinides.

nodes.html: Why do electrons fill atomic subshells in order of increasing n + ℓ, and for equal n + ℓ in order of increasing n, with exceptions such as chromium and copper? Löwdin challenged theorists in 1969 to derive this Madelung rule from quantum mechanics, and the proposed derivations remain contested. A solution derives the rule from the many-electron Schrödinger equation, or a controlled approximation to it, and predicts where it fails.
nodes.summary: Why do electrons fill atomic subshells in order of increasing n + ℓ, and for equal n + ℓ in order of increasing n, with exceptions such as chromium and copper?

nodes.title: Ab Initio Program Packages
nodes.html: John Pople’s group released Gaussian 70 in 1970, a program that packaged ab initio quantum chemistry with standard basis sets so that any chemist could compute molecular energies and structures. Systematic model chemistries and later versions made computation a routine partner to experiment; Pople shared the 1998 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
nodes.summary: John Pople’s group released Gaussian 70 in 1970, a program that packaged ab initio quantum chemistry with standard basis sets so that any chemist could compute molecular energies and structures.

nodes.title: Photoelectrochemical Water Splitting
nodes.html: Akira Fujishima and Kenichi Honda showed in 1972 that a titanium dioxide electrode under ultraviolet light splits water into hydrogen and oxygen. The Honda-Fujishima effect started research into solar fuels, photoelectrochemistry and photocatalysts, including self-cleaning titanium dioxide coatings.
nodes.summary: Akira Fujishima and Kenichi Honda showed in 1972 that a titanium dioxide electrode under ultraviolet light splits water into hydrogen and oxygen.

nodes.title: Vitamin B12 Total Synthesis
nodes.html: Robert Woodward at Harvard and Albert Eschenmoser at ETH Zürich, leading about a hundred co-workers over more than a decade, completed the total synthesis of vitamin B12 in 1972, one of the most complex natural products ever made. Puzzles met along the way led Woodward and Roald Hoffmann to the orbital symmetry rules.
nodes.summary: Robert Woodward at Harvard and Albert Eschenmoser at ETH Zürich, leading about a hundred co-workers over more than a decade, completed the total synthesis of vitamin B12 in 1972, one of the most complex natural products ever made.

nodes.title: Atomic Layer Deposition
nodes.html: Tuomo Suntola developed atomic layer epitaxy in 1974, building films one atomic layer at a time from alternating self-limiting surface reactions; Soviet chemists around Valentin Aleskovskii had worked on similar molecular layering since the 1960s. Atomic layer deposition makes the hafnium oxide gate insulators in chips from 2007 and is used in displays and batteries.
nodes.summary: Tuomo Suntola developed atomic layer epitaxy in 1974, building films one atomic layer at a time from alternating self-limiting surface reactions; Soviet chemists around Valentin Aleskovskii had worked on similar molecular layering since the 1960s.

nodes.title: Ozone-Depletion Chemistry
nodes.html: Mario Molina and Sherwood Rowland showed in 1974 that chlorine released from CFCs in the stratosphere destroys ozone in a catalytic chain, after Paul Crutzen’s work on nitrogen oxides (1970). The Antarctic ozone hole (1985) confirmed the threat and led to the Montreal Protocol (1987); the three shared the 1995 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
nodes.summary: Mario Molina and Sherwood Rowland showed in 1974 that chlorine released from CFCs in the stratosphere destroys ozone in a catalytic chain, after Paul Crutzen’s work on nitrogen oxides (1970).

nodes.title: Chemistry of Superheavy Elements
aliases: relativistic effects in the periodic table

progress.what: First chemistry of copernicium, element 112: single atoms behaved as a volatile metal on a gold surface.
progress.html: First chemistry of copernicium, element 112: single atoms behaved as a volatile metal on a gold surface.

progress.what: Showed that flerovium, element 114, is highly volatile and the least reactive member of group 14, binding to gold more weakly than mercury but more strongly than a noble gas.
progress.html: Showed that flerovium, element 114, is highly volatile and the least reactive member of group 14, binding to gold more weakly than mercury but more strongly than a noble gas.

progress.what: First chemistry of moscovium (115) and of nihonium (113) on quartz: adsorption enthalpies agree with relativistic calculations, and both are more reactive than flerovium but less than their lighter homologues.
progress.html: First chemistry of moscovium (115) and of nihonium (113) on quartz: adsorption enthalpies agree with relativistic calculations, and both are more reactive than flerovium but less than their lighter homologues.

nodes.html: How do the heaviest elements, 112 to 118, bond when relativistic effects reshape their electron shells? Pitzer asked in 1975 whether elements 112, 114 and 118 would be nearly inert gases, and single-atom experiments since 2007 find copernicium and flerovium volatile but metallic. A solution is relativistic quantum chemistry whose predictions for all of 112–118, including elements not yet studied chemically, match such experiments.
nodes.summary: How do the heaviest elements, 112 to 118, bond when relativistic effects reshape their electron shells?

nodes.title: QM/MM Simulation
nodes.html: Arieh Warshel and Michael Levitt combined quantum mechanics for the reacting atoms with classical mechanics for the surrounding protein in their 1976 study of the enzyme lysozyme. QM/MM methods made enzyme reactions computable, and Warshel, Levitt and Martin Karplus won the 2013 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for multiscale models.
nodes.summary: Arieh Warshel and Michael Levitt combined quantum mechanics for the reacting atoms with classical mechanics for the surrounding protein in their 1976 study of the enzyme lysozyme.

nodes.title: Conducting Polymers
nodes.html: Alan Heeger, Alan MacDiarmid and Hideki Shirakawa found in 1977 that polyacetylene doped with iodine conducts electricity almost like a metal. Conducting polymers opened organic electronics, with uses in antistatic coatings, organic light-emitting diodes and flexible devices, and the three shared the 2000 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
nodes.summary: Alan Heeger, Alan MacDiarmid and Hideki Shirakawa found in 1977 that polyacetylene doped with iodine conducts electricity almost like a metal.

nodes.title: Room-Temperature Polymer Electrolyte

progress.what: Reported complexes of poly(ethylene oxide) with alkali-metal salts, later shown to conduct ions, the starting point of solid polymer electrolytes.
progress.html: Reported complexes of poly(ethylene oxide) with alkali-metal salts, later shown to conduct ions, the starting point of solid polymer electrolytes.

progress.what: A graph neural network trained mostly on short, noisy molecular-dynamics runs screened 6,247 polymers as electrolytes and released an open dataset.
progress.html: A graph neural network trained mostly on short, noisy molecular-dynamics runs screened 6,247 polymers as electrolytes and released an open dataset.

progress.what: Reported a solvent-free electrolyte of PMMA-grafted natural rubber and LiTFSI with 2.7 mS/cm at 30 °C, attributed to an ionic cluster network.
progress.html: Reported a solvent-free electrolyte of PMMA-grafted natural rubber and LiTFSI with 2.7 mS/cm at 30 °C, attributed to an ionic cluster network.

progress.what: A PEO–PVDF–LiTFSI film made without solvent, using succinonitrile as a solid plasticizer, reached 1.04 mS/cm at 30 °C and kept 84% capacity over 300 cycles in LiFePO4 cells.
progress.html: A PEO–PVDF–LiTFSI film made without solvent, using succinonitrile as a solid plasticizer, reached 1.04 mS/cm at 30 °C and kept 84% capacity over 300 cycles in LiFePO4 cells.

nodes.html: Find a dry polymer electrolyte that conducts lithium ions at above 1 mS/cm at 25 °C and is stable against lithium metal. Poly(ethylene oxide)–salt electrolytes, proposed for batteries by Michel Armand in 1978, reach about 0.01 mS/cm at room temperature, and reports since 2022 of 1–3 mS/cm near 30 °C rely on high salt contents or plasticizers. A solution is a plasticizer-free polymer meeting the target in independent tests and long cycling.
nodes.summary: Find a dry polymer electrolyte that conducts lithium ions at above 1 mS/cm at 25 °C and is stable against lithium metal.

nodes.title: Palladium Cross-Coupling
nodes.html: Palladium catalysts join two carbon fragments into a new carbon-carbon bond: Richard Heck’s alkene coupling (1968 to 1972), Ei-ichi Negishi’s organozinc coupling (1977) and Akira Suzuki’s organoboron coupling (1979). The reactions are among the most used in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, and the three won the 2010 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
nodes.summary: Palladium catalysts join two carbon fragments into a new carbon-carbon bond: Richard Heck’s alkene coupling (1968 to 1972), Ei-ichi Negishi’s organozinc coupling (1977) and Akira Suzuki’s organoboron coupling (1979).

nodes.title: Relativistic Quantum Chemistry
nodes.html: Pekka Pyykkö and Jean-Paul Desclaux showed in 1979 that relativity shrinks the s orbitals of heavy atoms, which explains why gold is yellow and mercury is liquid. Relativistic effects were later shown to supply most of the voltage of a lead-acid battery (2011), and quantum chemists must include them for heavy elements.
nodes.summary: Pekka Pyykkö and Jean-Paul Desclaux showed in 1979 that relativity shrinks the s orbitals of heavy atoms, which explains why gold is yellow and mercury is liquid.

nodes.title: Solid–Electrolyte Interphase
nodes.html: Emanuel Peled proposed in 1979 that lithium and other alkali metals survive in organic electrolytes because a thin film forms on their surface, the solid electrolyte interphase, which passes ions but blocks electrons. The interphase decides the life, safety and fast charging of lithium-ion cells, and engineering it remains central to battery research.
nodes.summary: Emanuel Peled proposed in 1979 that lithium and other alkali metals survive in organic electrolytes because a thin film forms on their surface, the solid electrolyte interphase, which passes ions but blocks electrons.

nodes.title: Optimal Lieb–Oxford Constant

progress.what: Lowered the upper bound on the constant from Lieb and Oxford’s 1.68 to 1.6358.
progress.html: Lowered the upper bound on the constant from Lieb and Oxford’s 1.68 to 1.6358.

progress.what: Proved that jellium and the uniform electron gas have the same next-order energy, which together with the body-centred-cubic Wigner crystal gives the lower bound C ≥ 1.4442.
progress.html: Proved that jellium and the uniform electron gas have the same next-order energy, which together with the body-centred-cubic Wigner crystal gives the lower bound C ≥ 1.4442.

progress.what: Improved the upper bound to 1.58 and proved that the constant can be lowered to 1.25 for Hartree–Fock states.
progress.html: Improved the upper bound to 1.58 and proved that the constant can be lowered to 1.25 for Hartree–Fock states.

nodes.html: What is the smallest constant C for which the indirect Coulomb energy of every N-electron state is at least −C times the integral of the density to the power 4/3? Lieb and Oxford proved C ≤ 1.68 in 1981, and the bound is used to constrain density functionals such as PBE. Since 2022 it is known that 1.4442 ≤ C ≤ 1.58; a solution is the exact value, for instance a proof that the Wigner-crystal value 1.4442 is optimal.
nodes.summary: What is the smallest constant C for which the indirect Coulomb energy of every N-electron state is at least −C times the integral of the density to the power 4/3?

nodes.title: Quantum Dots
nodes.html: Alexei Ekimov saw in 1981 that tiny semiconductor crystals in glass change colour with their size, and Louis Brus found the same in solution in 1983. Moungi Bawendi’s hot-injection synthesis (1993) gave uniform nanocrystals, now used in displays and bioimaging, and the three received the 2023 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
nodes.summary: Alexei Ekimov saw in 1981 that tiny semiconductor crystals in glass change colour with their size, and Louis Brus found the same in solution in 1983.

nodes.title: C–H Activation
nodes.html: Robert Bergman and William Graham independently showed in 1982 that iridium complexes break the strong carbon-hydrogen bonds of alkanes, following Alexander Shilov’s platinum chemistry of 1969 to 1972. Turning C-H bonds into functional groups is now a core strategy of synthesis and an aim of fuel and chemical processing.
nodes.summary: Robert Bergman and William Graham independently showed in 1982 that iridium complexes break the strong carbon-hydrogen bonds of alkanes, following Alexander Shilov’s platinum chemistry of 1969 to 1972.

nodes.title: Chemically Amplified Photoresists
nodes.html: At IBM in 1982, Hiroshi Ito and Grant Willson, with Jean Fréchet, devised photoresists in which one acid molecule released by light triggers hundreds of chemical reactions in a polymer film. These chemically amplified resists made deep-ultraviolet lithography practical and became the standard for patterning chips.
nodes.summary: At IBM in 1982, Hiroshi Ito and Grant Willson, with Jean Fréchet, devised photoresists in which one acid molecule released by light triggers hundreds of chemical reactions in a polymer film.

nodes.title: H₃⁺ Near-Dissociation Spectrum

progress.what: Measured transitions of rotationally cold H3+ up to the mid-visible and matched them with first-principles calculations.
progress.html: Measured transitions of rotationally cold H3+ up to the mid-visible and matched them with first-principles calculations.

progress.what: A review found that levels below about 20,000 cm−1, halfway to dissociation, are now computed routinely, while the near-dissociation spectrum remains unassigned and non-adiabatic effects are the hardest remaining piece.
progress.html: A review found that levels below about 20,000 cm−1, halfway to dissociation, are now computed routinely, while the near-dissociation spectrum remains unassigned and non-adiabatic effects are the hardest remaining piece.

nodes.html: Close to its dissociation limit, H3+, the simplest polyatomic molecule, with two electrons, shows a rich infrared spectrum that Carrington, Buttenshaw and Kennedy discovered in 1982 and mapped over the following decade; it remains unassigned. A solution is a first-principles calculation, including non-adiabatic effects and states just above dissociation, that reproduces and assigns the observed lines.
nodes.summary: Close to its dissociation limit, H3+, the simplest polyatomic molecule, with two electrons, shows a rich infrared spectrum that Carrington, Buttenshaw and Kennedy discovered in 1982 and mapped over the following decade; it remains unassigned.

nodes.title: Molecular Docking
nodes.html: Irwin Kuntz’s DOCK program (1982) fitted small molecules into the pockets of protein structures by computer, scoring the fit by shape. It started structure-based virtual screening, and docking programs are now widely used in drug discovery.
nodes.summary: Irwin Kuntz’s DOCK program (1982) fitted small molecules into the pockets of protein structures by computer, scoring the fit by shape.

nodes.title: Quasicrystals
nodes.html: Dan Shechtman saw ten-fold symmetry in the electron diffraction of a rapidly cooled aluminium-manganese alloy in 1982 and published it in 1984. The pattern was ordered but not periodic, which forced crystallographers to redefine what a crystal is; he won the 2011 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
nodes.summary: Dan Shechtman saw ten-fold symmetry in the electron diffraction of a rapidly cooled aluminium-manganese alloy in 1982 and published it in 1984.

nodes.title: v-Representability Problem

progress.what: Gave explicit examples of physically reasonable densities that are not the ground-state density of any potential, even when ensembles are allowed.
progress.html: Gave explicit examples of physically reasonable densities that are not the ground-state density of any potential, even when ensembles are allowed.

progress.what: Proved that on a lattice every strictly positive density compatible with the Pauli principle is ensemble v-representable.
progress.html: Proved that on a lattice every strictly positive density compatible with the Pauli principle is ensemble v-representable.

progress.what: Solved the problem on a one-dimensional ring: every square-integrable density with a square-integrable derivative that stays away from zero is v-representable, with or without interactions, once distributional potentials are allowed.
progress.html: Solved the problem on a one-dimensional ring: every square-integrable density with a square-integrable derivative that stays away from zero is v-representable, with or without interactions, once distributional potentials are allowed.

progress.what: Extended the ring result to particles at finite temperature and showed that the characterized set of densities is maximal.
progress.html: Extended the ring result to particles at finite temperature and showed that the characterized set of densities is maximal.

progress.what: Claimed a three-electron molecule whose ground-state density has no noninteracting ensemble representation by any potential in L^(3/2) + L^∞, a counterexample to Kohn–Sham ensemble representability for that class (family 278 of OpenAI’s math release, not formalized). Not yet independently reviewed.
progress.html: Claimed a three-electron molecule whose ground-state density has no noninteracting ensemble representation by any potential in L^(3/2) + L^∞, a counterexample to Kohn–Sham ensemble representability for that class (family 278 of OpenAI’s math release, not formalized). Not yet independently reviewed.

nodes.html: Which electron densities are the ground-state density of some external potential? Levy (1982) and Lieb (1983) found densities that come from no pure ground state, a gap in the foundations of the Hohenberg–Kohn theorem and the Kohn–Sham method of density functional theory. A solution characterizes the v-representable densities for interacting electrons in three dimensions, or proves that Kohn–Sham theory is well defined there.
nodes.summary: Which electron densities are the ground-state density of some external potential?

nodes.title: Ozone Isotope Anomaly

progress.what: Proposed an intramolecular theory in which asymmetric ozone isotopologues have more reactive quantum states than symmetric ones, the η effect.
progress.html: Proposed an intramolecular theory in which asymmetric ozone isotopologues have more reactive quantum states than symmetric ones, the η effect.

progress.what: An RRKM-based theory combining symmetry restrictions with zero-point-energy differences reproduced a wide range of ozone isotope data, with the η factor fitted to experiment.
progress.html: An RRKM-based theory combining symmetry restrictions with zero-point-energy differences reproduced a wide range of ozone isotope data, with the η factor fitted to experiment.

progress.what: Mixed quantum–classical dynamics in a reduced-dimension model traced the effect to scattering resonances and reached semiquantitative agreement with experiment.
progress.html: Mixed quantum–classical dynamics in a reduced-dimension model traced the effect to scattering resonances and reached semiquantitative agreement with experiment.

nodes.html: When ozone forms from oxygen atoms and molecules, it becomes enriched in oxygen-17 and oxygen-18 by nearly equal amounts, although ordinary isotope effects scale with mass, as Thiemens and Heidenreich found in 1983; the signature is used to trace atmospheric and early Solar System chemistry. A solution is a quantum-dynamics calculation without fitted parameters that reproduces the measured enrichments and isotope-specific rate constants.
nodes.summary: When ozone forms from oxygen atoms and molecules, it becomes enriched in oxygen-17 and oxygen-18 by nearly equal amounts, although ordinary isotope effects scale with mass, as Thiemens and Heidenreich found in 1983; the signature is used to trace atmospheric and early Solar System chemistry.

nodes.title: Neodymium Magnets
nodes.html: Masato Sagawa at Sumitomo and John Croat at General Motors independently found in 1983 to 1984 that an alloy of neodymium, iron and boron, Nd2Fe14B, makes a permanent magnet far stronger than earlier ones. Neodymium magnets are used in hard drives, electric-vehicle motors, wind turbines and headphones.
nodes.summary: Masato Sagawa at Sumitomo and John Croat at General Motors independently found in 1983 to 1984 that an alloy of neodymium, iron and boron, Nd2Fe14B, makes a permanent magnet far stronger than earlier ones.

nodes.title: Car–Parrinello Molecular Dynamics
nodes.html: Roberto Car and Michele Parrinello introduced in 1985 a way to move atoms under forces computed from density functional theory on the fly, by treating the electrons as fictitious dynamical variables. Ab initio molecular dynamics made first-principles simulation of liquids, chemical reactions and materials possible.
nodes.summary: Roberto Car and Michele Parrinello introduced in 1985 a way to move atoms under forces computed from density functional theory on the fly, by treating the electrons as fictitious dynamical variables.

nodes.title: Fullerenes
nodes.html: Harold Kroto, Robert Curl and Richard Smalley vaporised graphite with a laser in 1985 and found a stable cluster of 60 carbon atoms shaped like a football, C60 or buckminsterfullerene. Wolfgang Krätschmer and Donald Huffman made it in bulk in 1990, and Kroto, Curl and Smalley shared the 1996 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
nodes.summary: Harold Kroto, Robert Curl and Richard Smalley vaporised graphite with a laser in 1985 and found a stable cluster of 60 carbon atoms shaped like a football, C60 or buckminsterfullerene.

nodes.title: How Copper Makes C₂ Fuels from CO₂

progress.what: Found ethylene as well as methane from CO2 electroreduction on copper, with ethylene’s Faradaic efficiency rising to about 20% at 40 °C.
progress.html: Found ethylene as well as methane from CO2 electroreduction on copper, with ethylene’s Faradaic efficiency rising to about 20% at 40 °C.

progress.what: DFT with the computational hydrogen electrode explained copper’s hydrocarbon activity and identified the hydrogenation of adsorbed CO as the potential-limiting step.
progress.html: DFT with the computational hydrogen electrode explained copper’s hydrocarbon activity and identified the hydrogenation of adsorbed CO as the potential-limiting step.

progress.what: Detected 16 different products of CO2 reduction on metallic copper.
progress.html: Detected 16 different products of CO2 reduction on metallic copper.

progress.what: Machine-learned potentials trained on OC25 simulated CO dimerization on copper in explicit water for up to 7 ns, finding it weakly sensitive to surface charge and cation and more favourable on stepped Cu(310) (preprint).
progress.html: Machine-learned potentials trained on OC25 simulated CO dimerization on copper in explicit water for up to 7 ns, finding it weakly sensitive to surface charge and cation and more favourable on stepped Cu(310) (preprint).

nodes.html: Copper is the only metal that electro-reduces CO2 to ethylene and ethanol in quantity, as Yoshio Hori’s group found in 1985–86, yet how the key carbon–carbon bond forms is disputed: CO dimerization, CO–CHO coupling, cations and surface restructuring have all been proposed. A solution is a mechanism, tested by simulation and in situ experiment, that predicts product selectivity well enough to design better catalysts.
nodes.summary: Copper is the only metal that electro-reduces CO2 to ethylene and ethanol in quantity, as Yoshio Hori’s group found in 1985–86, yet how the key carbon–carbon bond forms is disputed: CO dimerization, CO–CHO coupling, cations and surface restructuring have all been proposed.

nodes.title: High-Temperature Superconductors
nodes.html: Copper-oxide ceramics superconduct far above previous records (1986); by 1987 YBCO worked in liquid nitrogen at 93 K. The ambient-pressure record, held by a mercury cuprate since 1993, rose to 151 K in 2026 by pressure quenching. Nobody yet agrees on why they work.
nodes.summary: Copper-oxide ceramics superconduct far above previous records (1986); by 1987 YBCO worked in liquid nitrogen at 93 K.

nodes.title: Femtochemistry
nodes.html: Ahmed Zewail used femtosecond laser pulses in 1987 to watch ICN molecules break apart in real time, making the transition state of a reaction directly observable. Femtochemistry, rewarded with the 1999 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, opened the study of chemical dynamics on the timescale of bond vibrations.
nodes.summary: Ahmed Zewail used femtosecond laser pulses in 1987 to watch ICN molecules break apart in real time, making the transition state of a reaction directly observable.

nodes.title: Organic Crystal Structure Prediction

progress.what: Ranking with dispersion-corrected DFT predicted the structures of all four targets in the 2007 blind test.
progress.html: Ranking with dispersion-corrected DFT predicted the structures of all four targets in the 2007 blind test.

progress.what: In the sixth blind test every target, apart from one possibly disordered polymorph, was predicted by at least one submission.
progress.html: In the sixth blind test every target, apart from one possibly disordered polymorph, was predicted by at least one submission.

progress.what: In the seventh blind test many methods found the observed forms of a small flexible agrochemical, few succeeded on the more complex salt, cocrystal and metal-complex targets, and two groups blindly predicted disorder for the first time.
progress.html: In the seventh blind test many methods found the observed forms of a small flexible agrochemical, few succeeded on the more complex salt, cocrystal and metal-complex targets, and two groups blindly predicted disorder for the first time.

progress.what: OXtal, a diffusion model trained on 600,000 experimental crystal structures, recovered known structures with over 80% packing similarity at far lower cost than quantum-chemical searches (preprint).
progress.html: OXtal, a diffusion model trained on 600,000 experimental crystal structures, recovered known structures with over 80% packing similarity at far lower cost than quantum-chemical searches (preprint).

nodes.html: Predict, from the molecular diagram alone, which crystal structures and polymorphs a compound will adopt, with the observed form ranked most stable; John Maddox called the failure to do this a scandal in 1988. In the Cambridge Crystallographic Data Centre’s seventh blind test (2024), few groups succeeded on salts, cocrystals and complexes. A solution reliably finds and top-ranks the observed forms in such blind tests.
nodes.summary: Predict, from the molecular diagram alone, which crystal structures and polymorphs a compound will adopt, with the observed form ranked most stable; John Maddox called the failure to do this a scandal in 1988.

nodes.title: SMILES Notation
aliases: Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System
nodes.html: David Weininger introduced SMILES in 1988, a line notation that writes a molecule’s graph as a text string, such as CC(=O)O for acetic acid. SMILES became the standard compact format in chemical databases and cheminformatics, and later the input of chemical language models.
nodes.summary: David Weininger introduced SMILES in 1988, a line notation that writes a molecule’s graph as a text string, such as CC(=O)O for acetic acid.

nodes.title: Electrospray and MALDI
nodes.html: John Fenn’s electrospray ionisation (1988 to 1989) and the laser desorption methods of Koichi Tanaka (1987 to 1988) and of Michael Karas and Franz Hillenkamp (1988, later MALDI) lifted intact proteins into the gas phase for mass analysis. They made mass spectrometry a main tool of proteomics and biochemistry, and Fenn and Tanaka shared the 2002 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
nodes.summary: John Fenn’s electrospray ionisation (1988 to 1989) and the laser desorption methods of Koichi Tanaka (1987 to 1988) and of Michael Karas and Franz Hillenkamp (1988, later MALDI) lifted intact proteins into the gas phase for mass analysis.

nodes.title: Atom-by-Atom Positioning
nodes.html: Don Eigler and Erhard Schweizer at IBM used the tip of a scanning tunnelling microscope to drag 35 xenon atoms on a nickel surface into the letters IBM (Nature, 1990; the experiment was done in late 1989). It was the first deliberate placement of individual atoms and became an icon of nanotechnology.
nodes.summary: Don Eigler and Erhard Schweizer at IBM used the tip of a scanning tunnelling microscope to drag 35 xenon atoms on a nickel surface into the letters IBM (Nature, 1990; the experiment was done in late 1989).

nodes.title: Olefin Metathesis
nodes.html: Metal carbene catalysts swap the partners of carbon-carbon double bonds. Yves Chauvin proposed the mechanism in 1971, Richard Schrock made well-defined molybdenum catalysts in 1990 and Robert Grubbs made air-tolerant ruthenium catalysts in 1992 to 1995; the three shared the 2005 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. Metathesis is used for drugs, polymers and specialty chemicals.
nodes.summary: Metal carbene catalysts swap the partners of carbon-carbon double bonds.

nodes.title: Soot Inception Mechanism

progress.what: Proposed that resonance-stabilized hydrocarbon radicals drive clustering through chain reactions that extend conjugation, supported by mass spectrometry and theory.
progress.html: Proposed that resonance-stabilized hydrocarbon radicals drive clustering through chain reactions that extend conjugation, supported by mass spectrometry and theory.

progress.what: A review weighed physical condensation against chemical polymerization, favoured routes through π-radicals and diradicals, and found conclusive evidence and predictive models still lacking.
progress.html: A review weighed physical condensation against chemical polymerization, favoured routes through π-radicals and diradicals, and found conclusive evidence and predictive models still lacking.

progress.what: Mass spectrometry of nascent soot found only stable, compact aromatic molecules, interpreted as direct evidence that inception is physical stacking held by van der Waals forces.
progress.html: Mass spectrometry of nascent soot found only stable, compact aromatic molecules, interpreted as direct evidence that inception is physical stacking held by van der Waals forces.

progress.what: Argued that those data instead support chemical clustering, and that physical nucleation is inconsistent with thermodynamics.
progress.html: Argued that those data instead support chemical clustering, and that physical nucleation is inconsistent with thermodynamics.

nodes.html: How do hydrocarbon molecules in a flame turn into the first solid soot particles so quickly? Physical stacking of aromatic molecules and chemical routes such as resonance-stabilized radical chain reactions (2018) have been proposed, and a 2023 claim of physical nucleation was disputed in 2025. A solution is a mechanism that, in a validated kinetic model, reproduces measured inception rates and particle composition across flames.
nodes.summary: How do hydrocarbon molecules in a flame turn into the first solid soot particles so quickly?

nodes.title: Carbon Nanotubes
nodes.html: Sumio Iijima’s electron micrographs of multiwalled carbon nanotubes (1991) were followed in 1993 by single-walled tubes, reported by Iijima and by Donald Bethune’s group. The tubes are very strong, conduct heat well and are metallic or semiconducting depending on their structure, and they are used in composites and in electronics research.
nodes.summary: Sumio Iijima’s electron micrographs of multiwalled carbon nanotubes (1991) were followed in 1993 by single-walled tubes, reported by Iijima and by Donald Bethune’s group.

nodes.title: Combinatorial Chemistry
nodes.html: Árpád Furka devised split-and-pool synthesis on beads in the 1980s and published it in 1991, alongside Kit Lam’s and Richard Houghten’s peptide library methods; a few steps make millions of compounds. Combinatorial libraries fed high-throughput screening for drugs, and the idea returned in DNA-encoded libraries.
nodes.summary: Árpád Furka devised split-and-pool synthesis on beads in the 1980s and published it in 1991, alongside Kit Lam’s and Richard Houghten’s peptide library methods; a few steps make millions of compounds.

nodes.title: Dye-Sensitized Solar Cell
nodes.html: Brian O’Regan and Michael Grätzel reported in 1991 a solar cell in which a dye on nanoporous titanium dioxide absorbs light and injects electrons, reaching about 7 percent efficiency with cheap materials. The Grätzel cell inspired later photovoltaics, including the perovskite solar cell.
nodes.summary: Brian O’Regan and Michael Grätzel reported in 1991 a solar cell in which a dye on nanoporous titanium dioxide absorbs light and injects electrons, reaching about 7 percent efficiency with cheap materials.

nodes.title: Lithium-Ion Battery
nodes.html: Lithium ions shuttling between layered electrodes: Whittingham’s cells (1970s), Goodenough’s cobalt-oxide cathode (1980), Yoshino’s prototype (1985), Sony’s product (1991).
nodes.summary: Lithium ions shuttling between layered electrodes: Whittingham’s cells (1970s), Goodenough’s cobalt-oxide cathode (1980), Yoshino’s prototype (1985), Sony’s product (1991).

nodes.title: Liquid–Liquid Critical Point of Water

progress.what: X-ray laser scattering on evaporatively cooled microdroplets found maxima of compressibility and correlation length at 229 K, pointing to a Widom line that extends from a critical point.
progress.html: X-ray laser scattering on evaporatively cooled microdroplets found maxima of compressibility and correlation length at 229 K, pointing to a Widom line that extends from a critical point.

progress.what: Simulations longer than 40 microseconds of two realistic classical water models found a liquid–liquid critical point with critical behavior consistent with the 3D Ising class.
progress.html: Simulations longer than 40 microseconds of two realistic classical water models found a liquid–liquid critical point with critical behavior consistent with the 3D Ising class.

progress.what: Laser-heated amorphous ice under pressure gave high-density liquid water in which low-density liquid domains grew within microseconds, before ice could form: evidence of a liquid–liquid transition.
progress.html: Laser-heated amorphous ice under pressure gave high-density liquid water in which low-density liquid domains grew within microseconds, before ice could form: evidence of a liquid–liquid transition.

progress.what: Claimed the critical point: ultrafast heating of amorphous ices followed by X-ray scattering showed a crossover from a discontinuous to a continuous transition and a rising heat capacity indicating a critical divergence at 210 ± 8 K, near 1,000 bar. Independent confirmation is pending.
progress.html: Claimed the critical point: ultrafast heating of amorphous ices followed by X-ray scattering showed a crossover from a discontinuous to a continuous transition and a rising heat capacity indicating a critical divergence at 210 ± 8 K, near 1,000 bar. Independent confirmation is pending.

nodes.html: Does supercooled water have a second critical point, ending a line of transitions between a high-density and a low-density liquid, as Poole, Sciortino, Essmann and Stanley proposed in 1992 to explain water’s anomalies? Ice forms too fast for direct tests. In March 2026 Nilsson, Kim and co-workers reported X-ray laser evidence of a critical point near 210 K and 1,000 bar; independent confirmation would settle the question.
nodes.summary: Does supercooled water have a second critical point, ending a line of transitions between a high-density and a low-density liquid, as Poole, Sciortino, Essmann and Stanley proposed in 1992 to explain water’s anomalies?

nodes.title: Hybrid Density Functionals
nodes.html: Axel Becke showed in 1993 that mixing a fraction of exact Hartree-Fock exchange into density functional theory greatly improves accuracy; B3LYP, which adds Lee-Yang-Parr correlation, became the most used functional for organic molecules. The non-hybrid PBE functional (1996) remains the workhorse for solids.
nodes.summary: Axel Becke showed in 1993 that mixing a fraction of exact Hartree-Fock exchange into density functional theory greatly improves accuracy; B3LYP, which adds Lee-Yang-Parr correlation, became the most used functional for organic molecules.

nodes.title: Single-Molecule Magnets
nodes.html: Roberta Sessoli, Dante Gatteschi and colleagues showed in 1993 that a manganese cluster, Mn12-acetate, keeps its magnetisation like a tiny bar magnet at low temperature. Dysprosocenium complexes (Layfield and Mills groups, 2017 and 2018) raised the hysteresis temperature to 60 K and then 80 K, above the boiling point of liquid nitrogen, with hopes for dense data storage and quantum bits.
nodes.summary: Roberta Sessoli, Dante Gatteschi and colleagues showed in 1993 that a manganese cluster, Mn12-acetate, keeps its magnetisation like a tiny bar magnet at low temperature.

nodes.title: Asymmetric Amplification
nodes.html: Henri Kagan found nonlinear effects in asymmetric catalysis in 1986, and in 1995 Kenso Soai discovered a reaction in which a tiny excess of one mirror-image product catalyses its own formation and grows to near purity. It is discussed as a model for how biological handedness arose, and brought Kagan and Soai the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
nodes.summary: Henri Kagan found nonlinear effects in asymmetric catalysis in 1986, and in 1995 Kenso Soai discovered a reaction in which a tiny excess of one mirror-image product catalyses its own formation and grows to near purity.

nodes.title: Controlled Radical Polymerization
nodes.html: Atom transfer radical polymerisation (Krzysztof Matyjaszewski and Mitsuo Sawamoto, 1995) and RAFT polymerisation (Ezio Rizzardo’s group at CSIRO, 1998) gave ordinary radical polymerisation a living character. Chemists can now make polymers of controlled length and architecture, including block and brush polymers, with ordinary equipment under mild conditions.
nodes.summary: Atom transfer radical polymerisation (Krzysztof Matyjaszewski and Mitsuo Sawamoto, 1995) and RAFT polymerisation (Ezio Rizzardo’s group at CSIRO, 1998) gave ordinary radical polymerisation a living character.

nodes.title: d-Band Model of Catalysis
nodes.html: Bjørk Hammer and Jens Nørskov showed in 1995 that the energy of a metal’s d-band states determines how strongly adsorbates bind to its surface, which also explains why gold is the noblest metal. With scaling relations and volcano plots, the d-band model made computational screening and design of heterogeneous catalysts possible.
nodes.summary: Bjørk Hammer and Jens Nørskov showed in 1995 that the energy of a metal’s d-band states determines how strongly adsorbates bind to its surface, which also explains why gold is the noblest metal.

nodes.title: Mechanism of the Soai Reaction

progress.what: Crystal structures, kinetics and computations pointed to a tetrameric zinc alkoxide aggregate as the autocatalyst.
progress.html: Crystal structures, kinetics and computations pointed to a tetrameric zinc alkoxide aggregate as the autocatalyst.

progress.what: In situ mass spectrometry and kinetic modelling identified transient hemiacetalate isopropylzinc complexes as the key intermediates for both pyridyl and pyrimidyl substrates.
progress.html: In situ mass spectrometry and kinetic modelling identified transient hemiacetalate isopropylzinc complexes as the key intermediates for both pyridyl and pyrimidyl substrates.

nodes.html: How does the Soai reaction, found in 1995, turn a tiny excess of one mirror-image form of a pyridyl or pyrimidyl alcohol into almost pure product as its zinc alkoxide catalyses its own formation? A tetrameric zinc aggregate (Denmark, 2020) and hemiacetal zinc complexes (Trapp, 2025) compete as explanations. A solution is a mechanism and kinetic model that reproduces the amplification quantitatively. Soai shared the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
nodes.summary: How does the Soai reaction, found in 1995, turn a tiny excess of one mirror-image form of a pyridyl or pyrimidyl alcohol into almost pure product as its zinc alkoxide catalyses its own formation?

nodes.title: Lithium Iron Phosphate
nodes.html: Akshaya Padhi and John Goodenough showed in 1997 that olivine-structured lithium iron phosphate can reversibly store lithium and works as a battery cathode. It trades some energy density for low cost, safety and long cycle life, and with a carbon coating it now powers many electric cars, buses and grid storage systems.
nodes.summary: Akshaya Padhi and John Goodenough showed in 1997 that olivine-structured lithium iron phosphate can reversibly store lithium and works as a battery cathode.

nodes.title: Rule of Five
nodes.html: Christopher Lipinski observed in 1997 that most orally active drugs have a molecular weight below 500, a logP below 5 and no more than five hydrogen-bond donors and ten acceptors. His rule of five became a standard filter for drug-likeness in screening libraries and in the design of drug candidates.
nodes.summary: Christopher Lipinski observed in 1997 that most orally active drugs have a molecular weight below 500, a logP below 5 and no more than five hydrogen-bond donors and ten acceptors.

nodes.title: p-Type Transparent Conductor

progress.what: Showed p-type conduction in transparent thin films of CuAlO2, the first p-type transparent conducting oxide.
progress.html: Showed p-type conduction in transparent thin films of CuAlO2, the first p-type transparent conducting oxide.

progress.what: Room-temperature sputtered, iodine-doped CuI films raised the figure of merit of p-type transparent conductors a hundredfold.
progress.html: Room-temperature sputtered, iodine-doped CuI films raised the figure of merit of p-type transparent conductors a hundredfold.

progress.what: Sulfur-doped CuI films reached 511 S/cm, and 596 S/cm after peroxide treatment, with over 80% transmittance.
progress.html: Sulfur-doped CuI films reached 511 S/cm, and 596 S/cm after peroxide treatment, with over 80% transmittance.

progress.what: Amorphous Cu(S,I) films reached hole conductivities of 10³–10⁴ S/cm, comparable with indium tin oxide, with band gaps of 2.6–2.9 eV.
progress.html: Amorphous Cu(S,I) films reached hole conductivities of 10³–10⁴ S/cm, comparable with indium tin oxide, with band gaps of 2.6–2.9 eV.

nodes.html: Find a p-type transparent conductor as good as n-type indium tin oxide, which conducts about 10⁴ S/cm while staying clear, enabling transparent p–n electronics. Since CuAlO2 (1997), doped CuI films have reached about 600 S/cm and amorphous Cu(S,I) 10³–10⁴ S/cm (2023), but with band gaps of 2.6–2.9 eV that absorb blue light. A solution is an air-stable p-type film above 1,000 S/cm with a band gap above 3.1 eV, reproduced independently.
nodes.summary: Find a p-type transparent conductor as good as n-type indium tin oxide, which conducts about 10⁴ S/cm while staying clear, enabling transparent p–n electronics.

nodes.title: Green Chemistry
nodes.html: Paul Anastas and John Warner’s 1998 book set out twelve principles of green chemistry, building on Barry Trost’s concept of atom economy (1991). Preventing waste, choosing safer solvents and reagents and using catalysis became design criteria for chemical processes, and the principles are now taught and applied in industry.
nodes.summary: Paul Anastas and John Warner’s 1998 book set out twelve principles of green chemistry, building on Barry Trost’s concept of atom economy (1991).

nodes.title: Spectrum of Protonated Methane

progress.what: Full-dimensional quantum calculations reproduced a low-resolution infrared spectrum and traced an intense feature near 200 cm−1 to the motion that connects equivalent minima.
progress.html: Full-dimensional quantum calculations reproduced a low-resolution infrared spectrum and traced an intense feature near 200 cm−1 to the motion that connects equivalent minima.

progress.what: High-resolution spectroscopy of cold trapped ions yielded experimental ground-state combination differences, which constrain the lowest energy levels.
progress.html: High-resolution spectroscopy of cold trapped ions yielded experimental ground-state combination differences, which constrain the lowest energy levels.

progress.what: Neural canonical transformations computed ground and excited vibrational states; the authors note that accurately assigning the observed lines remains unsolved.
progress.html: Neural canonical transformations computed ground and excited vibrational states; the authors note that accurately assigning the observed lines remains unsolved.

nodes.html: Protonated methane, CH5+, is so floppy that its five protons scramble almost freely, and the dense high-resolution infrared spectrum recorded by White, Tang and Oka in 1999 has never been assigned line by line. A solution is a first-principles calculation of its rotation–vibration levels accurate enough to assign most observed lines and to reproduce the ground-state combination differences measured in 2015.
nodes.summary: Protonated methane, CH5+, is so floppy that its five protons scramble almost freely, and the dense high-resolution infrared spectrum recorded by White, Tang and Oka in 1999 has never been assigned line by line.

nodes.title: Metal–Organic Frameworks
nodes.html: Metal ions joined by organic linkers form crystalline frameworks with large pores. Richard Robson set out the principles in 1989, Susumu Kitagawa made gas-adsorbing frameworks in 1997 and Omar Yaghi’s MOF-5 (1999) showed permanent porosity; some MOFs have over 7,000 square metres of internal surface per gram. The three shared the 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
nodes.summary: Metal ions joined by organic linkers form crystalline frameworks with large pores.

nodes.title: Molecular Machines
nodes.html: Jean-Pierre Sauvage made interlocked-ring catenanes (1983), Fraser Stoddart a rotaxane shuttle (1991) and Ben Feringa a light-driven molecular rotary motor (1999), giving molecules that move in a controlled way. They shared the 2016 Nobel Prize in Chemistry; applications such as drug delivery and smart materials remain at an early stage.
nodes.summary: Jean-Pierre Sauvage made interlocked-ring catenanes (1983), Fraser Stoddart a rotaxane shuttle (1991) and Ben Feringa a light-driven molecular rotary motor (1999), giving molecules that move in a controlled way.

nodes.title: Organocatalysis
nodes.html: Benjamin List showed that the amino acid proline catalyses asymmetric aldol reactions, and David MacMillan developed chiral imidazolidinone catalysts for Diels-Alder reactions, both in 2000. Metal-free small-molecule catalysts proved cheap, robust and versatile, and the two shared the 2021 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
nodes.summary: Benjamin List showed that the amino acid proline catalyses asymmetric aldol reactions, and David MacMillan developed chiral imidazolidinone catalysts for Diels-Alder reactions, both in 2000.

nodes.title: Single-Molecule Reactions by STM
nodes.html: Saw-Wai Hla and Karl-Heinz Rieder used a scanning tunnelling microscope tip in 2000 to carry out every step of an Ullmann coupling on single molecules: removing iodine from iodobenzene, bringing the fragments together and joining them into biphenyl. It showed that chemical reactions can be directed one molecule at a time.
nodes.summary: Saw-Wai Hla and Karl-Heinz Rieder used a scanning tunnelling microscope tip in 2000 to carry out every step of an Ullmann coupling on single molecules: removing iodine from iodobenzene, bringing the fragments together and joining them into biphenyl.

nodes.title: Click Chemistry
nodes.html: K. Barry Sharpless called in 2001 for modular, high-yield reactions that join building blocks simply and safely, and the copper-catalysed azide-alkyne cycloaddition (Morten Meldal, and Valery Fokin with Sharpless, 2002) became the archetype. Carolyn Bertozzi’s bioorthogonal versions work in living cells; Sharpless, Meldal and Bertozzi won the 2022 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
nodes.summary: K.

nodes.title: MgB₂ Superconductor
nodes.html: Jun Akimitsu’s group in Japan found in 2001 that magnesium diboride, a cheap compound known since the 1950s, becomes superconducting at 39 K, the highest transition temperature of any conventional phonon-driven superconductor at ambient pressure. MgB2 wires are used in some magnets, and the discovery challenged ideas about the limits of conventional superconductivity.
nodes.summary: Jun Akimitsu’s group in Japan found in 2001 that magnesium diboride, a cheap compound known since the 1950s, becomes superconducting at 39 K, the highest transition temperature of any conventional phonon-driven superconductor at ambient pressure.

nodes.title: NMC Layered-Oxide Cathodes
nodes.html: Tsutomu Ohzuku and Yoshinari Makimura at Osaka City University, and Jeff Dahn’s group at Dalhousie University, reported layered lithium nickel-manganese-cobalt oxides in 2001 that store more charge than lithium cobalt oxide while using less cobalt. NMC cathodes, later made richer in nickel, power many long-range electric vehicles.
nodes.summary: Tsutomu Ohzuku and Yoshinari Makimura at Osaka City University, and Jeff Dahn’s group at Dalhousie University, reported layered lithium nickel-manganese-cobalt oxides in 2001 that store more charge than lithium cobalt oxide while using less cobalt.

nodes.title: Spin-State Energetics

progress.what: Showed that DFT spin-state splittings of iron complexes hinge on the share of exact exchange and proposed B3LYP* with 15% instead of 20%.
progress.html: Showed that DFT spin-state splittings of iron complexes hinge on the share of exact exchange and proposed B3LYP* with 15% instead of 20%.

progress.what: The SSE17 benchmark, derived from experimental data on 17 transition-metal complexes, found mean absolute errors of 1.5 kcal/mol for CCSD(T), under 3 for the best double hybrids and 5–7 for B3LYP* and TPSSh, with maximum errors above 10.
progress.html: The SSE17 benchmark, derived from experimental data on 17 transition-metal complexes, found mean absolute errors of 1.5 kcal/mol for CCSD(T), under 3 for the best double hybrids and 5–7 for B3LYP* and TPSSh, with maximum errors above 10.

progress.what: Computed CASPT2/CC spin gaps for 50 octahedral complexes, found that the best share of exact exchange depends on the spin transition, and extended this accuracy to 500 complexes with Δ-machine learning.
progress.html: Computed CASPT2/CC spin gaps for 50 octahedral complexes, found that the best share of exact exchange depends on the spin transition, and extended this accuracy to 500 complexes with Δ-machine learning.

nodes.html: Which spin state does a transition-metal complex prefer, and by how much? Density functionals disagree by many kcal/mol because the answer hinges on the share of exact exchange (Reiher, Salomon and Hess, 2001), and it governs catalysts, enzymes and spin-crossover materials. A solution is a method at DFT-like cost that matches experiment-derived spin-state energies within about 1 kcal/mol, for example on the SSE17 set (2024).
nodes.summary: Which spin state does a transition-metal complex prefer, and by how much?

nodes.title: Room-Temperature Hydrogen Sorbent

progress.what: First hydrogen-uptake measurements in a metal–organic framework, MOF-5, launching the search for framework hydrogen stores.
progress.html: First hydrogen-uptake measurements in a metal–organic framework, MOF-5, launching the search for framework hydrogen stores.

progress.what: NU-1501-Al balanced gravimetric and volumetric uptake, delivering 14% hydrogen by weight, but only in a cryogenic temperature and pressure swing.
progress.html: NU-1501-Al balanced gravimetric and volumetric uptake, delivering 14% hydrogen by weight, but only in a cryogenic temperature and pressure swing.

progress.what: Vanadium(II) sites in V2Cl2.8(btdd) bind H2 with an enthalpy of −21 kJ/mol, inside the window for room-temperature storage, giving usable capacity above compressed gas under the same conditions.
progress.html: Vanadium(II) sites in V2Cl2.8(btdd) bind H2 with an enthalpy of −21 kJ/mol, inside the window for room-temperature storage, giving usable capacity above compressed gas under the same conditions.

nodes.html: Design a porous material that stores hydrogen near room temperature well enough for a vehicle tank to meet the US Department of Energy’s system targets of 5.5 wt% and 40 g/L (2025) and ultimately 6.5 wt% and 50 g/L, between −40 and 60 °C. That needs binding of about 15–25 kJ/mol at many sites; frameworks tested since 2003 reach high capacities only near 77 K. A solution is a material whose measured usable capacity lets a system meet the targets.
nodes.summary: Design a porous material that stores hydrogen near room temperature well enough for a vehicle tank to meet the US Department of Energy’s system targets of 5.5 wt% and 40 g/L (2025) and ultimately 6.5 wt% and 50 g/L, between −40 and 60 °C.

nodes.title: Catalytic N₂ Reduction at One Metal
nodes.html: Dmitry Yandulov and Richard Schrock reported in 2003 a molybdenum complex that catalytically converts nitrogen gas into ammonia at room temperature and pressure with a proton source and a reductant. It was the first well-defined molecular catalyst for the reaction and a model for nitrogenase; later catalysts from the Peters and Nishibayashi groups were far more efficient.
nodes.summary: Dmitry Yandulov and Richard Schrock reported in 2003 a molybdenum complex that catalytically converts nitrogen gas into ammonia at room temperature and pressure with a proton source and a reductant.

nodes.title: Graphene
nodes.html: Andre Geim and Konstantin Novoselov peeled single-atom-thick layers of carbon from graphite with adhesive tape in 2004 and measured their remarkable electronic properties, work that won the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics. Graphene started the study of two-dimensional materials, which includes MXenes (2011) and transition-metal dichalcogenide monolayers.
nodes.summary: Andre Geim and Konstantin Novoselov peeled single-atom-thick layers of carbon from graphite with adhesive tape in 2004 and measured their remarkable electronic properties, work that won the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics.

nodes.title: High-Entropy Alloys
nodes.html: Jien-Wei Yeh and Brian Cantor independently reported in 2004 that alloys of five or more metals in near-equal proportions can crystallise as one simple solid solution. High-entropy alloys opened a very large composition space, now searched with computation and machine learning for materials with high strength at extreme temperatures.
nodes.summary: Jien-Wei Yeh and Brian Cantor independently reported in 2004 that alloys of five or more metals in near-equal proportions can crystallise as one simple solid solution.

nodes.title: The Zeolite Conundrum

progress.what: Enumerated hypothetical tetrahedral frameworks from polynodal graphs, an early step toward databases of possible zeolites that far outnumber the known ones.
progress.html: Enumerated hypothetical tetrahedral frameworks from polynodal graphs, an early step toward databases of possible zeolites that far outnumber the known ones.

progress.what: Named the zeolite conundrum and proposed that real frameworks stand out in how they decompose into packings of natural tiles.
progress.html: Named the zeolite conundrum and proposed that real frameworks stand out in how they decompose into packings of natural tiles.

progress.what: A machine-learning ‘sorting hat’ trained on known frameworks ranked hypothetical silica frameworks by likely synthesizability and suggested their compositional class.
progress.html: A machine-learning ‘sorting hat’ trained on known frameworks ranked hypothetical silica frameworks by likely synthesizability and suggested their compositional class.

nodes.html: Why have fewer than 300 zeolite framework types been made, when computer enumerations since 2004 have produced hundreds of thousands of hypothetical frameworks with energies close to those of real ones? The puzzle was named the zeolite conundrum in 2013. A solution is a criterion or model that predicts which hypothetical frameworks can be synthesized, confirmed when ones it ranks highly are made for the first time.
nodes.summary: Why have fewer than 300 zeolite framework types been made, when computer enumerations since 2004 have produced hundreds of thousands of hypothetical frameworks with energies close to those of real ones?

nodes.title: Covalent Organic Frameworks
nodes.html: Adrien Côté, Omar Yaghi and colleagues made COF-1 and COF-5 in 2005, crystalline porous networks built entirely from light elements joined by strong covalent bonds. COFs are tunable and stable, and COF-999 (2024) captured carbon dioxide from open air in tests; they are studied for gas storage, catalysis and energy storage.
nodes.summary: Adrien Côté, Omar Yaghi and colleagues made COF-1 and COF-5 in 2005, crystalline porous networks built entirely from light elements joined by strong covalent bonds.

nodes.title: DNA Origami
nodes.html: Paul Rothemund folded a long single strand of viral DNA into smiley faces and other shapes with about 200 short staple strands (Nature, 2006), building on Nadrian Seeman’s designed DNA junctions of 1982. DNA origami makes programmable nanostructures that position molecules with nanometre precision, for nanoscale devices, diagnostics and drug delivery.
nodes.summary: Paul Rothemund folded a long single strand of viral DNA into smiley faces and other shapes with about 200 short staple strands (Nature, 2006), building on Nadrian Seeman’s designed DNA junctions of 1982.

nodes.title: Neural-Network Potentials
nodes.html: Jörg Behler and Michele Parrinello trained neural networks in 2007 to reproduce density functional theory energies and forces, describing each atom’s surroundings with symmetry functions. Such machine-learned potentials give near-first-principles accuracy at far lower cost and, with Gaussian approximation potentials (2010) and equivariant networks, drive large-scale atomistic simulation.
nodes.summary: Jörg Behler and Michele Parrinello trained neural networks in 2007 to reproduce density functional theory energies and forces, describing each atom’s surroundings with symmetry functions.

nodes.title: Fixing DFT Delocalization Error

progress.what: The localized orbital scaling correction (LOSC) reduced delocalization error across common functionals, improving band gaps of molecules and polymer chains and photoemission spectra.
progress.html: The localized orbital scaling correction (LOSC) reduced delocalization error across common functionals, improving band gaps of molecules and polymer chains and photoemission spectra.

progress.what: DM21, a neural functional trained on chemical data and on fictitious systems with fractional charge and spin, fixed classic cases of spurious charge delocalization and beat traditional functionals on main-group benchmarks.
progress.html: DM21, a neural functional trained on chemical data and on fictitious systems with fractional charge and spin, fixed classic cases of spurious charge delocalization and beat traditional functionals on main-group benchmarks.

progress.what: Showed that DM21 does not extrapolate to transition-metal chemistry, where it often fails to converge, so the learned constraints do not yet transfer.
progress.html: Showed that DM21 does not extrapolate to transition-metal chemistry, where it often fails to converge, so the learned constraints do not yet transfer.

progress.what: Extended LOSC with orbital relaxation from linear response to larger molecules and transition-metal oxide complexes at about the cost of ordinary Kohn–Sham DFT (preprint).
progress.html: Extended LOSC with orbital relaxation from linear response to larger molecules and transition-metal oxide complexes at about the cost of ordinary Kohn–Sham DFT (preprint).

nodes.html: Approximate density functionals over-delocalize electrons: their energy curves between integer electron numbers where the exact energy is piecewise linear, which shrinks band gaps and distorts charge-transfer and barrier energies (Mori-Sánchez, Cohen and Yang, 2008). A solution is a functional that obeys the fractional-charge and fractional-spin conditions for molecules and solids at about hybrid-DFT cost while staying accurate on benchmarks.
nodes.summary: Approximate density functionals over-delocalize electrons: their energy curves between integer electron numbers where the exact energy is piecewise linear, which shrinks band gaps and distorts charge-transfer and barrier energies (Mori-Sánchez, Cohen and Yang, 2008).

nodes.title: Iron-Based Superconductors
nodes.html: Hideo Hosono’s group reported in 2008 that fluorine-doped LaFeAsO superconducts at 26 K, and relatives reached 55 K within months. Iron pnictides and chalcogenides were the second family of high-temperature superconductors after the cuprates, and their magnetism and electronic structure continue to inform theories of unconventional superconductivity.
nodes.summary: Hideo Hosono’s group reported in 2008 that fluorine-doped LaFeAsO superconducts at 26 K, and relatives reached 55 K within months.

nodes.title: Photoredox Catalysis
nodes.html: In 2008 and 2009 David MacMillan, Tehshik Yoon and Corey Stephenson and their groups showed that ruthenium and iridium complexes excited by visible light can shuttle single electrons to drive organic reactions under mild conditions. Photoredox catalysis became a mainstream tool for forming bonds in drug discovery and materials synthesis.
nodes.summary: In 2008 and 2009 David MacMillan, Tehshik Yoon and Corey Stephenson and their groups showed that ruthenium and iridium complexes excited by visible light can shuttle single electrons to drive organic reactions under mild conditions.

nodes.title: Aqueous Solubility Prediction

progress.what: The first Solubility Challenge asked for the intrinsic solubilities of 32 drug-like molecules, given 100 high-precision measurements for training.
progress.html: The first Solubility Challenge asked for the intrinsic solubilities of 32 drug-like molecules, given 100 high-precision measurements for training.

progress.what: Reported the 2019 Second Solubility Challenge on 132 drug-like molecules, scored on a tight set whose measurements agree to about 0.17 log units and a loose set with about 0.62 log units of scatter.
progress.html: Reported the 2019 Second Solubility Challenge on 132 drug-like molecules, scored on a tight set whose measurements agree to about 0.17 log units and a loose set with about 0.62 log units of scatter.

progress.what: A post hoc study with larger training sets found that the best model on the challenge data, a graph convolutional network, still had an error of 0.86 log units.
progress.html: A post hoc study with larger training sets found that the best model on the challenge data, a graph convolutional network, still had an error of 0.86 log units.

nodes.html: Predict how much of a new drug-like compound dissolves in water, its intrinsic solubility, from its structure alone. Careful shake-flask measurements agree to about 0.2 log units, yet the best models on the 2008 and 2019 Solubility Challenges err by several times that. A solution is a model whose blind predictions for a new set of drug-like compounds reach a root-mean-square error of 0.5 log units or better.
nodes.summary: Predict how much of a new drug-like compound dissolves in water, its intrinsic solubility, from its structure alone.

nodes.title: Perovskite Solar Cells
nodes.html: Akihiro Kojima, Tsutomu Miyasaka and colleagues used lead-halide perovskites as light absorbers in dye-sensitised solar cells in 2009 and obtained 3.8 percent efficiency. Work by Henry Snaith, Nam-Gyu Park and others in 2012 raised it to about 10 percent in solid-state cells, and single-junction cells now exceed 26 percent, with higher figures when stacked on silicon.
nodes.summary: Akihiro Kojima, Tsutomu Miyasaka and colleagues used lead-halide perovskites as light absorbers in dye-sensitised solar cells in 2009 and obtained 3.8 percent efficiency.

nodes.title: Direct Air Capture Sorbent

progress.what: Released Open DAC 2023, a large open DFT dataset of CO2 and water adsorption in metal–organic frameworks for machine-learned sorbent screening.
progress.html: Released Open DAC 2023, a large open DFT dataset of CO2 and water adsorption in metal–organic frameworks for machine-learned sorbent screening.

progress.what: COF-999, a covalent organic framework carrying amines, took up 0.96 mmol/g of CO2 from 400 ppm air when dry and 2.05 mmol/g at 50% humidity, ran over 100 cycles in open air and regenerated at 60 °C.
progress.html: COF-999, a covalent organic framework carrying amines, took up 0.96 mmol/g of CO2 from 400 ppm air when dry and 2.05 mmol/g at 50% humidity, ran over 100 cycles in open air and regenerated at 60 °C.

nodes.html: Design a sorbent that pulls CO2 from air at about 420 ppm, works in humid air, releases it with little heat and lasts thousands of cycles, so that direct air capture, assessed by the American Physical Society in 2011, can approach the US Department of Energy’s goal of under $100 per tonne; costs in 2025 exceeded $1,000. A solution is a sorbent whose measured capacity, kinetics and stability support a credible process cost below $100 per tonne.
nodes.summary: Design a sorbent that pulls CO2 from air at about 420 ppm, works in humid air, releases it with little heat and lasts thousands of cycles, so that direct air capture, assessed by the American Physical Society in 2011, can approach the US Department of Energy’s goal of under $100 per tonne; costs in 2025 exceeded $1,000.

nodes.title: Materials Project
nodes.html: Kristin Persson, Gerbrand Ceder and colleagues launched the Materials Project in 2011, an open database of density functional theory calculations for known and hypothetical inorganic compounds, alongside the US Materials Genome Initiative. Its free data and software trained a generation of machine-learning models for materials discovery.
nodes.summary: Kristin Persson, Gerbrand Ceder and colleagues launched the Materials Project in 2011, an open database of density functional theory calculations for known and hypothetical inorganic compounds, alongside the US Materials Genome Initiative.

nodes.title: Breaking the OER Scaling Relation

progress.what: DFT showed that a second, proton-accepting site next to the active site can in principle lift the volcano limit on oxygen evolution.
