progress.html: DFT showed that a second, proton-accepting site next to the active site can in principle lift the volcano limit on oxygen evolution.

progress.what: Activated lattice-oxygen redox in perovskite oxides, an oxygen-evolution pathway that bypasses the sequence of adsorbed intermediates behind the scaling limit.
progress.html: Activated lattice-oxygen redox in perovskite oxides, an oxygen-evolution pathway that bypasses the sequence of adsorbed intermediates behind the scaling limit.

progress.what: A review twenty years after the first scaling relations set out geometry-driven strategies, such as dual sites, for designing catalysts that escape them.
progress.html: A review twenty years after the first scaling relations set out geometry-driven strategies, such as dual sites, for designing catalysts that escape them.

nodes.html: Oxygen-evolution catalysts bind the OH and OOH intermediates through the same atom, so their energies rise and fall together and set a minimum overpotential of about 0.37 V (Man and colleagues; Koper, 2011), a major energy loss in water electrolysis. A solution is a catalytic site, designed with DFT and confirmed experimentally, that breaks this scaling relation and evolves oxygen stably at a clearly lower overpotential.
nodes.summary: Oxygen-evolution catalysts bind the OH and OOH intermediates through the same atom, so their energies rise and fall together and set a minimum overpotential of about 0.37 V (Man and colleagues; Koper, 2011), a major energy loss in water electrolysis.

nodes.title: Rare-Earth-Free Strong Magnet

progress.what: Reported Fe16N2 films with the highest room-temperature saturation magnetization of any known material, making iron nitride a long-standing candidate.
progress.html: Reported Fe16N2 films with the highest room-temperature saturation magnetization of any known material, making iron nitride a long-standing candidate.

progress.what: Made hard-magnetic tetrataenite, ordered FeNi, in bulk by ordinary casting, at cooling rates 11–15 orders of magnitude faster than in the meteorites where it forms.
progress.html: Made hard-magnetic tetrataenite, ordered FeNi, in bulk by ordinary casting, at cooling rates 11–15 orders of magnitude faster than in the meteorites where it forms.

progress.what: Broke ground in Sartell, Minnesota, on a plant for 1,500 tonnes a year of rare-earth-free iron nitride magnets, after pilot production in Minneapolis.
progress.html: Broke ground in Sartell, Minnesota, on a plant for 1,500 tonnes a year of rare-earth-free iron nitride magnets, after pilot production in Minneapolis.

nodes.html: Make a permanent magnet from abundant elements, without rare earths, that rivals neodymium–iron–boron magnets, whose best grades store over 400 kJ/m³ and which drive electric motors and wind turbines; the 2011 rare-earth price spike made this urgent. Iron nitride and tetrataenite (FeNi), cast in bulk in 2023, lead the candidates. A solution matches NdFeB’s energy product and keeps its coercivity at motor temperatures.
nodes.summary: Make a permanent magnet from abundant elements, without rare earths, that rivals neodymium–iron–boron magnets, whose best grades store over 400 kJ/m³ and which drive electric motors and wind turbines; the 2011 rare-earth price spike made this urgent.

nodes.title: Single-Atom Catalysis
nodes.html: Botao Qiao, Tao Zhang, Jun Li and colleagues showed in 2011 that isolated platinum atoms on iron oxide catalyse the oxidation of carbon monoxide efficiently, and coined the term single-atom catalysis. Using every metal atom as an active site saves precious metals, and single-atom catalysts became a large research field linking homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis.
nodes.summary: Botao Qiao, Tao Zhang, Jun Li and colleagues showed in 2011 that isolated platinum atoms on iron oxide catalyse the oxidation of carbon monoxide efficiently, and coined the term single-atom catalysis.

nodes.title: Superionic Solid Electrolytes
nodes.html: Noriaki Kamaya, Ryoji Kanno and colleagues reported in 2011 that Li10GeP2S12 conducts lithium ions as well as liquid electrolytes do, about 12 millisiemens per centimetre at room temperature. It revived research on all-solid-state batteries, which promise higher energy density and better safety than liquid-electrolyte cells.
nodes.summary: Noriaki Kamaya, Ryoji Kanno and colleagues reported in 2011 that Li10GeP2S12 conducts lithium ions as well as liquid electrolytes do, about 12 millisiemens per centimetre at room temperature.

nodes.title: Vitrimers
nodes.html: Ludwik Leibler’s group at ESPCI in Paris reported in 2011 polymer networks whose cross-links swap partners when heated without breaking the network, so a thermoset can be reshaped, repaired and recycled while staying insoluble. The material flows gradually like silica glass, hence the name vitrimer.
nodes.summary: Ludwik Leibler’s group at ESPCI in Paris reported in 2011 polymer networks whose cross-links swap partners when heated without breaking the network, so a thermoset can be reshaped, repaired and recycled while staying insoluble.

nodes.title: Methane Storage Target

progress.what: Measured that the framework HKUST-1 holds about 270 cm³(STP)/cm³ of methane at 65 bar and room temperature, a total uptake; the amount delivered down to 5.8 bar is smaller.
progress.html: Measured that the framework HKUST-1 holds about 270 cm³(STP)/cm³ of methane at 65 bar and room temperature, a total uptake; the amount delivered down to 5.8 bar is smaller.

progress.what: Simulations of 122,835 hypothetical frameworks found a maximum deliverable capacity of 206 cm³(STP)/cm³ between 65 and 5.8 bar at 298 K, well short of the 315 target.
progress.html: Simulations of 122,835 hypothetical frameworks found a maximum deliverable capacity of 206 cm³(STP)/cm³ between 65 and 5.8 bar at 298 K, well short of the 315 target.

progress.what: Flexible frameworks that switch structure under pressure raised usable capacity and partly absorbed the heat released while filling.
progress.html: Flexible frameworks that switch structure under pressure raised usable capacity and partly absorbed the heat released while filling.

progress.what: Binder-free monoliths of the framework UiO-66 with tuned mesopores reached benchmark volumetric working capacities for methane.
progress.html: Binder-free monoliths of the framework UiO-66 with tuned mesopores reached benchmark volumetric working capacities for methane.

nodes.html: Find a porous adsorbent that, at 25 °C, delivers 315 volumes of methane (at standard conditions) per volume of material between 65 and 5.8 bar, the target ARPA-E set in 2012 for natural-gas vehicles, or prove that none can. Screens of over 100,000 hypothetical frameworks (2014–15) found ceilings near 200. A solution is a material whose measured deliverable capacity meets the target, or a rigorous bound that rules it out.
nodes.summary: Find a porous adsorbent that, at 25 °C, delivers 315 volumes of methane (at standard conditions) per volume of material between 65 and 5.8 bar, the target ARPA-E set in 2012 for natural-gas vehicles, or prove that none can.

nodes.title: 2-Norbornyl Cation Settled
nodes.html: A crystal structure of the 2-norbornyl cation at 40 K, reported in 2013 by Ingo Krossing, Karsten Meyer, Paul von Ragué Schleyer and co-workers, showed a delocalised three-centre, two-electron bond. It ended a dispute of about six decades, begun by Saul Winstein and challenged by Herbert Brown, over whether this ion is nonclassical.
nodes.summary: A crystal structure of the 2-norbornyl cation at 40 K, reported in 2013 by Ingo Krossing, Karsten Meyer, Paul von Ragué Schleyer and co-workers, showed a delocalised three-centre, two-electron bond.

nodes.title: Variational Quantum Eigensolver
nodes.html: Alberto Peruzzo, Jarrod McClean, Alán Aspuru-Guzik and colleagues used a photonic quantum chip in 2014 to estimate the ground-state energy of the HeH+ molecule, with a classical computer tuning the quantum circuit’s parameters. The variational quantum eigensolver became the template for chemistry on noisy quantum computers.
nodes.summary: Alberto Peruzzo, Jarrod McClean, Alán Aspuru-Guzik and colleagues used a photonic quantum chip in 2014 to estimate the ground-state energy of the HeH+ molecule, with a classical computer tuning the quantum circuit’s parameters.

nodes.title: Conventional Superconductor Above 77 K

progress.what: Machine-learning-accelerated screening of more than a million compounds proposed Mg2XH6 hydrides (X = Rh, Ir, Pd, Pt) with predicted ambient-pressure critical temperatures of 45–80 K.
progress.html: Machine-learning-accelerated screening of more than a million compounds proposed Mg2XH6 hydrides (X = Rh, Ir, Pd, Pt) with predicted ambient-pressure critical temperatures of 45–80 K.

progress.what: High-throughput calculations predicted metastable Mg2IrH6 to superconduct near 160 K at ambient pressure and proposed making it from Mg2IrH7, stable above 15 GPa.
progress.html: High-throughput calculations predicted metastable Mg2IrH6 to superconduct near 160 K at ambient pressure and proposed making it from Mg2IrH7, stable above 15 GPa.

progress.what: Attempts to make Mg2IrH6 at pressures up to about 28 GPa gave instead the insulating, structurally related Mg2IrH5, which was more stable under every condition tested.
progress.html: Attempts to make Mg2IrH6 at pressures up to about 28 GPa gave instead the insulating, structurally related Mg2IrH5, which was more stable under every condition tested.

nodes.html: Find a conventional, phonon-mediated superconductor that works above 77 K, the boiling point of liquid nitrogen, at ambient pressure; the record has stood at 39 K for MgB2 since 2001. Calculations in 2024 predicted that Mg2IrH6 would superconduct near 160 K, but attempts to make it have given the insulator Mg2IrH5. A solution is a material whose zero resistance and Meissner effect above 77 K at 1 atm are confirmed by independent groups.
nodes.summary: Find a conventional, phonon-mediated superconductor that works above 77 K, the boiling point of liquid nitrogen, at ambient pressure; the record has stood at 39 K for MgB2 since 2001.

nodes.title: Automated Iterative Synthesis
nodes.html: Martin Burke’s group at the University of Illinois built a machine that assembled many different small molecules from MIDA boronate building blocks by repeated Suzuki couplings (Science, 2015). It was a step toward the push-button synthesis of organic molecules.
nodes.summary: Martin Burke’s group at the University of Illinois built a machine that assembled many different small molecules from MIDA boronate building blocks by repeated Suzuki couplings (Science, 2015).

nodes.title: Hydride Superconductors
nodes.html: Mikhail Eremets and Alexander Drozdov reported in 2015 that hydrogen sulfide compressed to about 150 gigapascals superconducts at 203 K, as density functional theory had predicted. Lanthanum hydride reached about 250 K in 2019, while later claims of room-temperature superconductivity in other hydrides were retracted.
nodes.summary: Mikhail Eremets and Alexander Drozdov reported in 2015 that hydrogen sulfide compressed to about 150 gigapascals superconducts at 203 K, as density functional theory had predicted.

nodes.title: Push-Button Synthesis Machine

progress.what: One automated process built many classes of small molecules by iterative coupling of MIDA boronate building blocks, with a general purification step.
progress.html: One automated process built many classes of small molecules by iterative coupling of MIDA boronate building blocks, with a general purification step.

progress.what: Paired an AI retrosynthesis planner with a robotically reconfigurable flow platform, though chemists still supplied details such as solvents and stoichiometry.
progress.html: Paired an AI retrosynthesis planner with a robotically reconfigurable flow platform, though chemists still supplied details such as solvents and stoichiometry.

progress.what: An AI-driven robotic chemist planned routes and conditions and refined its recipes from its own experimental feedback, validated on three organic compounds.
progress.html: An AI-driven robotic chemist planned routes and conditions and refined its recipes from its own experimental feedback, validated on three organic compounds.

progress.what: Grouping reactions by shared time and temperature let one robotic platform make structurally diverse molecules beyond the usual scaffold-decoration libraries.
progress.html: Grouping reactions by shared time and temperature let one robotic platform make structurally diverse molecules beyond the usual scaffold-decoration libraries.

nodes.html: Build a machine that takes the structure of any reasonable small organic molecule and, with no human help, plans a route, runs the reactions, purifies the product and confirms its identity. Burke’s iterative coupling machine (2015) and AI-planned robots since 2019 handle only restricted reaction types or still need chemists at key steps. A solution is an open system that makes most of a blind set of diverse drug-like targets this way.
nodes.summary: Build a machine that takes the structure of any reasonable small organic molecule and, with no human help, plans a route, runs the reactions, purifies the product and confirms its identity.

nodes.title: Underscreening in Concentrated Electrolytes

progress.what: Showed that screening lengths measured in many salt solutions and ionic liquids fall on one scaling curve in the ratio of ion diameter to Debye length.
progress.html: Showed that screening lengths measured in many salt solutions and ionic liquids fall on one scaling curve in the ratio of ion diameter to Debye length.

progress.what: Colloidal-probe AFM, which had not seen the effect, reproduced anomalously long screening lengths in concentrated LaCl3 solutions once experimental conditions were tuned, suggesting diffuse ion clusters (preprint).
progress.html: Colloidal-probe AFM, which had not seen the effect, reproduced anomalously long screening lengths in concentrated LaCl3 solutions once experimental conditions were tuned, suggesting diffuse ion clusters (preprint).

nodes.html: Surface-force measurements in 2016 found that the electrostatic screening length in concentrated salt solutions and ionic liquids grows with concentration, far beyond Debye–Hückel theory, but other techniques have not consistently reproduced it. A solution is a theory or simulation that agrees with all reliable measurements, settles whether this underscreening is a bulk property, and explains its scaling with ion size and concentration.
nodes.summary: Surface-force measurements in 2016 found that the electrostatic screening length in concentrated salt solutions and ionic liquids grows with concentration, far beyond Debye–Hückel theory, but other techniques have not consistently reproduced it.

nodes.title: Blind pKa and logP Prediction

progress.what: In the SAMPL6 logP challenge, 91 blind prediction methods were scored on 11 small molecules; 10 of them reached a root-mean-square error below 0.5 log units.
progress.html: In the SAMPL6 logP challenge, 91 blind prediction methods were scored on 11 small molecules; 10 of them reached a root-mean-square error below 0.5 log units.

progress.what: A thermodynamics-informed neural network ranked first overall for blind microscopic and macroscopic pKa predictions of 35 compounds in the 2024 euroSAMPL1 challenge.
progress.html: A thermodynamics-informed neural network ranked first overall for blind microscopic and macroscopic pKa predictions of 35 compounds in the 2024 euroSAMPL1 challenge.

nodes.html: Predict the acidity constants (pKa) and octanol–water partition coefficients (logP) of new drug-like molecules before the measurements are revealed, including tautomers and multiple ionizable groups. In blind SAMPL challenges since 2017 only a few methods have reached logP errors near 0.5 log units on small test sets. A solution is a method that predicts a new blind set within about 0.5 pKa units and 0.3 logP units.
nodes.summary: Predict the acidity constants (pKa) and octanol–water partition coefficients (logP) of new drug-like molecules before the measurements are revealed, including tautomers and multiple ionizable groups.

nodes.title: FeMoco Ground State

progress.what: Proposed the nitrogenase cofactor, in a 54-orbital model, as a flagship chemistry problem for fault-tolerant quantum computers and estimated the resources needed.
progress.html: Proposed the nitrogenase cofactor, in a 54-orbital model, as a flagship chemistry problem for fault-tolerant quantum computers and estimated the resources needed.

progress.what: Showed that the 54-orbital model misses the cofactor’s open-shell character and introduced a 76-orbital, 152-qubit model that became the standard benchmark.
progress.html: Showed that the 54-orbital model misses the cofactor’s open-shell character and introduced a 76-orbital, 152-qubit model that became the standard benchmark.

progress.what: Estimated with tensor hypercontraction that FeMoco could be simulated on a fault-tolerant quantum computer with about four million physical qubits in under four days.
progress.html: Estimated with tensor hypercontraction that FeMoco could be simulated on a fault-tolerant quantum computer with about four million physical qubits in under four days.

progress.what: Claimed the ground-state energy of the 76-orbital model to chemical accuracy with classical methods, by ranking competing broken-symmetry states and extrapolating high-order coupled-cluster and DMRG energies. Several spin isomers remain degenerate within that accuracy. Not peer reviewed as of October 2026.
progress.html: Claimed the ground-state energy of the 76-orbital model to chemical accuracy with classical methods, by ranking competing broken-symmetry states and extrapolating high-order coupled-cluster and DMRG energies. Several spin isomers remain degenerate within that accuracy. Not peer reviewed as of October 2026.

nodes.html: What is the ground-state energy of the iron–molybdenum cofactor of nitrogenase in the 76-orbital model used since 2019 to benchmark quantum computers, after Reiher and colleagues posed the problem in 2017? Solving it means an energy within chemical accuracy, about 1 kcal/mol, and a ranking of the spin states. A January 2026 preprint from Garnet Chan’s group claims the energy classically but finds several spin states tied.
nodes.summary: What is the ground-state energy of the iron–molybdenum cofactor of nitrogenase in the 76-orbital model used since 2019 to benchmark quantum computers, after Reiher and colleagues posed the problem in 2017?

nodes.title: AI Retrosynthesis
nodes.html: Marwin Segler, Mike Preuss and Mark Waller combined deep neural networks with Monte Carlo tree search to plan multistep syntheses, and chemists rated the routes as good as those from the literature (Nature, 2018). In the same year Bartosz Grzybowski’s group ran in the laboratory syntheses planned by the rule-based Chematica program.
nodes.summary: Marwin Segler, Mike Preuss and Mark Waller combined deep neural networks with Monte Carlo tree search to plan multistep syntheses, and chemists rated the routes as good as those from the literature (Nature, 2018).

nodes.title: Generative Molecular Design
nodes.html: Rafael Gómez-Bombarelli, Alán Aspuru-Guzik and colleagues trained a variational autoencoder on SMILES strings to map molecules into a continuous space (ACS Central Science, 2018; preprint 2016). Gradient-based search in that space proposes new molecules with desired properties, launching generative chemistry for drug and materials design.
nodes.summary: Rafael Gómez-Bombarelli, Alán Aspuru-Guzik and colleagues trained a variational autoencoder on SMILES strings to map molecules into a continuous space (ACS Central Science, 2018; preprint 2016).

nodes.title: Reaction Yield Prediction

progress.what: A random forest trained on a high-throughput screen of thousands of palladium-catalysed C–N couplings predicted the yields of held-out reactions.
progress.html: A random forest trained on a high-throughput screen of thousands of palladium-catalysed C–N couplings predicted the yields of held-out reactions.

progress.what: Showed that models fed random-valued features performed comparably on that screen, so its design could not show that chemistry had been learned.
progress.html: Showed that models fed random-valued features performed comparably on that screen, so its design could not show that chemistry had been learned.

progress.what: A transformer reading reaction SMILES predicted yields in two high-throughput datasets well, but patent yields from USPTO varied systematically with reaction scale, limiting their use for training.
progress.html: A transformer reading reaction SMILES predicted yields in two high-throughput datasets well, but patent yields from USPTO varied systematically with reaction scale, limiting their use for training.

progress.what: On 41,239 literature amide couplings the best of many models reached R² of only 0.395, against about 0.9 on a high-throughput set.
progress.html: On 41,239 literature amide couplings the best of many models reached R² of only 0.395, against about 0.9 on a high-throughput set.

nodes.html: Predict the yield of a reaction that has never been run from its reactants, reagents, catalyst and conditions. Machine-learning models do well inside high-throughput screens such as a 2018 C–N coupling set, but reached R² of only about 0.4 on 41,239 literature amide couplings (2023). A solution is a model whose prospective predictions for new substrates and reaction classes fall within about 10 percentage points of measured yields.
nodes.summary: Predict the yield of a reaction that has never been run from its reactants, reagents, catalyst and conditions.

nodes.title: Chemputer
nodes.html: Leroy Cronin’s group at Glasgow described in 2019 a modular robot that carries out organic syntheses from instructions written in a chemical programming language. Procedures written as code can be shared and reproduced between laboratories, a step toward digital chemistry.
nodes.summary: Leroy Cronin’s group at Glasgow described in 2019 a modular robot that carries out organic syntheses from instructions written in a chemical programming language.

nodes.title: Coupled-Cluster-Accurate ML Potential

progress.what: ANI-1ccx, trained on DFT data and then retrained on CCSD(T)/CBS energies, approached coupled-cluster accuracy for reaction energies, isomerizations and torsions of organic molecules made of H, C, N and O.
progress.html: ANI-1ccx, trained on DFT data and then retrained on CCSD(T)/CBS energies, approached coupled-cluster accuracy for reaction energies, isomerizations and torsions of organic molecules made of H, C, N and O.

progress.what: Released OMol25, more than 100 million ωB97M-V/def2-TZVPD calculations on systems of up to 350 atoms across 83 elements, so models trained on it target hybrid-DFT accuracy.
progress.html: Released OMol25, more than 100 million ωB97M-V/def2-TZVPD calculations on systems of up to 350 atoms across 83 elements, so models trained on it target hybrid-DFT accuracy.

progress.what: A Δ-learned potential reached CCSD(T) accuracy for a covalent organic framework, with errors below 0.4 meV/atom, and the authors found that ANI-1ccx fails even qualitatively for the benzene dimer.
progress.html: A Δ-learned potential reached CCSD(T) accuracy for a covalent organic framework, with errors below 0.4 meV/atom, and the authors found that ANI-1ccx fails even qualitatively for the benzene dimer.

nodes.html: Can a machine-learned interatomic potential match CCSD(T), the reference method of quantum chemistry, across chemistry at force-field speed? ANI-1ccx (2019) came close for small organic molecules, while broad models such as those trained on OMol25 (2025) learn from DFT. A solution is an open potential within 1 kcal/mol of CCSD(T) on standard benchmarks spanning main-group, transition-metal and non-covalent chemistry, including bond breaking.
nodes.summary: Can a machine-learned interatomic potential match CCSD(T), the reference method of quantum chemistry, across chemistry at force-field speed?

nodes.title: Cyclo[18]carbon
nodes.html: Katharina Kaiser, Leo Gross and colleagues at IBM Zurich, with Harry Anderson’s group at Oxford, made a ring of 18 carbon atoms, cyclo[18]carbon, on a salt surface by removing carbon monoxide groups from a precursor with the tip of a scanning probe microscope (Science, 2019). Atomic force microscopy showed alternating triple and single bonds.
nodes.summary: Katharina Kaiser, Leo Gross and colleagues at IBM Zurich, with Harry Anderson’s group at Oxford, made a ring of 18 carbon atoms, cyclo[18]carbon, on a salt surface by removing carbon monoxide groups from a precursor with the tip of a scanning probe microscope (Science, 2019).

nodes.title: Predicting Enantioselectivity

progress.what: Modelled more than 800 chiral phosphoric acid catalysts and, training on a subset of experiments, accurately predicted which would be more selective in an imine–thiol coupling.
progress.html: Modelled more than 800 chiral phosphoric acid catalysts and, training on a subset of experiments, accurately predicted which would be more selective in an imine–thiol coupling.

progress.what: One statistical model built from 367 reactions in 17 papers predicted selectivities of chiral phosphoric acid-catalysed additions to imines for catalysts and substrates outside its training set.
progress.html: One statistical model built from 367 reactions in 17 papers predicted selectivities of chiral phosphoric acid-catalysed additions to imines for catalysts and substrates outside its training set.

progress.what: An ensemble of chemical language models fine-tuned on 220 examples of an asymmetric C(sp3)–H activation predicted ee for new ligands, and most wet-lab tests agreed.
progress.html: An ensemble of chemical language models fine-tuned on 220 examples of an asymmetric C(sp3)–H activation predicted ee for new ligands, and most wet-lab tests agreed.

progress.what: Models trained on 1,007 literature Sharpless dihydroxylations predicted selectivity across alkene classes with mean errors of at most 0.3 kcal/mol and were validated on new alkenes.
progress.html: Models trained on 1,007 literature Sharpless dihydroxylations predicted selectivity across alkene classes with mean errors of at most 0.3 kcal/mol and were validated on new alkenes.

nodes.html: Predict, before any experiment, which mirror-image product a new chiral catalyst will favour and by how much. Data-driven models since 2019 reach errors near 0.3 kcal/mol within single, well-sampled reaction families such as the Sharpless dihydroxylation (2025), but do not transfer to new reaction classes. A solution makes prospective predictions for unseen catalysts and reaction types within about 0.3 kcal/mol of measured selectivities.
nodes.summary: Predict, before any experiment, which mirror-image product a new chiral catalyst will favour and by how much.

nodes.title: Inorganic Synthesis Planning

progress.what: Text-mined 19,488 solid-state synthesis recipes from 53,538 literature paragraphs into an open dataset.
progress.html: Text-mined 19,488 solid-state synthesis recipes from 53,538 literature paragraphs into an open dataset.

progress.what: A recommender that learns material similarity from 29,900 text-mined recipes proposed precursors for 2,654 held-out targets, with at least 82% matching a reported route among its top five suggestions.
progress.html: A recommender that learns material similarity from 29,900 text-mined recipes proposed precursors for 2,654 held-out targets, with at least 82% matching a reported route among its top five suggestions.

progress.what: The A-Lab, an autonomous robotic lab, planned recipes with literature-trained models and active learning and reported making 41 of 58 computed targets in 17 days; the paper’s current version gives 36 of 57.
progress.html: The A-Lab, an autonomous robotic lab, planned recipes with literature-trained models and active learning and reported making 41 of 58 computed targets in 17 days; the paper’s current version gives 36 of 57.

progress.what: Re-analysed the A-Lab’s diffraction data and argued that none of the claimed new materials was new, two thirds being likely known disordered versions of the targets, so automated phase identification is not yet reliable.
progress.html: Re-analysed the A-Lab’s diffraction data and argued that none of the claimed new materials was new, two thirds being likely known disordered versions of the targets, so automated phase identification is not yet reliable.

nodes.html: Given a target inorganic compound, predict the precursors, temperatures and atmosphere that make it phase-pure on the first attempt, the step that limits turning computed materials into real ones. Text-mined recipes (2019) and robotic labs such as the A-Lab (2023) help, but a 2024 re-analysis showed that even recognizing success is hard. A solution makes most of a blind set of new computed targets phase-pure, confirmed by diffraction.
nodes.summary: Given a target inorganic compound, predict the precursors, temperatures and atmosphere that make it phase-pure on the first attempt, the step that limits turning computed materials into real ones.

nodes.title: Neural-Network Wavefunctions
nodes.html: FermiNet (David Pfau, James Spencer and colleagues at DeepMind) and PauliNet (Jan Hermann, Frank Noé and colleagues), both introduced in 2019 and published in 2020, use deep neural networks as many-electron wavefunctions optimised by variational Monte Carlo. They match or beat coupled-cluster accuracy on small molecules.
nodes.summary: FermiNet (David Pfau, James Spencer and colleagues at DeepMind) and PauliNet (Jan Hermann, Frank Noé and colleagues), both introduced in 2019 and published in 2020, use deep neural networks as many-electron wavefunctions optimised by variational Monte Carlo.

nodes.title: Nickelate Superconductors
nodes.html: Danfeng Li, Harold Hwang and colleagues at Stanford found in 2019 that thin films of an infinite-layer nickel oxide, Nd0.8Sr0.2NiO2, superconduct at about 10 K. Bilayer La3Ni2O7 reached about 80 K under pressure (Meng Wang and colleagues, 2023), and strained thin films superconduct near 40 K at ambient pressure (2025), making nickelates a new family of high-temperature superconductors.
nodes.summary: Danfeng Li, Harold Hwang and colleagues at Stanford found in 2019 that thin films of an infinite-layer nickel oxide, Nd0.8Sr0.2NiO2, superconduct at about 10 K.

nodes.title: Ultra-Large Virtual Screening
nodes.html: Jiankun Lyu, John Irwin, Brian Shoichet, Bryan Roth and colleagues docked 170 million make-on-demand molecules against two targets and found new potent ligands (Nature, 2019). Docking libraries of billions of molecules followed, showing that larger virtual screens can find better hits.
nodes.summary: Jiankun Lyu, John Irwin, Brian Shoichet, Bryan Roth and colleagues docked 170 million make-on-demand molecules against two targets and found new potent ligands (Nature, 2019).

nodes.title: Enzymatic PET Recycling
nodes.html: An engineered leaf-compost cutinase depolymerised 90 percent of PET bottle plastic into monomers in 10 hours at 72 degrees Celsius (Vincent Tournier, Alain Marty and colleagues, Nature, 2020). Hal Alper’s FAST-PETase (2022), designed with machine learning, works at milder temperatures.
nodes.summary: An engineered leaf-compost cutinase depolymerised 90 percent of PET bottle plastic into monomers in 10 hours at 72 degrees Celsius (Vincent Tournier, Alain Marty and colleagues, Nature, 2020).

nodes.title: Open Catalyst Challenge

progress.what: Published OC20, over a million DFT relaxations of adsorbates on catalyst surfaces, with tasks scored by the share of predicted energies within 0.02 eV of DFT.
progress.html: Published OC20, over a million DFT relaxations of adsorbates on catalyst surfaces, with tasks scored by the share of predicted energies within 0.02 eV of DFT.

progress.what: Extended the benchmarks to oxide electrocatalysts with the OC22 dataset.
progress.html: Extended the benchmarks to oxide electrocatalysts with the OC22 dataset.

progress.what: AdsorbML found the lowest-energy adsorbate configuration 87% of the time at about 2,000 times lower cost by combining machine-learned relaxations with a few DFT calculations.
progress.html: AdsorbML found the lowest-energy adsorbate configuration 87% of the time at about 2,000 times lower cost by combining machine-learned relaxations with a few DFT calculations.

progress.what: Released OC25, the largest dataset for solid–liquid interfaces, extending the benchmarks to catalysis in explicit solvent (preprint).
progress.html: Released OC25, the largest dataset for solid–liquid interfaces, extending the benchmarks to catalysis in explicit solvent (preprint).

nodes.html: Predict the relaxed adsorption energies of molecules on catalyst surfaces as accurately as DFT, without running DFT, so that catalysts can be screened at scale. The Open Catalyst 2020 (OC20) benchmarks score the share of predictions within 0.02 eV of DFT, and the best search methods still check results with some DFT. A solution gets most OC20 test adsorption energies within 0.02 eV and finds the lowest-energy configurations without DFT checks.
nodes.summary: Predict the relaxed adsorption energies of molecules on catalyst surfaces as accurately as DFT, without running DFT, so that catalysts can be screened at scale.

nodes.title: Mobile Robotic Chemist
nodes.html: A mobile robot designed by Andrew Cooper’s group at Liverpool ran 688 experiments over 8 days, choosing each next experiment by Bayesian optimisation, and found a photocatalyst mixture six times more active than its starting point (Nature, 2020). It showed that a free-roaming robot can work in an ordinary laboratory and make its own decisions.
nodes.summary: A mobile robot designed by Andrew Cooper’s group at Liverpool ran 688 experiments over 8 days, choosing each next experiment by Bayesian optimisation, and found a photocatalyst mixture six times more active than its starting point (Nature, 2020).

nodes.title: CCSD(T) vs Quantum Monte Carlo Puzzle

progress.what: Traced much of the gap to the perturbative triples of CCSD(T), which overcorrelate highly polarizable systems: the corrected CCSD(cT) gives −19.3 kcal/mol for the coronene dimer, against −21.1 for CCSD(T) and −18.1 for diffusion Monte Carlo (published 2025).
progress.html: Traced much of the gap to the perturbative triples of CCSD(T), which overcorrelate highly polarizable systems: the corrected CCSD(cT) gives −19.3 kcal/mol for the coronene dimer, against −21.1 for CCSD(T) and −18.1 for diffusion Monte Carlo (published 2025).

progress.what: Benchmarks on acene and other dimers, with rank-reduced CCSDT(Q) for the smallest, found that CCSD(T) overbinds slightly, but by less than the quantum Monte Carlo results imply.
progress.html: Benchmarks on acene and other dimers, with rank-reduced CCSDT(Q) for the smallest, found that CCSD(T) overbinds slightly, but by less than the quantum Monte Carlo results imply.

progress.what: Found systematic CCSD(T)–DMC differences already in the 66 medium-sized complexes of the S66 set, with DMC binding more strongly for electrostatic complexes and more weakly for dispersion-bound ones.
progress.html: Found systematic CCSD(T)–DMC differences already in the 66 medium-sized complexes of the S66 set, with DMC binding more strongly for electrostatic complexes and more weakly for dispersion-bound ones.

nodes.html: For large, polarizable non-covalent complexes such as the coronene dimer and C60 held in a ‘buckyball catcher’, the two reference methods of quantum chemistry, CCSD(T) coupled cluster and diffusion Monte Carlo, disagree by up to 8 kcal/mol (Al-Hamdani and colleagues, 2021). A solution pins down these binding energies to within 1 kcal/mol by an independent route and identifies which approximation causes the gap.
nodes.summary: For large, polarizable non-covalent complexes such as the coronene dimer and C60 held in a ‘buckyball catcher’, the two reference methods of quantum chemistry, CCSD(T) coupled cluster and diffusion Monte Carlo, disagree by up to 8 kcal/mol (Al-Hamdani and colleagues, 2021).

nodes.title: Machine-Learned Density Functional
nodes.html: DeepMind’s DM21, a neural-network exchange-correlation functional trained partly on fractional-charge and fractional-spin data, reduced systematic errors of earlier functionals and improved thermochemistry benchmarks (Kirkpatrick, Cohen and colleagues, Science, 2021). Microsoft’s Skala (2025) beat hybrid functionals on a broad chemistry benchmark at semi-local cost.
nodes.summary: DeepMind’s DM21, a neural-network exchange-correlation functional trained partly on fractional-charge and fractional-spin data, reduced systematic errors of earlier functionals and improved thermochemistry benchmarks (Kirkpatrick, Cohen and colleagues, Science, 2021).

nodes.title: Hydrogen-Reduced Steel
nodes.html: Making steel by reducing iron ore with hydrogen from renewable electricity avoids the carbon dioxide released by coke. The HYBRIT consortium of SSAB, LKAB and Vattenfall delivered the first fossil-free steel to Volvo in 2021, and larger plants are planned.
nodes.summary: Making steel by reducing iron ore with hydrogen from renewable electricity avoids the carbon dioxide released by coke.

nodes.title: Skeletal Editing
nodes.html: Skeletal editing reactions delete, insert or swap single atoms in the ring skeleton of a finished molecule instead of rebuilding it from scratch. Mark Levin’s nitrogen deletion of secondary amines (Nature, 2021), and work by Richmond Sarpong, Bill Morandi and others, made this a recognised strategy for modifying drug candidates late in a synthesis.
nodes.summary: Skeletal editing reactions delete, insert or swap single atoms in the ring skeleton of a finished molecule instead of rebuilding it from scratch.

nodes.title: Sodium-Ion Battery
nodes.html: Sodium-ion cells pair hard-carbon anodes, developed by Stevens and Dahn in 2000, with layered-oxide or Prussian-white cathodes, and need no lithium or cobalt. CATL unveiled a commercial cell in 2021, and sodium-ion batteries have since entered Chinese cars and grid storage.
nodes.summary: Sodium-ion cells pair hard-carbon anodes, developed by Stevens and Dahn in 2000, with layered-oxide or Prussian-white cathodes, and need no lithium or cobalt.

nodes.title: Chromium Dimer Solved
nodes.html: The chromium dimer Cr2, a molecule with a formal sextuple bond, had resisted accurate calculation since the 1980s. Henrik Larsson, Huanchen Zhai, Cyrus Umrigar and Garnet Chan computed its potential energy curve close to experiment using DMRG and quantum Monte Carlo (JACS, 2022), in a paper titled ‘Closing a Chapter of Quantum Chemistry’.
nodes.summary: The chromium dimer Cr2, a molecule with a formal sextuple bond, had resisted accurate calculation since the 1980s.

nodes.title: Autonomous Materials Lab (A-Lab)
nodes.html: Berkeley Lab’s A-Lab, built by Gerbrand Ceder’s group with Nathan Szymanski, combined computed targets, literature-trained synthesis planning and robots to make 41 of 58 target compounds in 17 days (Nature, 2023). A 2024 re-analysis argued that most of the claimed products were misidentified or already known, so automated phase identification remains hard.
nodes.summary: Berkeley Lab’s A-Lab, built by Gerbrand Ceder’s group with Nathan Szymanski, combined computed targets, literature-trained synthesis planning and robots to make 41 of 58 target compounds in 17 days (Nature, 2023).

nodes.title: GNoME Crystal Discovery
nodes.html: Google DeepMind’s GNoME, a graph network trained on density functional theory data, predicted 2.2 million new crystal structures, about 380,000 of them stable (Amil Merchant, Ekin Dogus Cubuk and colleagues, Nature, 2023). Critics argued that few of the predictions are both new and useful, and the scale of the claim remains debated.
nodes.summary: Google DeepMind’s GNoME, a graph network trained on density functional theory data, predicted 2.2 million new crystal structures, about 380,000 of them stable (Amil Merchant, Ekin Dogus Cubuk and colleagues, Nature, 2023).

nodes.title: LLM Chemistry Agents
nodes.html: Coscientist (Daniil Boiko, Gabe Gomes and colleagues, Nature, 2023) and ChemCrow (Andres Bran, Philippe Schwaller and colleagues, 2023 to 2024) gave GPT-4 access to tools such as web search, code and laboratory automation. They planned and ran real experiments, including palladium cross-couplings on an automated platform.
nodes.summary: Coscientist (Daniil Boiko, Gabe Gomes and colleagues, Nature, 2023) and ChemCrow (Andres Bran, Philippe Schwaller and colleagues, 2023 to 2024) gave GPT-4 access to tools such as web search, code and laboratory automation.

nodes.title: Predictive Photochemistry Simulation

progress.what: MeV ultrafast electron diffraction of cyclobutanone excited at 200 nm, compared with 15 blind predictions, showed ring opening from the 3s Rydberg state within about 0.3 ps into ketene plus ethylene or C3H6 plus CO.
progress.html: MeV ultrafast electron diffraction of cyclobutanone excited at 200 nm, compared with 15 blind predictions, showed ring opening from the 3s Rydberg state within about 0.3 ps into ketene plus ethylene or C3H6 plus CO.

progress.what: A perspective by the participants concluded that the predictions captured the photochemistry qualitatively, that outcomes depended mainly on the electronic-structure method, and that XMS-CASPT2-based dynamics best matched the measured timescale.
progress.html: A perspective by the participants concluded that the predictions captured the photochemistry qualitatively, that outcomes depended mainly on the electronic-structure method, and that XMS-CASPT2-based dynamics best matched the measured timescale.

nodes.html: Can simulations predict what a molecule does after absorbing light, including products, branching ratios and timescales, before the experiment? In a 2023–24 challenge, 15 blind predictions for cyclobutanone agreed with ultrafast electron diffraction only qualitatively and hinged on the electronic-structure method. A solution is a reproducible protocol whose blind predictions match measured lifetimes and product ratios for new molecules.
nodes.summary: Can simulations predict what a molecule does after absorbing light, including products, branching ratios and timescales, before the experiment?

nodes.title: Universal ML Potentials
nodes.html: Graph neural networks trained on Materials Project data, M3GNet (Chi Chen and Shyue Ping Ong, 2022), CHGNet (2023) and MACE-MP-0 (Ilyes Batatia, Gábor Csányi and colleagues, 2023), can simulate almost any inorganic material across the periodic table without retraining. These universal interatomic potentials made machine-learned simulation an off-the-shelf tool.
nodes.summary: Graph neural networks trained on Materials Project data, M3GNet (Chi Chen and Shyue Ping Ong, 2022), CHGNet (2023) and MACE-MP-0 (Ilyes Batatia, Gábor Csányi and colleagues, 2023), can simulate almost any inorganic material across the periodic table without retraining.

nodes.title: Anti-Bredt Olefins
nodes.html: Bredt’s rule of 1924 says that a double bond cannot sit at the bridgehead of a small bridged ring system because of ring strain. Neil Garg’s group at UCLA generated and trapped such anti-Bredt olefins as reactive intermediates and used them in synthesis (Science, 2024).
nodes.summary: Bredt’s rule of 1924 says that a double bond cannot sit at the bridgehead of a small bridged ring system because of ring strain.

nodes.title: Hexanitrogen (N₆)
nodes.html: Weiyu Qian, Artur Mardyukov and Peter Schreiner made the nitrogen chain N6, hexanitrogen, by reacting chlorine or bromine with silver azide, and isolated it as a film at 77 K (Nature, 2025). It is the first neutral nitrogen allotrope other than N2 to be isolated, and it decomposes to N2 with a large release of energy.
nodes.summary: Weiyu Qian, Artur Mardyukov and Peter Schreiner made the nitrogen chain N6, hexanitrogen, by reacting chlorine or bromine with silver azide, and isolated it as a film at 77 K (Nature, 2025).

nodes.title: Generative Materials Design
nodes.html: Microsoft Research’s MatterGen, a diffusion model for crystal structures (Claudio Zeni, Tian Xie and colleagues, Nature, 2025), generates stable materials for specified chemistry, symmetry and property targets. One generated compound, TaCr2O6, was synthesised, and its measured bulk modulus came within about 20 percent of the target.
nodes.summary: Microsoft Research’s MatterGen, a diffusion model for crystal structures (Claudio Zeni, Tian Xie and colleagues, Nature, 2025), generates stable materials for specified chemistry, symmetry and property targets.

nodes.title: Open Molecules 2025
nodes.html: Meta FAIR Chemistry released Open Molecules 2025 (OMol25), more than 100 million density functional theory calculations at a hybrid-functional level covering biomolecules, electrolytes and metal complexes, together with the UMA models trained on it and related datasets. It is one of the largest open datasets of its kind and a shared base for machine-learned molecular simulation.
nodes.summary: Meta FAIR Chemistry released Open Molecules 2025 (OMol25), more than 100 million density functional theory calculations at a hybrid-functional level covering biomolecules, electrolytes and metal complexes, together with the UMA models trained on it and related datasets.

nodes.title: Ambient-Condition Ammonia Synthesis

progress.what: Set out a rigorous test protocol with quantitative 15N2 isotope measurements, needed because many reported electrochemical ammonia yields could come from contamination.
progress.html: Set out a rigorous test protocol with quantitative 15N2 isotope measurements, needed because many reported electrochemical ammonia yields could come from contamination.

progress.what: Lithium-mediated nitrogen reduction reached almost 100% current-to-ammonia efficiency.
progress.html: Lithium-mediated nitrogen reduction reached almost 100% current-to-ammonia efficiency.

progress.what: A continuous-flow electrolyzer coupling nitrogen reduction with hydrogen oxidation reached up to 61% Faradaic and 13% energy efficiency at 1 bar.
progress.html: A continuous-flow electrolyzer coupling nitrogen reduction with hydrogen oxidation reached up to 61% Faradaic and 13% energy efficiency at 1 bar.

progress.what: A layered solid–electrolyte interphase that speeds lithium-ion transport gave 98% Faradaic and 21% energy efficiency at 100 mA/cm², and 80% Faradaic efficiency was held for 40 hours.
progress.html: A layered solid–electrolyte interphase that speeds lithium-ion transport gave 98% Faradaic and 21% energy efficiency at 100 mA/cm², and 80% Faradaic efficiency was held for 40 hours.

nodes.html: Make ammonia from nitrogen, water and renewable electricity near room temperature, with efficiency and durability that rival the Haber–Bosch process, which emits about 1–2% of global CO2. Lithium-mediated electrolysis reached 98% Faradaic but only 21% energy efficiency at 100 mA/cm² in 2026, and molecular catalysts need costly reductants. A solution runs for thousands of hours at industrial current density with competitive efficiency and cost.
nodes.summary: Make ammonia from nitrogen, water and renewable electricity near room temperature, with efficiency and durability that rival the Haber–Bosch process, which emits about 1–2% of global CO2.

nodes.title: Direct Methane to Methanol

progress.what: Platinum bipyrimidine catalysts turned methane into a methanol ester in fuming sulfuric acid at over 70% one-pass yield.
progress.html: Platinum bipyrimidine catalysts turned methane into a methanol ester in fuming sulfuric acid at over 70% one-pass yield.

progress.what: A copper zeolite oxidized methane to methanol in a two-step cycle with water as the oxidant, which also released hydrogen.
progress.html: A copper zeolite oxidized methane to methanol in a two-step cycle with water as the oxidant, which also released hydrogen.

progress.what: Gold–palladium colloids made methanol from methane at 50 °C with 92% selectivity, using O2 as the main oxidant once hydrogen peroxide had started the reaction.
progress.html: Gold–palladium colloids made methanol from methane at 50 °C with 92% selectivity, using O2 as the main oxidant once hydrogen peroxide had started the reaction.

progress.what: A hydrophobic zeolite shell kept hydrogen peroxide generated in place near gold–palladium sites, oxidizing methane selectively to methanol.
progress.html: A hydrophobic zeolite shell kept hydrogen peroxide generated in place near gold–palladium sites, oxidizing methane selectively to methanol.

nodes.html: Oxidize methane straight to methanol with oxygen or air under mild conditions, at high conversion and selectivity, as the enzyme methane monooxygenase does; industry instead goes through energy-intensive syngas. Periana’s 1998 platinum catalyst needed fuming sulfuric acid, and later systems are selective only at low conversion or with stepwise schemes. A solution converts methane directly with O2 at practical conversion and over 90% selectivity.
nodes.summary: Oxidize methane straight to methanol with oxygen or air under mild conditions, at high conversion and selectivity, as the enzyme methane monooxygenase does; industry instead goes through energy-intensive syngas.

nodes.title: Room-Temperature Superconductor

progress.what: 151 K at ambient pressure in pressure-quenched HgBa₂Ca₂Cu₃O₈₊δ, the first new ambient-pressure record since 1993.
progress.html: 151 K at ambient pressure in pressure-quenched HgBa₂Ca₂Cu₃O₈₊δ, the first new ambient-pressure record since 1993.

nodes.html: A superconductor at ordinary temperature and pressure would transform power grids, magnets and computing. Claims so far, including LK-99 in 2023, have not survived replication.
nodes.summary: A superconductor at ordinary temperature and pressure would transform power grids, magnets and computing.

nodes.title: Dog Domestication
nodes.html: Wolves and hunter-gatherers began living together, and the wolves’ descendants became dogs, the first domesticated animal. The oldest undisputed dog burial, beside a human grave at Bonn-Oberkassel in Germany, is about 14,200 years old, and DNA suggests the split from wolves is older still. Dogs helped with hunting and guarding.
nodes.summary: Wolves and hunter-gatherers began living together, and the wolves’ descendants became dogs, the first domesticated animal.

nodes.title: Agriculture
nodes.html: Wheat, barley and lentils were domesticated in the Fertile Crescent around 9500 BCE, with independent starts in China, New Guinea, Mesoamerica and the Andes. Surplus food made cities, writing and specialists possible.
nodes.summary: Wheat, barley and lentils were domesticated in the Fertile Crescent around 9500 BCE, with independent starts in China, New Guinea, Mesoamerica and the Andes.

nodes.title: Livestock Domestication
nodes.html: Sheep, goats, pigs and cattle were domesticated in south-west Asia between about 8500 and 8000 BCE, in the same farming villages that grew wheat and barley. Herds gave meat, milk, wool, hides and manure, and later pulled ploughs and carts, and herding societies spread across Eurasia and Africa.
nodes.summary: Sheep, goats, pigs and cattle were domesticated in south-west Asia between about 8500 and 8000 BCE, in the same farming villages that grew wheat and barley.

nodes.title: Fermentation
nodes.html: People brewed and baked with microbes long before anyone knew they existed. Chemical residues in pottery from Jiahu in China show a fermented drink of rice, honey and fruit by about 7000 BCE, and wine, beer and leavened bread followed across the Near East. Fermentation also preserved milk and vegetables.
nodes.summary: People brewed and baked with microbes long before anyone knew they existed.

nodes.title: Maize Domestication
nodes.html: Farmers in the Balsas River valley of southern Mexico turned the wild grass teosinte into maize about 9,000 years ago, through changes in a handful of genes that control branching and the hard casing around each kernel. Maize spread across the Americas and is now the world’s most-produced grain.
nodes.summary: Farmers in the Balsas River valley of southern Mexico turned the wild grass teosinte into maize about 9,000 years ago, through changes in a handful of genes that control branching and the hard casing around each kernel.

nodes.title: Rice Domestication
nodes.html: Rice was domesticated in the lower Yangtze valley of China, with cultivation under way from about 7000 BCE and fully domesticated forms appearing over the following millennia. Asian rice (Oryza sativa) spread across Asia and became the staple food of more than half of humanity.
nodes.summary: Rice was domesticated in the lower Yangtze valley of China, with cultivation under way from about 7000 BCE and fully domesticated forms appearing over the following millennia.

nodes.title: Trepanation
nodes.html: Neolithic surgeons cut or scraped openings in the skulls of living people, and healed bone around the edges shows that many patients survived. A skull from Ensisheim in Alsace, dated to about 5100 BCE, is a well-documented early case. Motives probably included head injuries, headaches and ritual.
nodes.summary: Neolithic surgeons cut or scraped openings in the skulls of living people, and healed bone around the edges shows that many patients survived.

nodes.title: The Plough
nodes.html: Ox-drawn ards, wooden frames with a pointed share, were cutting furrows in Europe and Mesopotamia by about 3500 to 3000 BCE. They broke ground far faster than a hoe, so one family could farm much more land and a food surplus could support cities and specialists.
nodes.summary: Ox-drawn ards, wooden frames with a pointed share, were cutting furrows in Europe and Mesopotamia by about 3500 to 3000 BCE.

nodes.title: Horse Domestication
nodes.html: Ancient DNA shows that every modern domestic horse descends from a population on the lower Volga-Don steppe, which spread across Eurasia from about 2200 BCE (Librado and colleagues, 2021). Horses brought fast transport, mounted warfare and chariots, and changed trade, migration and war.
nodes.summary: Ancient DNA shows that every modern domestic horse descends from a population on the lower Volga-Don steppe, which spread across Eurasia from about 2200 BCE (Librado and colleagues, 2021).

nodes.title: Edwin Smith Papyrus
nodes.html: This Egyptian surgical text, copied about 1600 BCE from a much older original, describes 48 cases of injury working downward from the head. Each case gives an examination, a diagnosis, a verdict of treatable, uncertain or untreatable, and a treatment, and it relies on observation with very little magic.
nodes.summary: This Egyptian surgical text, copied about 1600 BCE from a much older original, describes 48 cases of injury working downward from the head.

nodes.title: Hippocratic Medicine
nodes.html: The Hippocratic Corpus, about sixty texts written around 400 BCE by Hippocrates and his followers, attributed disease to natural causes such as diet, climate and the balance of the humours. It set out methods of careful bedside observation and prognosis and an ethic for physicians that lives on in the Hippocratic Oath.
nodes.summary: The Hippocratic Corpus, about sixty texts written around 400 BCE by Hippocrates and his followers, attributed disease to natural causes such as diet, climate and the balance of the humours.

nodes.title: Sushruta Samhita
nodes.html: This Sanskrit compendium of surgery, attributed to Sushruta and in its oldest layers from the last centuries BCE, describes about 120 instruments and some 300 operations, including cataract couching and reconstruction of the nose with a skin flap. It was the central surgical text of Indian medicine for centuries.
nodes.summary: This Sanskrit compendium of surgery, attributed to Sushruta and in its oldest layers from the last centuries BCE, describes about 120 instruments and some 300 operations, including cataract couching and reconstruction of the nose with a skin flap.

nodes.title: De Materia Medica
nodes.html: Dioscorides, a Greek physician serving with Roman armies, described about 600 plants and some 1,000 drugs and their preparation in this five-volume work, written around 50 to 70 CE. It stayed the standard pharmacopoeia in Europe and the Islamic world for some 1,500 years and survives in illustrated Byzantine manuscripts.
nodes.summary: Dioscorides, a Greek physician serving with Roman armies, described about 600 plants and some 1,000 drugs and their preparation in this five-volume work, written around 50 to 70 CE.

nodes.title: Galenic Physiology
nodes.html: Galen of Pergamon, physician to gladiators and emperors, combined animal dissection and experiments on nerves with the humoral theory to build a complete system of anatomy and physiology (about 170 CE). It dominated European and Islamic medicine for some 1,400 years, until Vesalius and Harvey overturned much of it.
nodes.summary: Galen of Pergamon, physician to gladiators and emperors, combined animal dissection and experiments on nerves with the humoral theory to build a complete system of anatomy and physiology (about 170 CE).

nodes.title: The Canon of Medicine
nodes.html: Ibn Sina (Avicenna) completed this five-book encyclopedia in 1025. It organised Greek and Islamic medical knowledge, discussed the contagious spread of disease, set out rules for testing drugs on patients, and was taught in European universities from the 12th to the 17th century.
nodes.summary: Ibn Sina (Avicenna) completed this five-book encyclopedia in 1025.

nodes.title: Quarantine
nodes.html: In 1377 the Republic of Ragusa (now Dubrovnik) ordered travellers from plague-stricken places to wait thirty days outside the city before entering. The period was later lengthened to forty days, which gave quarantine its name. It was one of the first public-health laws, and isolation of travellers and the sick has been a basic response to epidemics ever since.
nodes.summary: In 1377 the Republic of Ragusa (now Dubrovnik) ordered travellers from plague-stricken places to wait thirty days outside the city before entering.

nodes.title: Human Anatomy
nodes.html: Andreas Vesalius published De humani corporis fabrica in 1543, based on his own dissections of human bodies at Padua and illustrated with detailed woodcuts. It corrected many of Galen’s errors, which had come from animal anatomy, and made direct observation the authority in anatomy.
nodes.summary: Andreas Vesalius published De humani corporis fabrica in 1543, based on his own dissections of human bodies at Padua and illustrated with detailed woodcuts.

nodes.title: Circulation of the Blood
nodes.html: William Harvey calculated that the heart ejects far more blood each hour than the body could possibly make, and showed with ligature experiments that blood flows from the arteries through the tissues to the veins and back to the heart. His De Motu Cordis (1628) replaced Galen’s account and is an early example of quantitative reasoning in physiology.
nodes.summary: William Harvey calculated that the heart ejects far more blood each hour than the body could possibly make, and showed with ligature experiments that blood flows from the arteries through the tissues to the veins and back to the heart.

nodes.title: Vital Statistics
nodes.html: John Graunt, a London haberdasher, analysed the weekly Bills of Mortality in his Natural and Political Observations (1662). He found regular patterns in births, deaths and causes of death, and built an early life table. His work founded demography and the statistical study of public health.
nodes.summary: John Graunt, a London haberdasher, analysed the weekly Bills of Mortality in his Natural and Political Observations (1662).

nodes.title: Variolation
nodes.html: Inoculating a healthy person with matter from a mild smallpox case was practised in Asia, Africa and the Ottoman Empire. Lady Mary Wortley Montagu brought it to Britain, and in 1721 Zabdiel Boylston and Cotton Mather, who had learned of it from the enslaved man Onesimus, applied it in Boston. About 2% of those inoculated died, against up to 30% in natural smallpox.
nodes.summary: Inoculating a healthy person with matter from a mild smallpox case was practised in Asia, Africa and the Ottoman Empire.

nodes.title: Crop Rotation
nodes.html: Medieval farmers left a third or half of their land fallow each year. The Norfolk four-course system, popularised by Charles Townshend from about 1730, replaced fallow with a cycle of wheat, turnips, barley and clover that fed livestock and restored soil nitrogen. Yields and herds grew, a foundation of the British agricultural revolution.
nodes.summary: Medieval farmers left a third or half of their land fallow each year.

nodes.title: Linnaean Taxonomy
nodes.html: Carl Linnaeus’s Systema Naturae (1735) arranged plants, animals and minerals in nested ranks, and his Species Plantarum (1753) gave each species a two-part Latin name. Binomial names gave naturalists everywhere an unambiguous label for every species, and the system is still in use.
nodes.summary: Carl Linnaeus’s Systema Naturae (1735) arranged plants, animals and minerals in nested ranks, and his Species Plantarum (1753) gave each species a two-part Latin name.

nodes.title: Photosynthesis
nodes.html: Jan Ingenhousz showed in 1779 that plants give off oxygen only in sunlight and only from their green parts, building on Joseph Priestley’s finding that plants restore air spoiled by burning. It revealed that life on land runs on sunlight, and later work identified carbon dioxide as the raw material.
nodes.summary: Jan Ingenhousz showed in 1779 that plants give off oxygen only in sunlight and only from their green parts, building on Joseph Priestley’s finding that plants restore air spoiled by burning.

nodes.title: Respiration as Combustion
nodes.html: Antoine Lavoisier and Pierre-Simon Laplace placed a guinea pig in an ice calorimeter in 1783 and measured the heat it gave out and the carbon dioxide it breathed out. The ratio resembled that of burning carbon, so they concluded that respiration is a slow combustion that powers the body.
nodes.summary: Antoine Lavoisier and Pierre-Simon Laplace placed a guinea pig in an ice calorimeter in 1783 and measured the heat it gave out and the carbon dioxide it breathed out.

nodes.title: Animal Electricity
nodes.html: Luigi Galvani found that frog legs twitched when touched with two metals or sparked by an electrical machine, and in 1791 published his view that nerve and muscle carry an intrinsic electricity. His dispute with Volta led to the battery, and electrical signalling was later shown to underlie nerve conduction.
nodes.summary: Luigi Galvani found that frog legs twitched when touched with two metals or sparked by an electrical machine, and in 1791 published his view that nerve and muscle carry an intrinsic electricity.

nodes.title: Extinction
nodes.html: Georges Cuvier compared living elephants with fossil mammoth and mastodon bones in 1796 and showed they were distinct species with no living counterparts. He argued that whole species can vanish, and later that catastrophes had repeatedly changed the fauna. The idea made a deep history of life thinkable.
nodes.summary: Georges Cuvier compared living elephants with fossil mammoth and mastodon bones in 1796 and showed they were distinct species with no living counterparts.

nodes.title: Vaccination
nodes.html: Jenner protected a boy against smallpox by inoculating him with cowpox (1796). Smallpox was declared eradicated in 1980.
nodes.summary: Jenner protected a boy against smallpox by inoculating him with cowpox (1796).

nodes.title: Comparative Embryology
nodes.html: Karl Ernst von Baer discovered the mammalian egg in 1827 and in 1828 set out his laws of development: embryos of different animals share general features early and diverge into specialised forms. His laws undercut the idea that embryos pass through the adult forms of lower animals, and became the basis of comparative embryology.
nodes.summary: Karl Ernst von Baer discovered the mammalian egg in 1827 and in 1828 set out his laws of development: embryos of different animals share general features early and diverge into specialised forms.

nodes.title: Logistic Growth
nodes.html: Pierre-François Verhulst proposed in 1838 that a population’s growth slows as it approaches the limit its environment can support, which gives an S-shaped curve. His logistic equation introduced the idea of carrying capacity and is still the standard model of limited growth in ecology and epidemiology.
nodes.summary: Pierre-François Verhulst proposed in 1838 that a population’s growth slows as it approaches the limit its environment can support, which gives an S-shaped curve.

nodes.title: Cell Theory
nodes.html: All living things are made of cells (Schleiden and Schwann, 1838–39), and every cell comes from another cell (Virchow, 1855).
nodes.summary: All living things are made of cells (Schleiden and Schwann, 1838–39), and every cell comes from another cell (Virchow, 1855).

nodes.title: Surgical Anaesthesia
nodes.html: On 16 October 1846 at Massachusetts General Hospital, William Morton gave ether to a patient while John Collins Warren removed a neck tumour without pain. Crawford Long had used ether in 1842 and John Snow later worked out safe dosing of ether and chloroform. Painless surgery allowed longer and more careful operations.
nodes.summary: On 16 October 1846 at Massachusetts General Hospital, William Morton gave ether to a patient while John Collins Warren removed a neck tumour without pain.

nodes.title: Mechanism of General Anaesthesia

progress.what: Anaesthetic potency tracks solubility in olive oil (Meyer 1899, Overton 1901), which suggested that all anaesthetics act nonspecifically on a lipid phase of nerve cells.
progress.html: Anaesthetic potency tracks solubility in olive oil (Meyer 1899, Overton 1901), which suggested that all anaesthetics act nonspecifically on a lipid phase of nerve cells.

progress.what: A pure soluble protein, firefly luciferase, is inhibited at the concentrations that anaesthetize animals across a 100,000-fold range of potencies, which moved the search from lipids to proteins.
progress.html: A pure soluble protein, firefly luciferase, is inhibited at the concentrations that anaesthetize animals across a 100,000-fold range of potencies, which moved the search from lipids to proteins.

progress.what: In mice with a single point mutation (N265M) in the β3 subunit of the GABA-A receptor, etomidate and propofol no longer suppress movement in response to pain, while volatile anaesthetics still largely work, so one residue is a major determinant for the intravenous drugs.
progress.html: In mice with a single point mutation (N265M) in the β3 subunit of the GABA-A receptor, etomidate and propofol no longer suppress movement in response to pain, while volatile anaesthetics still largely work, so one residue is a major determinant for the intravenous drugs.

progress.what: Propofol, ketamine and dexmedetomidine, which act on different receptors, all reduced the dynamic stability of cortical population activity in monkeys, extending a 2024 result for propofol.
progress.html: Propofol, ketamine and dexmedetomidine, which act on different receptors, all reduced the dynamic stability of cortical population activity in monkeys, extending a 2024 result for propofol.

nodes.html: How do chemically unrelated drugs, from ether and xenon to propofol and ketamine, all switch off consciousness? The first theory came in 1847, a year after ether was demonstrated in public, and many molecular targets are now known. Solving it means a chain from targets through brain circuits that predicts each agent’s potency and effects; in 2026 three drug classes were found to destabilize cortical dynamics in the same way in monkeys.
nodes.summary: How do chemically unrelated drugs, from ether and xenon to propofol and ketamine, all switch off consciousness?

nodes.title: Hand Hygiene
nodes.html: At the Vienna General Hospital, Ignaz Semmelweis noticed that women died of childbed fever far more often in the clinic staffed by doctors fresh from autopsies. After he ordered chlorinated-lime handwashing in May 1847, deaths there fell from 18% in April to about 2% by June. Colleagues rejected his explanation, and it was accepted only after germ theory.
nodes.summary: At the Vienna General Hospital, Ignaz Semmelweis noticed that women died of childbed fever far more often in the clinic staffed by doctors fresh from autopsies.

nodes.title: Cholera and Epidemiology
nodes.html: During the 1854 cholera outbreak in Soho, London, John Snow plotted deaths on a map, traced them to the Broad Street water pump and persuaded the parish to remove its handle. His argument that cholera spreads through contaminated water, made decades before germs were accepted, is a founding case of modern epidemiology.
nodes.summary: During the 1854 cholera outbreak in Soho, London, John Snow plotted deaths on a map, traced them to the Broad Street water pump and persuaded the parish to remove its handle.

nodes.title: Evolution by Natural Selection

quote.text: There is grandeur in this view of life.

nodes.html: On the Origin of Species (1859): heritable variation plus selection explains both the diversity and the unity of life.
nodes.summary: On the Origin of Species (1859): heritable variation plus selection explains both the diversity and the unity of life.

nodes.title: Cortical Localization
nodes.html: In 1861 Paul Broca examined the brain of a patient who could say only the syllable ‘tan’ and found a lesion in the left frontal lobe. Carl Wernicke described a second language area in 1874. Together they showed that particular mental functions depend on particular regions of the cortex.
nodes.summary: In 1861 Paul Broca examined the brain of a patient who could say only the syllable ‘tan’ and found a lesion in the left frontal lobe.

nodes.title: End of Spontaneous Generation
nodes.html: Louis Pasteur boiled nutrient broth in swan-necked flasks (1859-61) and showed that it stayed clear until dust carrying microbes reached it. The experiments ended the long belief that living things arise from non-living matter, and gave bacteriology and surgery the principle of keeping microbes out.
nodes.summary: Louis Pasteur boiled nutrient broth in swan-necked flasks (1859-61) and showed that it stayed clear until dust carrying microbes reached it.

nodes.title: Batesian Mimicry
nodes.html: Henry Walter Bates, after eleven years collecting in the Amazon, explained in 1862 why harmless butterflies resemble distasteful ones: predators learn to avoid the model, so lookalikes gain protection. Published soon after the Origin of Species, it was an early and persuasive example of natural selection at work.
nodes.summary: Henry Walter Bates, after eleven years collecting in the Amazon, explained in 1862 why harmless butterflies resemble distasteful ones: predators learn to avoid the model, so lookalikes gain protection.

nodes.title: Pasteurization
nodes.html: Louis Pasteur showed in 1864 that heating wine to about 55 degrees Celsius kills the microbes that spoil it without ruining the wine. The method was extended to beer and then to milk, where from the 1890s it sharply reduced tuberculosis and other milk-borne disease.
nodes.summary: Louis Pasteur showed in 1864 that heating wine to about 55 degrees Celsius kills the microbes that spoil it without ruining the wine.

nodes.title: Homeostasis
nodes.html: Claude Bernard argued, most fully in his 1865 Introduction to the Study of Experimental Medicine, that the body keeps its internal environment (milieu intérieur) constant and that this constancy makes independent life possible. Walter Cannon named the principle homeostasis in 1926 and showed how nerves and hormones maintain it.
nodes.summary: Claude Bernard argued, most fully in his 1865 Introduction to the Study of Experimental Medicine, that the body keeps its internal environment (milieu intérieur) constant and that this constancy makes independent life possible.

nodes.title: Mendelian Inheritance
nodes.html: Mendel’s pea crosses (1866) revealed discrete units of inheritance. The work was ignored until three botanists rediscovered it in 1900.
nodes.summary: Mendel’s pea crosses (1866) revealed discrete units of inheritance.

nodes.title: Antiseptic Surgery
nodes.html: Inspired by Pasteur’s work on microbes, Joseph Lister used carbolic acid on wounds, dressings and instruments in Glasgow from 1865 and published his method in 1867. Deaths after amputation in his wards fell from 46% to 15%. Antisepsis led on to aseptic surgery, in which everything that touches the wound is sterile.
nodes.summary: Inspired by Pasteur’s work on microbes, Joseph Lister used carbolic acid on wounds, dressings and instruments in Glasgow from 1865 and published his method in 1867.

nodes.title: Sexual Selection
nodes.html: In The Descent of Man (1871) Darwin proposed that traits such as peacock tails and stag antlers evolve because they help individuals win mates or defeat rivals, even when they lower survival. The theory explains many differences between the sexes and underlies modern work on mate choice.
nodes.summary: In The Descent of Man (1871) Darwin proposed that traits such as peacock tails and stag antlers evolve because they help individuals win mates or defeat rivals, even when they lower survival.

nodes.title: Biogeography
nodes.html: Alfred Russel Wallace’s The Geographical Distribution of Animals (1876) divided the world into six zoogeographic regions and explained their faunas by evolution and past land connections. It built on Humboldt’s maps of plant zones and on Wallace’s own line through Indonesia between Asian and Australian animals.
nodes.summary: Alfred Russel Wallace’s The Geographical Distribution of Animals (1876) divided the world into six zoogeographic regions and explained their faunas by evolution and past land connections.

nodes.title: Germ Theory
nodes.html: Specific microbes cause specific diseases: Pasteur’s experiments in the 1860s, and Koch’s identification of the anthrax bacillus (1876) and of tuberculosis (1882).
nodes.summary: Specific microbes cause specific diseases: Pasteur’s experiments in the 1860s, and Koch’s identification of the anthrax bacillus (1876) and of tuberculosis (1882).

nodes.title: Darwin’s Abominable Mystery

quote.text: The rapid development, as far as we can judge, of all the higher plants within recent geological times is an abominable mystery.
quote.by: Charles Darwin, letter to J. D. Hooker, 22 July 1879

progress.what: A plastid tree from 2,881 genomes dated crown angiosperms to the Upper Triassic, tens of millions of years before any accepted angiosperm fossil. The authors named the discrepancy the Jurassic angiosperm gap.
progress.html: A plastid tree from 2,881 genomes dated crown angiosperms to the Upper Triassic, tens of millions of years before any accepted angiosperm fossil. The authors named the discrepancy the Jurassic angiosperm gap.

progress.what: A nuclear tree of almost 8,000 angiosperm genera from 353 genes, dated with 200 fossils, confirmed an early explosive radiation that produced more than 80% of living angiosperm orders, with a second burst in the Cenozoic.
progress.html: A nuclear tree of almost 8,000 angiosperm genera from 353 genes, dated with 200 fossils, confirmed an early explosive radiation that produced more than 80% of living angiosperm orders, with a second burst in the Cenozoic.

progress.what: Argued that the clash between clocks and fossils is an artefact of how disputed fossils are read. Dropping them puts the crown group in the Late Jurassic to Early Cretaceous and moves the unexplained gap onto the stem lineage.
progress.html: Argued that the clash between clocks and fossils is an artefact of how disputed fossils are read. Dropping them puts the crown group in the Late Jurassic to Early Cretaceous and moves the unexplained gap onto the stem lineage.

progress.what: Calibrating 110 nodes of a 644-species tree from more than 25,000 fossil occurrences with a Bayesian Brownian bridge model gave a short, latest-Jurassic history for angiosperms and ruled out a post-Jurassic origin.
progress.html: Calibrating 110 nodes of a 644-species tree from more than 25,000 fossil occurrences with a Bayesian Brownian bridge model gave a short, latest-Jurassic history for angiosperms and ruled out a post-Jurassic origin.

nodes.html: Flowering plants appear suddenly in the Cretaceous and diversify explosively, which Darwin called an abominable mystery in a letter of 22 July 1879. Molecular clocks place their origin well before any accepted fossil. Settling it takes a dated tree that reconciles clocks with the fossil record and identifies what drove the burst.
nodes.summary: Flowering plants appear suddenly in the Cretaceous and diversify explosively, which Darwin called an abominable mystery in a letter of 22 July 1879.

nodes.title: Mitosis
nodes.html: Walther Flemming stained dividing salamander cells and watched threadlike chromatin split lengthwise and pass into two daughter nuclei, which he described in 1882 and named mitosis. It showed how a cell copies its contents exactly when it divides.
nodes.summary: Walther Flemming stained dividing salamander cells and watched threadlike chromatin split lengthwise and pass into two daughter nuclei, which he described in 1882 and named mitosis.

nodes.title: Cellular Immunity
nodes.html: Élie Metchnikoff saw mobile cells in starfish larvae gather around a thorn pushed into the body, and in 1884 watched similar cells engulf yeast spores in water fleas. He proposed that white blood cells ingest invaders as a defence, founding cellular immunity, and shared the 1908 Nobel Prize with Paul Ehrlich.
nodes.summary: Élie Metchnikoff saw mobile cells in starfish larvae gather around a thorn pushed into the body, and in 1884 watched similar cells engulf yeast spores in water fleas.

nodes.title: Pure Culture and Staining
nodes.html: In the early 1880s Robert Koch’s laboratory introduced solid culture media, with agar suggested by Fanny Hesse, and staining methods that let single bacterial colonies be grown and identified. Hans Christian Gram’s stain followed in 1884. With these tools Koch identified the causes of tuberculosis (1882) and cholera (1883).
nodes.summary: In the early 1880s Robert Koch’s laboratory introduced solid culture media, with agar suggested by Fanny Hesse, and staining methods that let single bacterial colonies be grown and identified.

nodes.title: Rabies Vaccine
nodes.html: Louis Pasteur and Émile Roux weakened rabies by drying the spinal cords of infected rabbits, and in July 1885 used the product to treat Joseph Meister, a nine-year-old bitten by a rabid dog, who survived. It was the first vaccine made in the laboratory against a viral disease of humans, and it showed that vaccines could be produced by design.
nodes.summary: Louis Pasteur and Émile Roux weakened rabies by drying the spinal cords of infected rabbits, and in July 1885 used the product to treat Joseph Meister, a nine-year-old bitten by a rabid dog, who survived.

nodes.title: Neuron Doctrine
